 You will negotiate directly with large enterprise customers across a large variety of industries including financial services, healthcare, government, and other regulated industries, partner daily with Enterprise Sales, Partnerships, Deal Desk, Security, Privacy, Product, and Finance, and advise on the legal questions that come with agentic, retrieval, and API products deployed inside enterprise environments. This is a high-impact, hands-on role for someone who is genuinely a self starter.
 
 This role is for you if you get energy from ambiguous, first‑of‑their‑kind problems and enjoy designing repeatable approaches that scale. You default to enabling the business, frame risk in practical terms, and focus on durable structures rather than one‑off fixes.
 
 Responsibilities 
 Independently lead end-to-end drafting, review, and negotiation of Enterprise customer agreements across our suite of offerings: Enterprise Pro, Enterprise Max, Computer, and API product lines, including MSAs, order forms, SaaS and API terms, DPAs, BAAs, security exhibits, customer-paper redlines, product-specific addenda, and public-sector vehicles such as GSA MAS orders and federal RFP responses.

 Serve as a trusted legal partner to Enterprise Sales, Partnerships, Deal Desk, and Customer Success, providing fast, practical, business-aligned counsel that accelerates deal velocity, protects the terms that matter, and scales as the Sales organization grows.

 Extend and maintain the existing Enterprise negotiation playbook, DPA and Privacy Notice architecture, product-specific term libraries, and fallback positions as our product surface, customer mix, and regulatory environment evolve, so that positions compound into reusable precedent rather than being re-litigated deal by deal.

 Advise on AI-specific contract terms for enterprise deployments, including bespoke data postures; negotiate output ownership and liability, agentic-feature risk allocation and translate product operations into enterprise contract commitments.

 Partner cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Security, Privacy, Finance, and Compliance to surface and address legal risk early, particularly on customer-data flows, enterprise integrations, model routing, and customer-specific compliance requirements.

 Monitor the evolving regulatory landscape for enterprise AI, data protection, and public-sector procurement (GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, HIPAA, DORA, EU AI Act, sector-specific frameworks) and translate emerging requirements into practical contractual positions and updated playbook guidance.

 Represent Perplexity Legal externally on customer negotiation calls with counterparty counsel at sophisticated enterprises.

 What we are looking for
 Exceptional communicator who owns deadlines, proactively manages internal and external expectations, and escalates early and clearly to protect deal timelines and momentum.

 A proactive problem‑solver who defaults to “yes, and” when engaging with internal stakeholders: you look for ways to make deals work, frame risk clearly, and design long‑term, scalable solutions.

 A disciplined drafter who favors surgical, minimal‑footprint edits over wholesale rewrites, grounds positions in documented rationale, and preserves material legal meaning and risk allocation under time pressure.

 Someone who can articulate complex legal risk and concepts in the form of simple, actionable terms for non‑legal stakeholders, leads with practical “how to make this work” advice, and designs creative, long‑term solutions to novel, cutting‑edge challenges.

 Someone genuinely excited by novel, cutting‑edge challenges in AI products and the commercial and regulatory questions they surface, and who enjoys turning ambiguity into clear, reusable approaches.

 Qualifications
 JD and in good standing with an active U.S. state bar membership.

 At least 7+ years of combined law firm and in-house experience, with a substantial in-house component, and a demonstrated track record of independently owning complex enterprise SaaS or API deals from the vendor side, including work with regulated-industry customers (financial services, healthcare, or government).

 Experience advising on commercial terms and pricing structures for high‑growth SaaS/API businesses, including usage‑based and tiered pricing, pilots, and expansion frameworks.

 Familiarity with data protection and security frameworks (GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, DORA, EU AI Act) and hands-on experience negotiating DPAs.

 Strong business acumen and the ability to partner effectively with Sales, Deal Desk, Product, Security, and executive stakeholders on live deals under time pressure.

 Proven ability to triage and progress multiple concurrent deals under tight timelines while maintaining rigorous diligence, clear risk assessment, and high‑quality documentation.

 Demonstrated ability to build and extend durable legal infrastructure — playbooks, templates, precedent repositories, or self-serve tools.

 Ability to communicate clearly with business and technical audiences and to translate legal concepts into usable guidance for non-lawyers, including Sales and Deal Desk.

 Hands-on, can-do approach to tackle projects large and small, low-ego approach to working closely with the Director and across the organization, and judgment about when to escalate and when to close.

 Positive collaborative attitude, comfort with ambiguity and a fast pace, high level of integrity, and intellectual curiosity about AI technology.

 
 Nice to have
 Prior experience with public-sector contracting or with on-prem deployment structures.

 Experience with AI-native contracting questions related to agentic products

 Experience with contracting with regulated entities (financial institutions or health care), especially in the EU/UK.

job_title: GTM Senior Business Systems Analyst, Marketing & Pre-Sales
description:
About Ramp 
 Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
 The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
 We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.
 The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
 If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.
 
 About the Role 
 Ramp is in a critical phase of growth, and marketing is one of the biggest drivers of it. We're building out our business systems team to make sure the systems behind every campaign, list, and lead can keep up. You'll work directly with Growth Marketing, Demand Generation, Lifecycle, Events, Sales Development, and Sales to own the systems that turn marketing programs into pipeline. You'll own HubSpot and how it connects to Salesforce and the rest of our GTM stack.
 
 What You'll Do 
 Own top-of-funnel marketing systems: the roadmap, the architecture decisions inside them, and their operational health

description:
The Product Solutions Architecture (PSA) team acts as a technical multiplier across Datadog. PSAs are domain experts who partner with Field teams on complex customer use cases across pre- and post-sales engagements and scale their impact by producing reusable collateral, including reference architectures, technical guides, and enablement assets. By feeding real-world customer insights back to Datadog Product teams, PSAs help influence product roadmaps while accelerating adoption, usage, and long-term customer success.

Datadog's Cloud Cost Management (CCM) suite helps Platform, Application Teams, Operations, FinOps, and Finance teams understand, allocate, and reduce cloud spend by putting cost data next to the observability data that explains it. As a Product Solutions Architect, you will partner closely with Datadog customers and the Cloud Cost Management product team to design product use cases, implement best practices, and drive adoption of CCM across customer environments. This includes infrastructure cost allocation, cloud costs, token usage, container costs, budgets, and optimization recommendations.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds, and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What You'll Do

  • Serve as the in-house subject matter expert for Datadog's Cloud Cost Management products, including cost visibility across AWS, Azure, and GCP, Kubernetes and container cost allocation, custom and SaaS cost ingestion, budgets, anomaly detection, and cost optimization recommendations
  • Provide architectural guidance on capacity planning, comparing cloud service cost models, and balancing performance vs. cost trade-offs across different cloud environments
  • Guide customers on tokenomics and AI cost attribution across providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Google Gemini, Vertex AI, and GitHub Copilot), helping teams map API keys, models, and usage to teams and business units using Tag Pipelines.
  • Help enterprise clients track real-time AI spend changes, set up cost anomaly monitoring, and connect token usage back to business outcomes and unit economics (such as cost per user or cost per ticket).
  • Partner with Field teams to provide hands-on technical and architectural guidance to enterprise customers adopting CCM, including designing tagging and cost allocation strategies, showback and chargeback models, and cost reporting that connects spend to services, teams, and business units
  • Create high-impact technical collateral, including reference architectures, technical guides, blog articles, and documentation to enable Field teams and the broader customer community, covering topics like cloud billing data onboarding (AWS, Azure, GCP billing), Kubernetes cost attribution, token usage, unit economics, and rightsizing and commitment optimization
  • Act as a trusted advisor to Product Management by delivering actionable feedback informed by real-world field experience, helping shape the roadmap for cost allocation, multi-cloud cost visibility, token usage, optimization workflows, and FinOps integrations

Who You Are

  • You bring a strong engineering foundation, with hands-on experience managing, allocating, or optimizing cloud spend, or building FinOps programs and internal cost tooling in production environments at a large scale, and are comfortable diving deep into billing data and architectural tradeoffs to understand what drives cost
  • You are familiar with cloud infrastructure and core observability concepts, such as tracing, metrics, and logging, and understand how compute, storage, networking, and container platforms (including Kubernetes) translate into cloud bills
  • Deep understanding of cost models, performance characteristics, and capacity planning across various cloud services and managed platforms
  • Experience with languages such as Python and/or SQL, and familiarity with querying and modeling large billing datasets, tagging strategies, and infrastructure-as-code
  • Comfortable operating in rapidly evolving, ambiguous technical domains
  • You build deep context across teams and translate it into reusable, scalable solutions
  • You take ownership from problem definition through implementation and measurable outcomes
  • Highly detail-oriented, particularly when working on architectures and customer-facing technical assets
  • You bring strong listening and consultative skills and are experienced supporting customers across engineering, FinOps, and finance stakeholders, including in high-stakes situations such as cost spikes, budget overruns, and commitment planning
  • Demonstrates capability of utilizing AI tooling and scaling it 
  • Able to sit up to 4 hours, traveling to and from client sites
  • Able to travel via auto, train, or air up to 40% of the time

  • Successful track record with 5+ years experience working as a Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, or FinOps practitioner supporting cloud cost management, FinOps, or cloud financial optimization tools (e.g., Cloudability, CloudHealth, Vantage, Kubecost, native AWS Cost Explorer, Azure Cost Management, or GCP Billing)
  • Experience using Datadog and/or other observability tools in an SRE, DevOps, or platform engineering capacity, particularly owning cloud cost accountability or building internal cost reporting and automation

description:
Datadog's Technical Solutions (TS) organization is one of the largest organizations in the company — spanning Sales Engineers, Technical Account Managers, Enterprise Customer Success Managers, Technical Support Engineers, and Solutions Architects who work with prospects and customers across every stage of their journey with Datadog.

Technical Solutions Operations (TSO) exists to make that organization faster, smarter, and more scalable. We build the systems, analytics & programs that give TS teams more leverage — and we measure our success by the business outcomes we drive, not the projects we complete. The programs this team runs touch every function in TS, and the operating model you build will define how that scales.

We're looking for a Director of Technical Program Management to lead the TSO Program Management team. This role sits at the intersection of strategy and execution: you'll own the programs that shape how TS operates at scale, lead a team of technical program managers, and serve as a peer to the Directors and VPs who run the teams you support. Your counterparts are leaders overseeing hundreds of customer-facing technical professionals, and your role is to successfully interface with each organization with proactive solutions on how your team can help them be more effective. This is a rare opportunity to lead a function where the output isn't a deliverable, it's organizational capability. If you want to build something that compounds across an entire organization, this is the role.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What You’ll Do

  • Run the PMO as a business impact function. Own the PMO operating model end-to-end, including intake, prioritization, scoping, execution, and impact measurement — with every program directly linked to measurable business outcomes such as productivity gains, revenue influence, cost efficiency, or customer experience improvements. Establish a PMO operating standard that other TS leaders adopt as the benchmark.
  • Build capabilities that scale across TS, not point solutions. Build durable, cross-functional capabilities that drive business outcomes across every function in TS. Solve systemic problems with scalable solutions and operating models — not one-off fixes — and hold your team to the same standard.
  • Drive programs from alignment to impact. Establish clear scope, sequencing, ownership, and success metrics before execution begins. Hold your team to rigorous delivery standards and close every program with post-launch reporting that connects leverage created directly to business outcomes for partner teams.
  • Represent TSO in executive forums. Represent TSO in executive forums with Director and VP-level counterparts across TS. Come prepared with clear recommendations, framed trade-offs, and the ability to drive decisions — not surface issues. Own stakeholder relationships and outcomes and drive alignment across disparate teams. 
  • Deploy AI to create operational leverage. Identify and build AI-enabled workflows that reduce friction across how programs are planned, communicated, and executed — for your team and for the TS functions you support. This is a core expectation, not a future initiative. You bring a clear point of view on where AI creates a genuine capability shift and you build toward it.
  • Develop the TPM team and raise the bar. Lead a team of senior Technical Program Managers delivering complex, concurrent initiatives across TS. Raise the bar for execution quality, stakeholder management, and accountability — and develop a team that operates independently and owns outcomes.
  • Build cross-functional relationships before you need them. Build cross-functional relationships across TS and adjacent functions before programs require it. Use influence, credibility, and direct engagement to drive alignment, resolve tension, and expand the reach and impact of TSO well beyond its own boundaries.

Who You Are

  • 10+ years running complex, cross-functional programs at a senior level, with VPs and senior Directors as your primary stakeholders — ideally within a high-growth B2B SaaS go-to-market, customer-facing, or revenue operations organization
  • A systems builder with a track record of designing operating models, playbooks, and frameworks that other teams adopted as a reference standard
  • Autonomously executive-ready — decisive under ambiguity, composed under pressure, and capable of leading VP-level conversations without preparation coaching
  • Experienced applying AI as an operational tool, with a practical point of view on where it creates capability shifts — not just productivity gains
  • A developer of senior talent who raises the bar on what great program management looks like and builds teams that operate independently at a high standard
  • Outcome-oriented and metric-driven — you define success before work begins and hold yourself and your team accountable to delivering against it

Preferred Experience

  • Experience supporting large-scale go-to-market or customer-facing technical organizations spanning sales engineering, post-sales, technical support, or solutions architecture
  • Familiarity with support operations platforms and the workflows they enable across technical teams
  • Experience designing org-wide AI-enabled capabilities in an operational context
  • Background in tooling strategy, workforce planning, or operational transformation at scale in a SaaS environment

About the role

Datadog employs roughly 8,100 people across 35 countries through global subsidiaries, all under a Nevada parent. Some are operating companies. Others came to us through acquisitions. We open in new markets often enough that the structure is always moving, and we manage it in Diligent Entities. This role owns it.

The work is entity formation and maintenance in many jurisdictions, corporate records and statutory filings, and daily coordination with the Finance, Tax and People teams. You will deal directly with government agencies, registries, registered agents and local counsel around the world. You will also be the person the rest of the company asks whenever a question touches our corporate structure.

The role sits in Legal Operations, and you will report to our Senior Director, Legal Operations, who has supported entity management operations in the past. Our Associate General Counsel, Corporate & Securities owns the work product and sets the standards for entity management and for our securities filings. Legal Operations runs the function; Corporate & Securities owns the substance.

The placement also gives you breadth. Legal Operations covers legal technology and systems, process design, outside counsel and spend operations, restricted party and sanctions screening, product legal support, and the department's AI work. We expect to cross-train you across those areas over time, and to cross-train colleagues into entity work. Entity management will remain the substantial majority of this job.

On AI in particular, Legal Operations is where most of that work happens for the legal department. We look at how our current tools could be used better, we assess new ones, and we look for ways to extend AI into systems that were never built with it in mind. If you look at a manual process and wonder whether software should be doing it, there is room here for that.

On the securities side of the role

You will also handle Section 16 filings (Forms 3, 4 and 5), Forms 144 and Rule 10b5-1 plan administration, supervised by our Associate General Counsel, Corporate & Securities, who trains the team on it. Prior public company reporting experience is welcome but not required. We have trained people into this work before and it went well. What we need is someone who wants to learn it and who will hold the deadlines once trained.

 

What you will do

Global entity management: the core of the role

  • Entity lifecycle. Manage formations, foreign qualifications, branch registrations, conversions, mergers, dissolutions, liquidations and deregistrations for our US and international entities, working with outside service providers and local counsel in each jurisdiction.
  • Good standing. Keep every entity in good standing wherever it operates. That covers annual reports and returns, statutory filings and business licenses. It also covers records for registered agents and agents for service of process, and the local compliance requirements that differ by country.
  • Government agencies and registries. Deal directly with company registries, tax authorities, chambers of commerce and other government bodies on filings, registrations, certificates and inquiries, some of which need regular follow-up.
  • Compliance calendar. Own the global entity compliance calendar. Know what is due, where and when, and flag it early rather than relying on a service provider's reminder.
  • Directors, officers and authority. Track director and officer appointments and resignations, maintain signature and delegation of authority records, and prepare powers of attorney, incumbency certificates and secretary's certificates. Keep internal systems current and make sure the people who need to know about a change in signing authority are told.
  • Portfolio rationalization. Review the legacy and dormant entities we hold, including those that came in through acquisitions. Form a view on which should be maintained, consolidated or wound down, then carry out the plan.

Corporate records and governance

  • Corporate records. Maintain minute books, statutory registers, organizational charts and entity records worldwide, in physical and electronic form, so the portfolio stays audit-ready.
  • Governance documents. Draft board and stockholder resolutions, written consents, minutes for subsidiary matters, and organizational documents such as articles, bylaws and operating agreements, in support of routine governance matters and corporate transactions, for attorney review.
  • Document requests. Turn around internal and external requests for certificates of good standing, certified copies, apostilles and legalizations. These usually block something, so speed matters.

KYC and due diligence support

  • Incoming requests. Respond to and manage Know Your Customer (KYC), Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO) and related diligence requests from banks, financial partners, customers and other stakeholders.
  • Supporting documentation. Compile and maintain the entity ownership, formation and governance documentation those requests rely on.

Working with Finance, Tax and People

Entity decisions are rarely made by Legal alone, so a large share of this role is coordination.

  • Tax. Support tax-driven entity changes, restructurings and intercompany arrangements, and provide the corporate approvals, resolutions and records they require.
  • Finance and Treasury. Support statutory audits, bank account openings and closures, and signatory changes. Supply the entity data behind financial reporting and audit requests.
  • People. Work with the People team when we open in a new country. That covers employer registrations, local entity setup and the corporate steps that have to happen before anyone can be hired or paid.
  • Across the company. Be the reliable answer when Procurement, Sales, Real Estate or anyone else needs to know which entity to use, or how Datadog is structured.

Systems, data and process

  • Diligent Entities. Own Diligent Entities as our system of record, covering data integrity, configuration and reporting. You will be the internal expert who trains others on it.
  • Data quality. Run periodic audits of entity records, fix records where the data has drifted, and get the register to a point where it can be trusted without a manual check.
  • Process. Build and maintain the trackers, workflows and standard operating procedures the function runs on, and document them well enough that someone else can pick them up.
  • Automation and AI. Work with the wider Legal Operations team to automate the repetitive parts of entity work, and help assess where AI tools earn their place, both here and elsewhere in the department. Entity management is full of high-volume, rules-based work, which makes it a good place to test them. No prior AI experience is needed. Curiosity and judgment about where AI does and does not belong matter more.

Securities support

Supporting work, learnable on the job, performed for and supervised by our Associate General Counsel, Corporate & Securities.

  • Section 16. Prepare, file and track Forms 3, 4 and 5 for our Section 16 officers and directors, and maintain the supporting ownership records.
  • Forms 144 and 10b5-1. Prepare and file Forms 144 and administer the mechanics of Rule 10b5-1 plan adoptions, modifications and terminations.
  • Entity data for reporting. Supply the entity information behind our periodic SEC filings, including the subsidiary list filed with the Form 10-K.
  • Board support. Support board and committee matters as needed. Board and committee administration sits with our Corporate & Securities group.

Your team and the wider function

  • Your direct report. Manage, develop and set priorities for one Corporate Paralegal, and bring them along on the entity work as you standardize it.
  • Shared services. Legal Operations runs as a shared services team. You will be cross-trained across other Legal Operations workstreams, and colleagues will be cross-trained into entity work, so the team can cover for each other and hold consistent standards.

Who you are

What we need

  • Seven or more years of hands-on entity management experience, with substantial time on a multi-jurisdictional portfolio, whether in-house at a multinational, at a law firm or at a corporate services provider.
  • Practical experience with entity formation and ongoing maintenance in multiple countries, including foreign qualification, good standing, annual filings, registered agents and local statutory requirements.
  • Direct experience dealing with government agencies, company registries and regulators on corporate filings. You have chased a registry, fixed a rejected filing, and learned how long these things take.
  • A track record of working with internal partners outside Legal, such as Finance, Tax and People, where the work only lands if the coordination is good.
  • Proficiency with an entity management platform. We use Diligent Entities. If you have used a comparable system and will become an expert in ours, that works too.

job_title: Manager I, Engineering - Reference Tables Access
description:
The Reference Tables Access team owns the UI, MCP, APIs, and control plane that customers use to bring external data into Datadog. Reference Tables lets them use their own reference data to enrich and filter observability data without leaving the platform. The team also owns the table identity, metadata, permissions, quotas, validation, and lifecycle services behind these experiences.

Beyond the current product, the team is developing a consistent tabular abstraction that product teams can use without needing to manage the details of the underlying storage systems. This abstraction supports use cases from log enrichment and security to emerging analytical workflows built on Datadog’s internal Data Lake (ADP Lakehouse).

We’re looking for a hands-on technical leader to guide the team’s roadmap and develop these capabilities into a reliable platform. This role will shape how Datadog teams manage and build product experiences on top of tabular data.

description:
Datadog's Forward Deployed Engineering function is in an active growth phase, and the FDE Manager will play a central role in shaping what comes next. You are part field technical leader, part program architect, and part cross-functional connector. You will help determine what the FDE motion looks like at Datadog, contribute to its playbook, and push the boundaries of what the team can deliver.

description:
Datadog AI Research — Scholars Program with Carnegie Mellon University

Datadog AI Research (DAIR) is partnering with Carnegie Mellon University to support a small number of PhD students working on open research problems grounded by ongoing efforts at Datadog/DAIR. 

You will frame a problem, run your own experiments, and write up what you find, with compute and data at a scale most academic labs cannot provide.  You will collaborate with colleagues working on the same questions.

 

The Lab And The Research:

DAIR is an industrial research lab motivated by practical challenges in observability and software operation: detecting and diagnosing failures, understanding complex production environments, and helping engineers operate software more effectively. The lab focuses on creating specialized foundation models, post-training and evaluating AI agents, and building frontier-scale machine learning systems. By combining fundamental research with Datadog's large-scale, real-world data and infrastructure, the lab develops new AI capabilities and translates them into practical systems with meaningful impact.

Internship projects are shaped with your DAIR mentor and your CMU faculty advisor. You do not need prior experience with observability, monitoring, or infrastructure.

 

What You'll Do:

  • Own a research project end to end: framing the question, running the experiments, writing it up
  • Work directly with a DAIR mentor engaged in the same problem, and stay connected to your advisor and lab
  • Publish, and use the work toward your dissertation
  • See research reach production, when it works

Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. 

The Cashiering team’s mission is to ensure accurate, timely movement of funds across customer brokerage and retirement accounts while delivering a compliant, high-quality client experience. We operate with ethics and precision at the center of everything we do to protect our customers' assets.

Our team works closely with partners in Compliance, Operations, and Technology to streamline cashiering processes. We foster a supportive, collaborative environment where team members work together to solve complex operational challenges! Our collective goal is to build trusted, scalable financial processes that support Robinhood's growth.

As a Cashiering Specialist, you will manage high-volume cashiering workflows—primarily reviewing money movement requests, including ACH, check, wire, and other brokerage transactions—serving as a key operational link between advisors, clients, custodians, and internal partners. In this position, you will serve as quality assurance overview of transactions with high accuracy and efficiency while adhering to strict regulatory requirements including AML, and OFAC review. You will collaborate daily with advisors and internal operations teams to resolve inquiries and transaction discrepancies. Your work directly impacts the customer experience by ensuring that fund movements are completed seamlessly. This role provides an excellent opportunity to expand your knowledge of financial markets and back-office operations!

This role is based in our Westlake, TX or Clearwater, FL office, with in-person attendance expected 5 days per week during the 90-day onboarding period. After onboarding, in-person attendance is expected at least 3 days a week.

Shift Options:

  • 7:30 - 4 PM
  • 8:30 - 5 PM

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. 

What you’ll do

  • Review a high volume of money movement requests efficiently, and in line with internal policies and regulatory requirements.
  • Monitor and manage daily transaction queues to meet strict deadlines and service-level expectations, researching and resolving discrepancies and inquiries from initial intake to final resolution.
  • Safeguard the firm by enforcing AML and OFAC requirements and reviewing transactions for adherence to SOPs.
  • Partner with our clearing firm and internal teams (Operations, Compliance, Technology, Advisor Services) to facilitate transactions, resolve issues, and support collaborative projects across these departments.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement by identifying opportunities to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and client experience within cashiering operations.

What you bring

  • Strong knowledge of asset movement procedures, workflows, and regulatory considerations, along with a basic understanding of financial markets and the securities industry.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and organization, with the ability to manage multiple priorities at once.
  • Clear, professional communication skills, including excellent data entry, written, and verbal communication, and comfort engaging with clients and advisors over the phone.
  • 1-2 years of experience in financial operations, with an SIE required, (99 preferred) and a proven ability to manage transactional workflows using proprietary financial systems.
  • Committed and dependable in a fast-paced, high-volume environment, bringing a collaborative spirit, steady focus, and genuine care for clients and outcomes.
  • Proactive problem-solving abilities, strong analytical, decision-making, and critical thinking skills, with accountability for results and the ability to adapt quickly to new systems.

What we offer

  • Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career.
  • Performance-driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching.
  • Best-in-class benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents.
  • Access to the Robinhood Employee Fund that gives eligible US employees the opportunity to invest in a private employee fund that provides exposure to Robinhood Ventures funds.
  • Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not.
  • Lifestyle wallet — a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more.
  • Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits.
  • Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more!
  • Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces.

description:
About Ramp 
 Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
 The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
 We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.
 The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
 If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.
 
 About the Role
 Ramp’s Token Spend Management team helps finance and technical teams understand and manage what they spend across AI providers and subscriptions. We are building the third pillar of finance. The product brings provider usage and billing information together so customers can see where costs come from, attribute spend, and act on it with greater confidence.
 
 We’re looking for a senior backend engineer to build the systems behind that experience. You’ll own substantial projects from design through production, turn data from different providers into dependable product experiences, and work with product, design, data, and engineering partners to make complex spend information useful to customers. You will be involved in key company initiatives such as inference accounting, and figuring out new and novel ways to help companies not just manage, but think about their AI Spend.
 
 What You’ll Do
 Design and build backend services and APIs that support AI spend visibility, attribution, insights, and controls

 Build and improve integrations that ingest usage and billing information from supported providers

 Taking the data from those integrations and converting it into helpful structures for external customers, and internal product consumers

 Create reliable data models and processing workflows that make spend information accurate, traceable, and useful across the product

 Own projects from technical design through launch, monitoring, and iteration

 Improve the reliability, performance, and observability of systems as customer usage and provider coverage grow

 Partner with product, design, data, and engineering teammates to turn customer needs into practical solutions

 Raise the engineering bar through thoughtful design reviews, code reviews, and mentorship

 
 What You’ll Need
 Experience designing, building, and operating production backend systems, including APIs, data models, and asynchronous workflows

 Strong judgment about system design, data correctness, reliability, and when to keep a solution simple

 A track record of independently owning complex projects and shipping high-quality software

 Experience working with external data sources or integrations where data quality and changing interfaces matter

 Comfort working through ambiguous product problems with cross-functional partners

 Clear communication and a collaborative approach to technical decisions and feedback

 
 Nice to Haves
 Experience with usage metering, billing, spend management, or financial data products

 Experience integrating with AI providers or other third-party usage and billing APIs

 Experience building attribution, alerts, limits, or other systems that help customers understand and manage spend

 
 Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global) 
 Flexible PTO

 Centralized home-office equipment ordering

 Health and wellness stipend

 Budget for intra-office travel

 Weekly coffee stipend

 Pet insurance

About Ramp 
 Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
 The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
 We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.
 The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
 If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.
 
 About the Role
 Getting paid is still one of the most manual parts of running a business. Finance teams chase invoices over email, match payments to invoices by hand in spreadsheets, and close the books late because cash data is scattered across banks, payment processors, and ERPs.

Ramp's Accounts Receivable team is building the system that automates all of it, from the moment an invoice is sent to the moment cash is reconciled in the general ledger. We own the full receivables lifecycle: invoicing, collections, payments, cash application, and accounting sync.

We're looking for a senior backend engineer to own core pieces of that system. The work sits where hard engineering problems meet real money: matching messy payment data to the right invoices, keeping ledgers correct to the cent, and syncing reliably with the accounting systems our customers depend on. You'll own projects end to end, from design through production, and work closely with product and design to turn complex finance workflows into software that just works.
 
What You’ll Do
 Build the payment-matching systems that automatically apply incoming ACH, wire, card, and check payments to the right invoices, even when payment details are incomplete or inconsistent

 Design accurate data models where every dollar is traceable from invoice to payment to general ledger

 Build two-way integrations with ERPs like NetSuite and QuickBooks that stay consistent through retries, partial failures, and edits on either side

 Build collections workflows that help businesses get paid faster without hurting their customer relationships

 Own projects from problem definition and technical design through launch, monitoring, and iteration

 Raise the engineering bar through design reviews, code reviews, and mentorship

 What You’ll Need
 Product sense: you care about the customer problem, not just the ticket, and you push back when the spec is wrong

 Experience designing and operating production backend systems, including APIs, data models, and asynchronous workflows

 Strong system design judgment and the ability to balance speed, correctness, reliability, and simplicity

 A track record of independently owning complex projects and shipping high-quality software

 Strong communication skills and a collaborative approach to technical decisions

The Opportunity

We’re looking for an experienced Senior Associate to join our growing GTM Strategy & Operations team as the product owner for our GTM data and tooling products. Our team solves complex problems that require insight, creativity, and execution through building scalable processes, tools, and systems for our rapidly growing global business. You will own the roadmap, delivery, and adoption of the data products and sales productivity tools that power our Sales and Customer Success organizations, spanning both internally built products and third-party solutions, with decisions guided by speed, cost, scalability, and long-term maintainability. Doing this successfully requires a deep understanding of the “day in the life” for field teams, strong product management instincts, and the ability to translate business needs into build-versus-buy decisions and tooling solutions that help Datadog grow 10x.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

You Will

  • Own the product roadmap: Set the vision, strategy, and prioritized roadmap for GTM data products and sales productivity tools. Balance field needs, business impact, technical feasibility, cost, and maintainability while making clear decisions about where to invest, consolidate, replace, or retire.
  • Run the end-to-end product lifecycle for in-house tools: Write requirements and user stories, define MVPs, establish acceptance criteria, manage the backlog, and partner with GTM Systems, Data Engineering, and Analytics to ship, iterate, and sunset internally built products.
  • Establish the product operating model: Create a consistent approach to intake, prioritization, roadmap planning, product ownership, release readiness, feedback collection, and lifecycle management across our portfolio of products.
  • Make build-versus-buy calls: Lead structured evaluations (e.g., RFPs, pilots, time-boxed POCs) of third-party tools against in-house alternatives, build business cases, and present investment recommendations to GTM leadership
  • Lead AI product strategy: Identify, evaluate, prototype, and scale AI-powered capabilities, whether built in-house or bought, that improve prospecting, enrichment, personalization, and rep workflows, and help define the forward-looking AI roadmap for the Sales and CS organizations
  • Measure impact: Define and track success metrics across every tool and data product (e.g., adoption, data quality, time saved, pipeline influenced) and use the findings to make data-driven decisions to invest, consolidate, or retire
  • Partner with the field: Work closely with Sales and Customer Success to uncover workflow pain points through interviews, workflow observation, usage analysis and feedback loops. Distinguish user problems from requested features and translate these opportunities into product improvements that directly increase rep productivity.
  • Lead launch and adoption: Own release planning, change management, and onboarding in collaboration with Sales Enablement so field teams get maximum value from every product
  • Ensure seamless integration: Work with GTM Systems to maintain and improve integrations between our tools, Salesforce CRM, and the broader GTM tech stack and data infrastructure
  • Set the standard: Build and enforce governance frameworks, acceptable use policies, and data hygiene standards across all managed tools and data products to ensure consistency and compliance

Requirements

  • Experience: 4-6+ years of experience in GTM Strategy & Operations, data or analytics roles, product management, or management consulting, ideally within SaaS or high-growth B2B technology
  • Product management fundamentals: Proven ability to take a product from problem definition through requirements, prioritization, launch, and iteration, including writing clear PRDs, user stories, scope tradeoffs, and communicating to technical and non-technical teams why the team will or will not invest in a request. 
  • Build-versus-buy judgment: Experience weighing in-house development against third-party solutions on cost, speed, scalability, and strategic fit, and making a clear recommendation
  • Data fluency: Strong understanding of GTM data (contacts, accounts, intent and enrichment signals) and the ability to define data quality standards; comfortable with SQL and working with data warehouses and BI tools to analyze usage and outcomes
  • AI innovation: Strong interest in exploring, launching, and scaling new GTM AI technologies, including practical experience prototyping or deploying AI-enabled workflows
  • Cross-functional collaboration: Strong track record of partnering with Sales, CS, Engineering, and Data teams to identify pain points and deliver solutions from requirements through rollout
  • Analytical mindset: Comfortable defining product metrics, measuring adoption and ROI, and communicating findings clearly to senior stakeholders
  • CRM knowledge: Solid understanding of Salesforce CRM and how data products and sales tools integrate into the broader GTM tech stack
  • Communication: Effective communicator, both written and verbal, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously
  • Ownership mentality: Self-starter who takes initiative, operates independently, and drives projects through to completion without heavy oversight

Bonus Points

  • SaaS background: Experience at a high-growth B2B SaaS company managing a GTM or sales tool portfolio or an internal data product
  • AI passion: Stays current on the latest AI news, has a passion for experimentation, has fully integrated AI into professional workflows, and vibe codes on the weekend
  • Technical aptitude: Working knowledge of APIs and how sales tools connect to CRM systems and data infrastructure; has shipped a prototype or internal tool of their own
  • Tool fluency: Hands-on familiarity with the B2B sales technology landscape, including contact intelligence (e.g., ZoomInfo, Cognism), outbound sequencing (e.g., Groove, Salesloft, Outreach), and data enrichment tools (e.g., Clay, Clearbit, Crunchbase)
  • Broader stack exposure: Familiarity with adjacent tools such as buyer intent platforms (e.g., Bombora, G2) or conversation intelligence (e.g., Gong)
  • Full-funnel experience: Experience supporting tool adoption across Sales Development, Account Executive, and Customer Success teams

Fuse Energy is an energy startup on a mission to make energy abundant and affordable, fast. We combine first-principles thinking with cutting-edge technology to build a radically better energy system.
 We've raised over $200M from top-tier investors including Balderton, Lakestar, Accel, Creandum, Lowercarbon, Ribbit, 20VC, Hummingbird and Collaborative Fund, alongside strategic angels including Nico Rosberg and GPs behind Meta, Revolut, Spotify and Uber.
 We're building a fully integrated energy company: developing our own solar, batteries and other generation projects, building our own hardware, improving and developing grid infrastructure, trading power in real time, using AI across the business, and installing distributed energy in homes. By selling directly to consumers we cut out the middleman, lower costs and pass the savings on to our customers.
 As a Senior Test Engineer, you will play a critical role in ensuring Fuse’s hardware products and energy systems meet applicable regulatory, safety, and performance requirements throughout their lifecycle. You will work hands-on with prototypes and deployed systems, collaborating closely with hardware, firmware, software, and operations teams to translate regulatory requirements into practical, testable engineering outcomes.
 In this role, you will be directly involved in design validation, certification, and end-of-line verification, navigating a broad regulatory landscape including electrical safety, EMC, grid connection standards, and environmental compliance.
 
 Responsibilities: 
 Plan, set up, and execute hands-on validation, verification, and compliance tests on Fuse Energy hardware systems, both in laboratory environments and on live sites.
 Prepare systems for external certification and type testing, coordinating with notified bodies, test houses, and third-party laboratories.
 Support in-field testing, commissioning, and acceptance activities at customer, partner, or pilot sites to validate safety, performance, and grid interoperability.
 Execute targeted test campaigns covering areas such as electrical safety (LVD), EMC, grid code compliance (e.g. G99/G100 and EU equivalents), functional safety, and environmental requirements.
 Identify, analyse, and troubleshoot hardware, firmware, and system-level issues uncovered during testing, working closely with design and software engineers to drive corrective actions.
 Design test equipment and software to perform automated test either in HIL testing or EOL verification at the production site.
 Develop and maintain thorough test documentation, including test procedures, reports, evidence packs, and compliance dossiers for internal use and external audits.
 Communicate test results, risks, and compliance status clearly to engineering, operations, and leadership teams, supporting informed technical and commercial decisions.
 Contribute to continuous improvement of Fuse’s compliance, testing, and quality processes as products and deployments scale.
 Requirements 
 Bachelor’s degree or higher in Electrical Engineering, Electronic Engineering, or a closely related technical discipline.
 At least 5 years of experience in a hardware test, compliance, regulatory, or certification-focused engineering role.
 Strong hands-on experience working with electrical or power-electronic systems in laboratory and/or field environments.
 Proficiency with standard electrical test and measurement equipment, such as oscilloscopes, power analysers, multimeters, insulation testers, and data acquisition systems.
 Experience creating structured test plans, executing formal test procedures, and producing clear, high-quality technical documentation.
 Working knowledge of relevant standards and regulations, such as LVD, EMC, grid connection codes, and related EU/UK directives (or a strong ability to learn them quickly).
 Excellent problem-solving and debugging skills, with a rigorous, detail-oriented approach to engineering work.
 Ability to work independently, manage multiple test activities in parallel, and operate effectively across lab, site, and external partner environments.
 Benefits 
 Competitive salary and an equity sign-on bonus
 Biannual bonus scheme
 Fully expensed tech to match your needs
 Paid annual leave
 Breakfast and dinner allowance for office based employees

As we continue with rapid growth, you will own the day-to-day mechanics of cash, optimal capital allocation, banking, and liquidity at a company that commits significant capital to compute and infrastructure.  Cash and Liquidity Management 
 Own daily cash positioning across operating accounts and entities across various banking and treasury partners, and maintain the rolling cash forecasts

 Own bank account administration across all entities and banking partners, including account openings and closures, signer updates, KYC requests, and portal access reviews.

 Oversee payment controls, including approval workflows, segregation of duties, and review of high-value or unusual wires.

 Manage the company’s investment portfolio, including money market funds, bank deposits, and separately managed accounts, in line with the investment policy, and oversee the external managers who run it.

 Design and build an in-house investment and hedging program, including direct fixed income, compute price hedging, and yield rates

 Develop management reporting covering portfolio performance, market conditions, and policy compliance for leadership and board

 Monitor FX exposure from international entities and vendors, and support hedging analysis and execution.

 Automate repeatable treasury work such as cash positioning, bank reconciliations, and reporting using AI and workflow tools, while keeping people accountable for every approval and movement of money.

 Prepare FBAR filings, manage letters of credit and bank guarantees, and support audit requests related to cash and investments.

 
 Qualifications

 Experience with developing and managing an in-house investment program and market hedging

 Working knowledge of cash forecasting, bank operations, payment rails, and short-duration fixed income.

 Strong controls mindset and attention to detail: this role touches money movement, and accuracy is non-negotiable.

 Clear written communication, sound escalation judgment, and comfort building process from scratch.

 Nice to have: FX hedging, treasury management systems, debt or credit facilities, IPO and SOX readiness, or CTP, CFA, or CPA progress.

job_title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, Enterprise Agent Evals & Efficiency)
description:
About the Role 
 The Enterprise Agent Evals & Efficiency team makes Perplexity's agents better at completing real work across enterprise connectors, tools, and data. Our goal is to help agents choose the right tools, use the right context, and complete complex workflows reliably, with less time and compute. This team owns the improvement loop: define what successful work looks like, build evaluations that measure it, understand where agents fail, and ship changes that improve outcomes.
 This is a hands-on engineering role with end-to-end ownership, from building realistic enterprise evaluation environments to shipping improvements across the agent harness, tools, and skills. You'll create complex scenarios spanning connected systems, data, and permissions, use them to identify where agents struggle, and improve the tools agents call, the skills they follow, the context they receive, and the models they use. Working with AI Research, Connectors, and Platform teams, you'll turn experimental results into measurable gains in task success, latency, and cost per successful task. The goal is not just to measure agents, but to make more enterprise work reliable and practical to automate.
 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Build realistic enterprise evaluation environments spanning connected applications, representative datasets, user roles, and permissions, with complex, multi-step workflows and reproducible system state.

 Own evaluation infrastructure, task suites, and automated graders that measure how well agents complete enterprise work, calibrated against human judgment and grounded in end-to-end outcomes.

 Analyze agent trajectories and production failures, identify root causes, and ship improvements across the agent harness, tools, and skills that measurably improve task success and reliability.

 Develop reusable skills and improve tool descriptions, schemas, and result handling so agents can select the right tools, execute workflows correctly, and recover from errors with fewer unnecessary calls.

 Build and evaluate model-selection and routing strategies that match each task to the right model and effort level, balancing quality, latency, reliability, and cost.

 Improve agent efficiency through context management, skill loading, caching, and execution strategies that reduce wasted tokens and cost per successful task without compromising quality or safety.

 Build regression gates and launch-readiness signals for model, connector, tool, skill, and harness changes, and validate that evaluation gains translate into better production outcomes.
 

 Qualifications 
 5+ years of software engineering or machine learning engineering experience, with a track record of owning complex production systems from design through deployment and operation.

 Strong system design skills, including building reliable, scalable infrastructure for experimentation, evaluation, or data-intensive applications.

 Strong proficiency in a backend language such as Python, Go, or Rust, and the ability to work effectively across a multi-language production stack.

 Hands-on experience building, evaluating, or improving LLM-based applications or agents, including tool use and multi-step workflows.

 Deep expertise in at least one of the following:
 Evaluation infrastructure, benchmark design, and automated grading.

 Agent harnesses, tool interfaces, and reusable skills for complex workflows.

 Realistic test environments or simulations spanning multiple systems, datasets, permissions, and stateful workflows.

 Model selection, routing, and inference efficiency, including context management and caching.

 
 Strong experimental and statistical judgment, including choosing representative tasks, defining meaningful success criteria, diagnosing failures, and distinguishing real improvements from noise.

 Sound technical judgment in balancing task quality, latency, reliability, and cost, with a track record of translating evaluation findings into shipped improvements.

 A track record of leading ambiguous, cross-team initiatives from architecture through production adoption, setting technical direction, and raising engineering quality through mentorship.

 
 If you’re excited about this role, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every qualification. We value demonstrated impact, deep ownership, and the initiative to turn ambiguity into results.

Fuse Energy is an energy startup on a mission to make energy abundant and affordable, fast. We combine first-principles thinking with cutting-edge technology to build a radically better energy system.
 We've raised over $200M from top-tier investors including Balderton, Lakestar, Accel, Creandum, Lowercarbon, Ribbit, 20VC, Hummingbird and Collaborative Fund, alongside strategic angels including Nico Rosberg and GPs behind Meta, Revolut, Spotify and Uber.
 We're building a fully integrated energy company: developing our own solar, batteries and other generation projects, building our own hardware, improving and developing grid infrastructure, trading power in real time, using AI across the business, and installing distributed energy in homes. By selling directly to consumers we cut out the middleman, lower costs and pass the savings on to our customers.
 We’re looking for a Supplier Quality Engineer to join our China supply chain team. As an early member, you’ll own quality across our external factories, working directly with our Head of Supply Chain China and our UK R&D teams. We’re looking for a hands-on engineer with deep technical acumen, who can audit a production line, find the root cause of a defect and enforce stringent quality standards with top-tier suppliers under compressed timelines.
 
 Responsibilities
 Audit supplier production lines and quality systems, and track corrective actions to closure
 Own quality through new product introduction (NPI): first article inspection, pilot builds and ramp to mass production
 Work with R&D on manufacturing standards, certifications and acceptance criteria, so quality and compliance are built in at source
 Run incoming and outgoing quality control with clear acceptance criteria for each supplier
 Lead root cause analysis on defects (8D reports, FMEA) and push suppliers to permanent fixes
 Track supplier quality performance (defect rate, yield)
 Be the real-time link between Chinese factories and our UK teams on quality
 Requirements 
 Bachelor’s degree or higher in a STEM discipline from a top-tier university
 Supplier quality, manufacturing quality or related experience in hardware, electronics or manufactured physical products
 Hands-on factory audit experience across multiple external manufacturers
 Working knowledge of 8D (structured problem-solving report), FMEA (failure mode analysis) and SPC (statistical process control)
 Strong understanding of electrical and mechanical components, specifically PCBAs, power electronics or battery packs/systems

description:
Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. 

The Financial Crimes Team at Robinhood works across multiple verticals to protect our customers and ensure strict compliance with all relevant Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Sanctions regulations. As our team of passionate professionals continues to evolve the program, we are intensely focused on leveraging innovative thinking, advanced analytics, and cutting-edge technology to build a best-in-class Financial Crimes Program.

As the Senior Specialist, Model Validation & Analytics, you will play a key role in this mission by executing the validation, testing, tuning, and optimization of various transaction monitoring and filtering programs across Financial Crimes. You will partner closely with the AML Surveillance Team, engineering partners, and cross-functional verticals to ensure our financial crimes models and systems are accurately implemented, rigorously evaluated, and effectively calibrated to meet the diverse regulatory requirements of our domestic and international lines of business.

This role is based in our Denver, CO, New York, NY, or Westlake, TX office(s), with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What you’ll do

  • Model Validation & Review Execution: Perform independent, rigorous quantitative and qualitative analyses of rule-based and machine learning financial crimes surveillance models, filtering systems, and detection logic targeting model design, algorithm soundness, data integrity, and change management
  • Technical Review & Remediation: Act as a technical bridge within a fast-paced fintech environment by leveraging a solid foundation in data engineering, data modeling, and infrastructure. Collaborate seamlessly with software engineers, data engineers, and data scientists to decipher complex logic, evaluate model implementations, test data pipelines, and support the remediation of model issues.
  • Optimization & Model Tuning: Execute effective tuning methodologies and statistical analyses to continuously calibrate and enhance surveillance models. Work on strategic initiatives focused on maximizing risk detection capabilities while systematically reducing false positive volumes to ensure an efficient and effective alert review process.
  • Logic & Data Integrity Assurance: Conduct comprehensive data validation and logic testing initiatives to establish a strong foundation of data quality. Ensure the completeness, accuracy, and end-to-end reliability of critical data pipelines and inputs feeding our compliance models, mitigating systemic risks and safeguarding the integrity of our transaction monitoring ecosystem.
  • Subject Matter Expertise: Serve as a knowledgeable subject matter resource in AML and Model Risk, providing practical domain insights and supporting cross-functional partners in understanding model logic, performance, and risk trade-offs.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Build strong working partnerships across engineering, product, and compliance teams to ensure technical solutions are conceptually sound, effective, and aligned with our risk tolerance.
  • Change & Issue Management: Uphold change and issue management policies for covered systems, models, and solutions, ensuring end-to-end traceability and maintaining defensible documentation for internal audit and external regulators.
  • AI Strategy & Tech-Forward Adoption: Bring hands-on capabilities and experience leveraging AI tools, Large Language Models (LLMs), and automation techniques to enhance daily productivity, elevate deliverable quality, and optimize team workflows.
  • Documentation & Reporting: Author thorough, concise, and defensible validation reports, change and issues management documentation, and executive summaries that clearly explain model theory, testing logic, performance findings, and actionable recommendations for key stakeholders.

 

What you bring

  • Education: Bachelor's Degree or equivalent in a quantitative, technical, or financial field (e.g., Computer Science, Data Analytics, Statistics, or Finance)
  • Experience: 5+ years of experience across AML, Financial Crimes, or risk management within the financial services or fintech industry, with a focus on model validation, quantitative analysis, or surveillance system management.
  • Domain Expertise: 3+ years of direct experience in the verification, validation, testing, or tuning of AML rule-based systems and/or machine learning models, along with a working knowledge of core Model Risk Management (MRM) principles and governance standards.
  • Technical & Analytical Skills: Proficiency in SQL and experience using quantitative tools or programming languages (e.g., Python, R) to query large datasets, perform statistical analyses, and evaluate model performance.
  • Adaptability & Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to explain complex technical and quantitative concepts to non-technical partners, coupled with an ability to manage multiple competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.

 

What we offer

  • Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career.
  • Performance-driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching.
  • Best-in-class benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents.

  • Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits.
  • Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more!
  • Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces.

job_title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, Enterprise Trust & Governance)
description:
About the Role
 The Enterprise Trust & Governance team builds the control plane that lets the world’s largest organizations deploy Perplexity broadly and with confidence. Computer and our agents work across a growing share of our customers’ environments, tools, and models. For administrators, that makes precise, enforceable control essential: who can do what, with which data, through which agents, and within what usage limits. This team makes those controls easy to manage, reliable and consistent across every product, and transparent to the people accountable for them.
 This is a product and platform engineering role with end-to-end ownership, from shaping the architecture and policy models to shipping the experiences our customers’ administrators and security teams use every day. You’ll work across product and infrastructure teams to turn complex enterprise requirements into reusable primitives and intuitive controls. The scope spans identity and provisioning, fine-grained role-based access across connectors, tool actions, and models, customer-managed encryption keys, admin APIs, audit logs, and policy and usage controls. Strong governance helps enterprises move from pilots to company-wide rollouts and gives them the confidence to entrust agents with greater responsibility over time.
 
 Key Responsibilities
 Own enterprise identity and provisioning, including SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM, WorkOS integrations, and support for identity providers such as Okta and Microsoft Entra ID.

 Build the permissions platform, with fine-grained roles and permissions for connectors, tool actions, models, and model effort levels, enforced consistently across products and agent workflows.

 Design and ship secure, well-documented admin APIs for audit logs, members, groups, roles, and settings.

 Build policy controls for model and feature availability, staged rollouts, model deprecations, usage and spend limits, alerts, and cost-center allocation.

 Build admin-facing analytics for adoption, usage, spend, and policy enforcement, helping organizations measure value and manage their deployments.

 Deliver audit logs and change notifications that help administrators investigate activity, track configuration changes, and support compliance.

 Set the technical bar for authorization correctness and reliability, with fast, consistent, explainable permission checks, well-defined failure behavior, and strong tenant isolation.

 Partner with Product, Design, Security, Sales, and Customer Success to translate complex enterprise requirements into reusable platform capabilities and intuitive admin experiences.
 

 Qualifications
 4+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of owning complex backend systems from design through production operation.

 Strong system design skills, including building reliable, scalable, multi-tenant SaaS platforms with clear security and isolation boundaries.

 Strong proficiency in a backend language such as Python, Go, or Rust, and hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure such as AWS and Kubernetes.

 Deep expertise in at least one of the following:
 Enterprise identity and provisioning, including OAuth, OIDC, SAML, and SCIM.

 Permissions platforms, fine-grained authorization, and policy enforcement.

 Encryption, customer-managed keys, and key lifecycle management.

 Enterprise admin platforms, audit infrastructure, or usage and spend analytics.

 
 Experience building or integrating enterprise identity and access systems, including platforms such as WorkOS, Okta, or Microsoft Entra ID.

 Sound technical judgment in security-sensitive systems, balancing threat models, authorization correctness, and failure behavior with usability and delivery speed.

 A track record of leading ambiguous, cross-team initiatives from architecture through adoption, setting technical direction for shared platforms, and raising engineering quality through mentorship.

 If you’re excited about this role, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every qualification. We value demonstrated impact, deep ownership, and the initiative to turn ambiguity into results.

The Growth team owns the product loops that help people discover, adopt, and build lasting habits around our most important AI experiences — and on mobile that means owning everything from the App Store listing to the first task a user finishes to the moment they upgrade.
 As an Android growth engineer at Perplexity, you'll work across the full mobile funnel — install, activation, onboarding, push and lifecycle messaging, conversion, retention, and in-app purchase moments — for Perplexity, Comet, and Computer on Android. Engineers are responsible for end-to-end projects: rebuilding onboarding as a series of experiments, wiring in-app purchase and paywall surfaces to our billing systems, shipping notification experiences people actually keep enabled, and turning ASO and deep-link work into measurable adoption.
 Growth at Perplexity goes beyond incremental funnel optimization. The team sits close to the core product — we translate behavioral signals, model outputs, and fast experimentation into durable product surfaces used across consumer and enterprise workflows. You'll move fast, run many experiments in parallel, and own the outcome end-to-end, while respecting the constraints mobile brings: release cycles, store review, and version fragmentation.
 Why Perplexity is different 
 Craftsmanship. We build high quality, tasteful products targeting both the AI native and AI curious.

 Ownership. You identify the problem, design the solution and ship it.

 Entrepreneurship. We think like founders, act with urgency, and hustle to deliver for each other and our users.

 Scholarship. Work among highly talented peers, pursuing knowledge and truth, upleveling ourselves, our teams, and our products.

 Partnership. We amplify each others' strengths, break down silos, and give selflessly to help our colleagues deliver excellence.

 What you'll do 
 Design, build, and own growth surfaces across the mobile funnel — install, activation, onboarding, lifecycle, conversion, retention, and paid upgrade moments — on Android.

 Lead experiments end-to-end, from hypothesis and instrumentation through implementation, analysis, and rollout, shipping many in parallel despite app release cadence. Build the flag-driven and server-driven patterns that let us test without waiting on a store release.

 Own in-app purchase and paywall surfaces: billing integrations, subscription and credit purchase flows, entitlement correctness, and pricing and packaging experiments.

 Build push and lifecycle notification experiences that earn their opt-in — permission prompts, targeting, timing, deep links back into the right task, and the instrumentation to prove they drive retention rather than churn.

 Make cross-platform surfaces feel native. Partner with web and design engineers so onboarding, upsells, and in-task nudges are consistent across web, iOS, and Android

 Partner with rest of Growth to optimize app store performance and attribution

 Hill-climb on the metrics that matter: install-to-activation, D1/D7/D30 retention, notification opt-in and engagement, paid conversion, and habit formation, instrumented with clean data and trustworthy experiment readouts.

 Partner closely with Product, Design, Data Science, Monetization, Marketing, and the core Mobile team to translate behavioral signals into durable product surfaces.

 Qualifications 
 3+ years of professional mobile engineering experience shipping consumer apps at meaningful scale on Android.

 Strong native skills — Kotlin/Jetpack Compose — and the willingness to flex into other parts of the stack to unblock yourself and others.

 Experience owning a full release cycle: build and release tooling, phased rollouts, store review, crash and regression monitoring, and rolling back safely.

 Strong execution: you ship many experiments and product improvements in parallel and drive them to a clear outcome.

 Familiarity with A/B testing and experimentation platforms (Eppo, Statsig, Optimizely, or in-house equivalents) especially inside a versioned app.

 Comfort data-informed decision-making — you can pull, segment, and interpret your own funnel data.

 Strong product judgment; you translate user behavior and growth opportunities into simple, effective technical solutions.

 Self-motivated with strong ownership instincts; you propose experiments, ship features ahead of schedule, and drive improvements without asking for permission.

 Genuine interest and adoption of AI products and willingness to learn quickly.

 Nice to have 
 Direct experience on a growth or experimentation-heavy team

 Deep experience with in-app payments

 Experience with mobile attribution and measurement stacks (AppsFlyer, Adjust, Branch) and paid mobile acquisition.

 ASO experience, including store listing experiments and localized metadata.

 Comfort reaching into the backend or web stack to unblock yourself end-to-end.

 Time spent at a fast-growing startup or on a high-ownership engineering team.
