About Ramp 
 Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
 The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
 We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.
 The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
 If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.
 
 About the Role 
 Ramp's Financial Crime Compliance (FCC) team is looking for a senior investigator ready to shift from running cases to scaling the systems that run cases. You've built real depth in TM Alerts, AML Investigations, Complex Fraud, and EDD Reviews; you know what a good escalation looks like, where analysts get stuck, and where automation actually holds up in production versus just looks good in a demo. In this role, you'll spend most of your time partnering with Engineering and the Head of FCC Tooling to turn that judgment into scaled AI systems: testing model outputs, labeling and calibrating results, and making sure every automated decision point is well-documented and properly governed. You'll stay close enough to FCC's day-to-day workflows and will partake in some of them, but this is fundamentally a builder role.
  
 What You'll Do
 Partner directly with Engineering and the Head of FCC Tooling on automation experimentation and AI initiatives across TM, sanctions, complex fraud, and EDD, moving prototypes from one-off calibration exercises to defined, repeatable evaluation processes.

 Design and run labeling and tagging workflows for model outputs (e.g., TM alert dispositions, sanctions/PEP hit review) building a structured, documented pipeline in place of today's ad hoc process

 Define and maintain test sets, scenario coverage, and evaluation frameworks for compliance AI/agent tools in partnership with the engineers building them

 Own the documentation and governance layer for every automated or AI-assisted decision point

 Work with the FCC team to understand current workflows to guide innovative solutions

 Recommend automation and AI adoption decisions with evidence and escalate control-posture or model-risk trade-offs to compliance leadership

 5+ years of financial services experience in compliance, AML, or related regulatory advisory roles, preferably in fintech

 Demonstrated senior-investigator experience across TM Alerts, AML Investigations, Complex Fraud, and EDD Reviews

 Direct experience testing, labeling, or evaluating AI/ML model outputs, or strong aptitude and demonstrated fast ramp-up if new to formal model evaluation

 Strong AI fluency and data analytics skills

 Comfort partnering with engineers day-to-day and ability to translate compliance judgment into build specs, test cases, and evaluation criteria engineers can act on

 Strong project management and documentation rigor

 Ability to scope an ambiguous automation problem, choose an approach, and deliver a durable outcome with minimal oversight

 Experience working with outsourced testing/QA partners on model tuning or signal collection

 At Linear, we are committed to quality. Security is an essential part of that quality — not a layer that we add later, but something we build in from the start. We have a foundational security program we're proud of but, as Linear evolves our product and scales into enterprise, there's meaningful work ahead: staying ahead of vulnerabilities as our attack surface grows, responding fast and cleanly when incidents happen, and hardening our product and infrastructure. As Security Engineer at Linear, you'll be operating in a high-autonomy role with real scope, doing hands-on security work across the product and infrastructure we build.
 Location & work mode

 What you’ll do 
 Depending on your experience / skillset and our broader priorities, you could:
 Operate, automate, and extend vulnerability management end-to-end: triage, prioritize, and drive remediation across product, infrastructure, and dependencies, and keep the program’s SLAs meaningful rather than theoretical

 Run our bug bounty program: triage incoming reports, validate severity, work with engineering on fixes, and keep researcher relationships professional and responsive

 Lead product security testing: threat model new features (including AI/agent-facing surfaces), review designs and code for security-relevant risk, and do hands-on testing (manual and tool-assisted) rather than relying solely on scanners

About the Team

The Office Technology team designs, deploys, and operates the network infrastructure that keeps Datadog’s global offices connected, secure, and reliable. The team owns routing, switching, wireless, office firewalls, connectivity, and the observability and operational practices needed to provide a dependable employee experience at scale.

About the Role

As a Senior Network Engineer on the Office Technology team, you will own major network services and complex multi-site initiatives from problem definition and design through implementation, migration, and stable operations. You will act as a technical anchor for the team, leading design reviews and difficult troubleshooting, improving standards and automation, and helping other engineers deliver high-quality work.

This is a senior level role that combines hands-on engineering with technical leadership. You will shape team roadmap proposals and technical decisions through evidence and clear tradeoffs, while remaining accountable for reliable delivery and day-to-day operability.

What You’ll Do

  • Design resilient, scalable solutions across LAN, Wi-Fi, routing, switching, and office firewalls, with explicit failure domains, capacity assumptions, security controls, and migration paths
  • Author RFCs and lead design reviews, clearly documenting goals, constraints, alternatives, decisions, risks, validation, rollout, and rollback
  • Build production readiness into network changes through meaningful service objectives, monitoring, alerting, runbooks, capacity planning, failure testing, and operational handoff
  • Design reusable automation for provisioning, configuration, policy, compliance, telemetry, and change validation, with appropriate testing, peer review, drift detection, staged rollout, and safe rollback
  • Own, alongside other senior engineers and leadership, the health and lifecycle of major network services, using data to improve reliability, coverage, performance, security, supportability, and cost
  • Lead difficult incidents and root-cause investigations, communicate clearly during high-impact events, and ensure follow-up work addresses systemic causes
  • Evaluate technology and vendor options and make pragmatic recommendations grounded in operability, security, scalability, and business impact
  • Partner closely with Security, IT Support, Endpoints, AV, Workplace, Construction, Infrastructure teams, and external vendors on cross-functional initiatives
  • Mentor other engineers, delegate effectively, improve team standards and documentation, and raise the quality of design and operational practices
  • Participate in operational support, incident response, and planned maintenance activities as appropriate for the team

Who You Are

  • A deeply experienced, hands-on network engineer with strong knowledge of TCP/IP, routing, switching, VLANs, wireless, DNS, DHCP, firewalls, and enterprise network security
  • Experienced designing and operating resilient network infrastructure across distributed offices or campus environments
  • Skilled at diagnosing complex issues using packet captures, logs, flow data, dashboards, and vendor telemetry, and at reasoning from protocols and failure modes
  • Comfortable building maintainable automation using scripting, APIs, infrastructure-as-code, version control, testing, and CI/CD practices
  • Strong in production engineering practices, including observability, service objectives, capacity planning, change safety, incident response, and post-incident improvement
  • Able to take ambiguous problems from problem statement to durable solution, balancing reliability, security, user experience, cost, and delivery speed
  • A clear, concise communicator who can lead technical discussions, explain tradeoffs, and build alignment with technical and non-technical partners
  • A thoughtful mentor who raises the quality of others’ work without becoming a bottleneck or creating unnecessary process
  • Responsible in your use of AI-assisted engineering tools: you protect sensitive data, validate outputs, and know when deterministic automation is the safer choice

 

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you're passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply.

Bonus Points

  • Experience with Datadog or other observability platforms, including network device monitoring, flow analytics, synthetic testing, and service-level reporting
  • Experience with Python, Ansible, Terraform, Git-based workflows, or network automation frameworks
  • Experience with network access control, RADIUS or 802.1X, segmentation, VPNs, or identity-aware and zero-trust networking
  • Experience delivering global office expansions, infrastructure refreshes, or complex migrations in a rapidly scaling organization

The Datadog Security design team (K9 Design, as we lovingly call it) is hiring a senior product design manager to lead design across our security products. This is a chance to shape an industry-leading experience for a new kind of Datadog user: security practitioners who need to catch threats where they start, stop them when they land, and shut down exposures before they turn into something worse.

You'll lead a team of designers at various stages of their careers across cloud, code and data security, turning an overwhelming amount of signal into something a security team can act on. Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards.

As a Software Engineer, you’ll build and own backend services, infrastructure, and data systems that support Robinhood’s core financial products. You’ll solve complex scalability challenges while gaining deep expertise in U.S. financial systems and making a direct impact on the products used by millions.

The Brokerage team’s mission is to pave the way for launching new features, expanding into diverse financial services, and welcoming millions more people into the financial system. The team owns critical services that support trading and brokerage infrastructure and partners closely with other engineering, product, and operations teams across Robinhood.

The Incentives team drives user growth and engagement through both strategic incentives and platform capabilities. One sub-team focuses on increasing net deposits by testing incentive and non-incentive levers, while the other builds Robinhood’s centralized, scalable platform to support personalized, company-wide rewards.

The Identity team protects both Robinhood and its customers by preventing fraud and ensuring regulatory compliance. They own key systems for identity verification, KYC, and fraud prevention across all products, and collaborate closely with teams like Data Science, Brokerage, Crypto, and Security to support global expansion and product launches.

These roles are based in either our Menlo Park, CA or New York city offices, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What you’ll do

  • Design, build, test, and deploy scalable backend services and systems with a strong emphasis on long-term maintainability.

  • Develop product-facing features and platform enhancements that meet strict correctness and scalability standards.

  • Identify and implement improvements to system performance, engineering productivity, and risk reduction.

  • Collaborate closely with client teams, cross-functional partners, and external vendors to deliver impactful technical solutions.

What you bring

  • 2+ years of experience in software development.

  • Strong track record of successfully delivering large-scope technical projects in cross-functional team environments.

  • Commitment to high standards in code quality and review processes.

  • Solid understanding of backend development, system design, and the intersection of product and engineering.

  • Proficiency in Go or Python.

  • Hands-on experience with Kafka or similar data streaming technologies.

  • Familiarity with managing and processing large-scale datasets.

Bonus points

  • Experience working at a fintech company or financial institution.

  • Familiarity with technologies like Postgres, Kubernetes (K8s), Redis, and AWS (or similar cloud platforms).

What we offer

  • Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career

  • Performance-driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching

  • Best-in-class benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents

  • Lifestyle wallet — a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more

  • Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health support

  • Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more!

  • Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces

The Anomaly Detection team’s mission is to build scalable, cost effective systems that can automatically detect anomalies in our customers’ system telemetry. The ultimate goal is to be  able to intelligently find problems in system telemetry proactively without the need for our customers to set up or configure specific alarms or alerts. This is a chance to work on a team that sits at the intersection of distributed systems and machine learning and applying those techniques at massive scale to serve a real world customer need.

 

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships that it builds, the creativity it brings to the table, and the collaboration of being together. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our employees can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

 

What You’ll Do: 

  • Lead and develop an existing engineering team of 8; building trust, setting technical direction, and establishing a high bar for ownership and execution
  • Own the roadmap and execution for our key signal finding systems
  • Work closely with product management and applied scientists to build an effective detection system and the right evaluation mechanisms to ensure the quality of our signals
  • Build and operate both traditional machine learning and LLM based systems in production at scale
  • Drive the team's AI-native development practices, setting high standards for safety, validation, and increasing agent autonomy over time

Who You Are: 

  • Experienced engineering manager with a track record of shipping robust and scalable distributed systems with AI and/or ML components. Distributed systems experience is a must-have
  • Experience with Java, Python or Go, and experience working in a platform-focused team
  • Strong cross-team collaboration and stakeholder management skills
  • Comfortable making significant contributions to product strategy in an ambiguous environment rather than executing a pre-defined roadmap
  • Direct experience building and training ML models in production environments is a plus
  • Familiarity utilizing streaming technology (e.g. Flink, Kafka) is a plus

As a Fraud Operations Intern you will be responsible for reviewing fraud alerts, determining fraud or no-fraud and help identify emerging fraud trends through data analysis. 

This role is based in our Denver, CO office with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. 

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. 

What you’ll do

  • Review and investigate suspected fraudulent alerts — both proactive and reactive — using multiple internal and external tools
  • Use data analysis techniques, critical thinking, and pattern detection to identify emerging fraud trends and detection methodologies
  • Recognize and actively communicate emerging fraud trends and findings to relevant stakeholders
  • Document the rationale and determination for each alert and submit referrals to other Robinhood teams where necessary
  • Occasionally communicate with customers regarding information on their accounts related to an active fraud investigation

What you bring

  • Currently enrolled in a full-time, degree-seeking program in Business, Accounting, Criminal Justice, Psychology, or a related field with an expected graduation date of Winter 2027/Spring 2028
  • Interest in the end-to-end fraud investigation process and various fraud typologies, including Account Takeovers, Identity Theft, and Money Movement Fraud
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to independently make sound decisions on potentially fraudulent cases
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills with strong attention to detail
  • Experience collaborating with cross-functional teams, such as product, engineering, legal, compliance, or financial crimes

What we offer

  • Time away including company holidays, paid time off, and sick time

Datadog's Tel Aviv engineering site builds across some of our fastest-moving product areas — from Product Analytics, to Universal Service Monitoring, to Security Monitoring, to the Software Delivery tools that help engineers everywhere ship and operate software safely. It's a site with real engineering depth, and we're investing in the on-site senior leadership to match it.

We are looking for a Director of Engineering, based in Tel Aviv, to lead a multi-team engineering organization in one of these areas, and help shape the site as it grows. In this role, you will partner closely with product managers and with engineering leaders across Tel Aviv, Paris, and the US to shape the roadmap; grow and develop the team to match the business needs; raise the bar on engineering practices and craft; and play a central role in building the culture of a site we're investing in for the long term.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture — the relationships it builds, the creativity it brings to the table, and the collaboration of being together. This role is based in our Tel Aviv office, where being present on site is central to anchoring and growing the team.

What You'll Do:

  • Manage and grow a team of talented engineers, making sure they deliver high-quality, timely work and that they're happy, motivated, and developing in their careers
  • Hire and develop senior talent, engineers and managers alike, raising the seniority bar on site as we scale

  • Help shape the future of the Tel Aviv site and the broader engineering organization

Who You Are:

  • You are a product-building leader with real product sense, comfortable working hand in hand with product and design to decide what to build, not just how to build it
  • You came up through engineering and can earn the trust of senior engineers in a fast conversation; you favor breadth and adaptability, and you can ramp quickly into a technical domain you didn't start in
  • You integrate AI into how you lead and how your teams build, treating AI-first thinking as core engineering practice rather than a feature bolted onto the product
  • You have hired, grown, and developed engineering teams, creating long-term plans for people's growth and motivation
  • You have managed managers — you've hired, coached, and developed engineering managers, and led an organization with multiple layers of leadership beneath you

The Security Libraries team owns the customer-side integrations behind Datadog’s run-time security products — App & API Protection, Workload Protection, and Code Security — shipping and maintaining security capabilities across seven open-source language libraries (.NET, Java, Go, Node.js, Python, Ruby, PHP) and a set of HTTP proxy integrations (Envoy, NGINX, and HAProxy), running inside thousands of production clusters worldwide.

Fuse Energy is an energy startup on a mission to make energy abundant and affordable, fast. We combine first-principles thinking with cutting-edge technology to build a radically better energy system.
 We've raised over $200M from top-tier investors including Balderton, Lakestar, Accel, Creandum, Lowercarbon, Ribbit, 20VC, Hummingbird and Collaborative Fund, alongside strategic angels including Nico Rosberg and GPs behind Meta, Revolut, Spotify and Uber.
 We're building a fully integrated energy company: developing our own solar, batteries and other generation projects, building our own hardware, improving and developing grid infrastructure, trading power in real time, using AI across the business, and installing distributed energy in homes. By selling directly to consumers we cut out the middleman, lower costs and pass the savings on to our customers.
 The Electrical Engineering Lead owns all electrical engineering for Fuse’s EPC function, from design through testing, commissioning and energisation, across all of our infrastructure projects (Solar PV, BESS, Distribution Network, Wind, Gas-Peaker and Data Centres). You are the technical authority for HV and MV systems and lead the team that designs, builds, tests and energises them. You are also familiar with NERS, allowing Fuse to carry out contestable grid connection works as an Independent Connections Provider (ICP), so every system we deliver is safe, compliant and accepted by the DNO.

 About the role 
 We're looking for a Senior or Lead Security Engineer (Detection & Response) to build out the next generation of detection systems.
 You'll sit within the team responsible for security across our IT and cloud environment, spanning AWS, identity, endpoints, SaaS and data center infrastructure. You'll own security monitoring and detection end-to-end: anticipating how our systems could be compromised, ensuring we have the right telemetry to see it, and building the detections and response workflows to act on it.
 Think of it like SRE for security. We want someone who can answer questions like: Has this account been compromised? Is someone accessing AWS who shouldn't be? Has an attacker moved laterally through our network? How would we know? 
 You'll also lead investigations and incident response, automate repetitive security work, and work with IT and Engineering to fix the underlying problems you uncover.
 
 Responsibilities
 Own security monitoring and detection across AWS, identity, endpoints, SaaS, networks and data center environments
 Build and maintain the telemetry and logging pipelines needed to detect security incidents, and continuously test and improve detection coverage
 Lead security investigations and incident response from detection through containment, recovery and post-mortem
 Proactively hunt for threats and identify gaps in our visibility, controls and detection coverage
 Build automation to improve detection, investigation and response, making effective use of AI and emerging tools to improve efficiency and capabilities.
 Work closely with IT and Engineering to turn security findings into preventative controls and better system design
 Develop and test incident response playbooks and continuously improve our response capability
 Implement and enhance internal AI agents and security bots that assist with monitoring, investigations, reporting, and other security operation tasks.
 Requirements 
 Significant hands-on experience in detection engineering, security engineering, incident response, threat hunting or a similar technical role 
 Strong understanding of cloud environments, ideally AWS, and how to monitor them for unauthorised or suspicious activity
 Strong networking fundamentals and an understanding of how attackers move through networks and systems
 Strong understanding of attacker tradecraft and the ability to turn it into useful, high-signal detections
 Experience investigating real security incidents and taking ownership through to resolution
 Strong scripting or programming skills, ideally Python, and a habit of automating repetitive work
 Experience with security monitoring and response tooling such as SIEM, EDR, SOAR or equivalent
 Strong systems thinking and a natural instinct for asking “how would we know if this was compromised?”
 Comfortable working autonomously and closely with IT and Engineering teams
 Curious about emerging AI capabilities and proactive in experimenting with AI-assisted development, automation and security workflows.

 Detection-as-code, Sigma, Git-based detections and automated testing
 CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Defender or another EDR
 Network security monitoring, PCAP, NetFlow/sFlow or firewall telemetry
 Digital forensics, threat intelligence, purple teaming or security validation
 Data centre or colocation security, including OOB networks and BMC/IPMI
 Security automation, AI-assisted development or applying AI/LLMs to security engineering and operations.
 Energy, trading, fintech, critical infrastructure or other high-value-target environments

About Ramp 
 Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
 The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
 We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.
 The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
 If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.
 
 About the Role
 Ramp is hiring its first dedicated Physical Security Lead to build and run the program that protects our people, our leaders, our events, and our offices. Our footprint now spans a multi-floor New York headquarters, Ramp-managed offices, and a growing set of hubs across North America and Europe. Our leaders are increasingly visible on public stages.

 You'll own three areas in roughly equal measure: executive protection , event security , and office security (access control, cameras, guards, and building security). Your job is to turn a set of strong vendors and partner teams into one measurable, risk-based program.

 This is a high-ownership IC role on the Corporate Security team. It reports to the Director of IT & Corporate Security and is based at our NYC HQ. This is a physical security role; cybersecurity and information security are owned by other Ramp security teams. We aren't looking for a guard supervisor or a box-checker. We want someone who makes it safe for Ramp to move fast, host great events, and keep our leaders accessible.

 
 What You'll Do
 Build and run Ramp's executive protection program: 
 Protective risk assessments and residential security reviews.

 Domestic and international travel security.

 Advance work for high-visibility appearances.

 Selecting, standing up, and managing our executive protection provider.

 
 Turn threat intelligence into protective action. Partner with Detection & Response to move from online threat and exposure monitoring to threat assessments, personal-information exposure reduction, and clear escalation playbooks.

 Own security for internal and external events, from all-hands and offsites to conferences, customer events, and executive dinners:
 Risk-tiered intake and written security plans.

 Coordination with venues and vendors.

 On-site leadership for the highest-risk events.

 After-action reviews.

 
 Set Ramp's global physical security standards for access control, video surveillance, intercoms, visitor management, and alarm monitoring. Tier them for headquarters, Ramp-managed offices, and flexible or serviced hub spaces.

 Build security into every new office, move, and expansion: 
 Write the security design requirements and review drawings.

 Manage integrators through installation and acceptance testing.

 Partner with IT on network and identity integration.

 
 Manage the guard program and security vendors end to end: scope, post orders, SLAs and KPIs, budget, and quarterly business reviews. Own the security relationship with landlords and building management.

 Lead emergency preparedness and physical incident response: 
 Emergency notifications, evacuation and shelter-in-place plans, and drills.

 Liaison with local law enforcement.

 Workplace-violence prevention, in partnership with People and Legal.

 
 Run physical access governance with IT. Tie access to joiner/mover/leaver events, run regular access reviews, and keep audit-ready evidence for physical security controls.

 Measure and report program health to leadership. Use AI and automation to scale the program without scaling headcount.
 

 What You Need
 6+ years in corporate or physical security, including 3+ years owning a security program or major workstream at a multi-site company. Executing someone else's program doesn't count toward this.

 Hands-on depth in at least two of the three areas (executive protection, event security, physical security systems such as access control and cameras) and solid working knowledge of the third.

 Experience administering or deploying enterprise access control and video platforms (e.g., Avigilon Alta/Openpath, Verkada, Genetec, LenelS2), and partnering with IT on networking and SSO.

 A track record of managing security vendors (guard, protection, integrator, event staffing) through contracts, SLAs, budgets, and performance reviews.

 Strong risk judgment. You size controls to the actual threat, explain the tradeoffs, and lead with "here's how we do this safely" rather than "no."

 Excellent writing. You can produce a crisp SOP, an event security plan, and a one-page executive brief.

 Willingness to work from our NYC office 4 days a week, travel 10–15%, support occasional evening and weekend events, and serve as primary on-call for physical security incidents (with the Director as backup and guard and vendor partners as on-site first response).

 Real, day-to-day use of AI tools in your work.
 

 Nice-to-Haves
 ASIS CPP or PSP; formal executive protection training; first aid or Stop the Bleed certification.

 Experience at a high-growth tech, fintech, or financial services company with a high-profile founder or CEO.

 Experience writing security design standards for office buildouts and reading architectural or low-voltage drawings.

 Familiarity with physical and environmental control requirements in SOC 2, PCI DSS, or FedRAMP.

 A government protective, law enforcement, or military background, combined with corporate program ownership.

 An established network of protection, event security, and integrator vendors in NYC, SF, and internationally.
 

 Fair Warning
 This is a builder role. Parts of the program exist today (vendors, a responsibility matrix, some SOPs). You'll turn them into a system.

 You're an IC who directs vendors and partner teams, not a manager of a security staff. You'll need to influence Workplace, Events, IT, Executive Assistants, People, and Legal without formal authority.

 Security at Ramp enables the business. Events still happen, offices stay welcoming, and executives stay accessible. Your job is to make that safe.

 Evenings, weekends, and travel come with the territory, especially around major events.

description:
Developer Advocates at Datadog are engineers who share their expertise with technical practitioners, help customers tell their stories, and represent the perspectives of our community inside Datadog.

As a Manager II on the Advocacy team, you will lead our Community Advocacy functions. You will manage a team of Developer Advocates responsible for global programs such as Datadog Ambassadors, Champions, and User Groups, as well as opportunities for customer engineers to share their expertise through technical writing, public speaking, and other community contributions.


Across these interconnected programs, your team will enable customer engineers to contribute technical knowledge, lead communities, and turn their experiences into compelling content and conference talks for Datadog and third-party channels. This role combines people leadership, program strategy, technical judgment, and cross-functional influence to amplify authentic customer voices, deepen understanding of Datadog and its products, and foster a thriving community of practitioners.

 

What You’ll Do: 

  • Lead and develop a team of Developer Advocates, setting clear expectations, guiding priorities, coaching performance, supporting career growth, and fostering an inclusive, high-performing culture
  • Own the strategy, goals, and roadmap for Community Advocacy, translating broader Advocacy and company priorities into focused programs and measurable outcomes
  • Guide the continued development of our Ambassador, Champion, and User Group programs, creating clear contributor journeys, expectations, enablement, recognition, and opportunities for customer engineers to increase their impact
  • Build repeatable systems that enable customer engineers to contribute technical knowledge, create content, share best practices, and serve as trusted leaders within their communities
  • Develop a strong pipeline of customer stories by identifying compelling practitioners and helping them shape authentic, technically credible narratives
  • Oversee the support, co-development, and coaching of conference talks by customer engineers—from identifying an idea and developing an abstract through content review, rehearsal, and delivery—for Datadog events, including our flagship user conference, DASH, as well as third-party industry conferences
  • Establish measures of success for Community Advocacy, using qualitative and quantitative insights to evaluate program health, contributor engagement, content quality, audience impact, and customer outcomes
  • Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Marketing, Events, Customer Success, and regional teams to align priorities, identify opportunities, and scale customer participation across Datadog initiatives
  • Ensure insights from Ambassadors, Champions, User Group participants, speakers, and other community members are shared with the appropriate teams inside Datadog, strengthening the connection between our customers and our products
  • Balance strategic leadership with selective hands-on contribution, including coaching speakers, reviewing technical content, participating in community programs, and representing Datadog when appropriate

 

Who You Are: 

  • You are an experienced people manager who has led autonomous technical professionals, coached performance, developed talent, and translated complex goals into achievable plans
  • You have experience defining and delivering successful developer advocacy, developer relations, technical community, or a related functions
  • You have built or meaningfully contributed to programs that enable external practitioners to participate, contribute, create content, or lead communities at scale
  • You have experience helping technical practitioners develop and communicate their stories, including coaching conference speakers or co-developing technically credible talks and content
  • You are a former software developer, SRE, or other technical practitioner—or have equivalent technical depth—with the judgment needed to assess technical accuracy and coach effective technical narratives
  • You are a thoughtful cross-functional leader who can build alignment, make prioritization decisions, and influence partners across Product, Engineering, Marketing, Events, and customer-facing organizations
  • You use both data and community insight to evaluate program effectiveness, identify opportunities, and make decisions about where the team should invest
  • You understand how to build trust with technical communities and value authentic practitioner voices over purely promotional messaging
  • You are comfortable operating through ambiguity, establishing structure where needed, and evolving programs as Datadog’s products, customers, and technical audiences grow

 

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply. 

 

Benefits and Growth: 

  • New hire stock equity (RSUs) and employee stock purchase plan (ESPP)
  • Continuous professional development, product training, and career pathing
  • Intradepartmental mentor and buddy program for in-house networking
  • An inclusive company culture, ability to join our Community Guilds (Datadog employee resource groups)

Business Systems drives efficiency across Datadog through business process analysis, systems automation and integrations, AI agent and MCP development, and vendor/software review. The team is increasingly embedded in cross-functional initiatives across People, Finance, GTM, Legal, Recruiting, and Technical Solutions — translating ambiguous business problems into scoped, buildable solutions and owning delivery end-to-end.

 

This is not a generalist BSA role. Each Senior BSA will own a cluster of business functions end-to-end, acting as an internal product manager for their domain rather than processing inbound requests reactively. There are two openings, each covering a different domain:

People, Recruiting, Legal or Finance, GTM, Procurement

 

As the role evolves alongside AI, Senior BSAs leverage agentic tools for data aggregation and context gathering while remaining the critical human-in-the-loop layer — owning business context and product outlook, validating use cases, managing stakeholder relationships, and making the judgment calls agents can't.

 

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships that it builds, the creativity it brings to the table, and the collaboration of being together. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our employees can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.


What You’ll Do:

Many stakeholders don't know what they want or the cross-functional impact of what they're asking for — you surface both before engineering begins.

Datadog's Digital Experience Monitoring (DEM) group is one of the company's fastest-growing product areas, spanning Real User Monitoring (RUM), Product Analytics, Synthetic Monitoring, Feature Flags, and Datadog Studio, our newest AI-native observability surface. As Director, you will own engineering for one or more of these product areas, with scope shaped by your background and interests, and you will manage 50-60 engineers through a team of Engineering Managers. You'll partner with Senior Directors and product leadership to shape the roadmap, not just execute against it, and you'll help drive AI adoption across engineering tooling, workflows, and product features. This role is based in Paris, one of Datadog's most established engineering hubs, with a clear growth path to Senior Director for the right candidate.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships that it builds, the creativity it brings to the table, and the collaboration of being together. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our employees can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

 

What You'll Do:

  • Own engineering for one or more DEM product areas with scope calibrated to your background and strengths
  • Manage 50-60 engineers through a layer of Engineering Managers; this is a manager-of-managers role
  • Shape the roadmap alongside product leadership rather than simply executing against it — push back on, iterate on, and help author the strategy for your area
  • Drive AI adoption across the engineering org, from tooling and workflows to product features and team practices
  • Navigate cross-team dependencies across DEM, APM, Core Platform, AI Platform, and Data Science
  • Build and retain engineering talent in Paris, mentor Engineering Managers toward Director readiness, and participate in the on-call rotation

 

Who You Are:

  • You have directly managed Engineering Managers, not just individual contributors — this is a non-negotiable requirement for the role
  • You integrate AI deeply into how you lead and how your teams build, treating AI-first thinking as core engineering practice rather than a feature bolted onto the product
  • You have a track record of shaping product decisions, not just executing against a spec
  • You've worked with large-scale, event-driven or data-intensive backend systems — ingestion pipelines, high-throughput APIs, or time-series/event data at scale

job_title: Staff Product Manager - Self Improving Software
description:
As a Staff Product Manager on Datadog's Self-Improving Products team, you will take a new product family from zero to one: a closed loop that watches how a customer's software and its users behave, ranks what is worth changing, proposes the change, proves whether it worked, and carries the result into the next cycle. Datadog already holds every piece this product needs, including behavioral data from Product Analytics and Session Replay, full-stack telemetry from APM, Log Management, Error Tracking, and Continuous Profiler, rollout control through Feature Flags and Experimentation, and a coding agent in Bits AI Dev Agent that opens verified pull requests from production signal. You will own assembling these into one product where the loop closes on its own. This is founding work with no precedent inside Datadog, and an opportunity to grow as a product leader by shaping the scope, recruiting the first design partners, and setting the quality bar for an AI-native product from the ground up.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships that it builds, the creativity it brings to the table, and the collaboration of being together. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our employees can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

 

What You'll Do:

  • Set product direction for a new product family by defining the problems and desired outcomes, and partnering with engineering to find the narrowest first slice that proves the loop closes and delivers value to customers in phases.
  • Own the product decisions at every stage of the loop: what signal is trustworthy enough to trigger an automated change, which opportunities rank highest and with what confidence, what a proposed change must contain before a customer merges it, what evidence proves it worked, and what the system remembers for the next cycle.
  • Define the autonomy ladder and its limits, from suggestion, to draft, to auto-opened pull request, to auto-rollout, along with the controls, defaults, and audit trail customers need to rely on it. Some rungs stay off by design, and you own those decisions.
  • Set the quality bar for a product that is non-deterministic: build the evaluation sets with engineering, decide what "good enough to ship" means, and hold that bar when it moves a date.
  • Recruit the first design partners yourself, sit in their triage rotations, turn what you learn there into the roadmap, and keep talking to them after launch.
  • Develop and defend the sizing, impact, and cost-to-serve analysis that engineering leadership and pricing partners need to make resourcing calls, partnering with engineering on the unit economics of inference and the data platform and bringing that cost profile into packaging, metering, and pricing before launch rather than after.
  • Deliver concise written and verbal communication to executive, engineering, and customer audiences, clarifying complex architecture, quality trade-offs, and go-to-market, including where agentic observability, product analytics, and experimentation are heading and how that shapes the product.

 

Who You Are:

  • You have shipped AI products, not prototypes: you have taken at least one AI-native product to production customers, and you can describe what it got wrong in the field and what you changed in response.
  • You treat evaluation as product work: you have built or commissioned evaluation sets, set the bar for shipping a model or prompt change, and held that bar under schedule pressure.
  • You are fluent in agent failure modes and design for non-determinism deliberately, accounting for confidence, reversibility, blast radius, review surfaces, and graceful failure.
  • You have a zero-to-one track record: you have started something with no roadmap and no team and got it to customers who renewed, you narrow ruthlessly, and you have ended a direction you championed and can explain why.
  • You read across staff engineers, consuming product teams, sales and FinOps, marketing, and finance, and turn diffuse signals into a defensible product position.
  • You are collaborative, opinionated, and comfortable with ambiguity: you build trust quickly with engineers, PM peers, designers, and commercial partners, you bring strong product opinions and adapt as new evidence emerges, and you write the document that gives diffuse work a shape.
  • You have 8+ years of Product Management experience, or a track record showing Staff-level capabilities in related software roles. We weigh shipped AI products and zero-to-one evidence more heavily than years.
  • You have a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent experience (preferred).

The Incident and Escalation Management team (IEM) is part of Datadog's Global Support Engineering (GSE) organization. IEM exists to continuously improve Datadog's overall customer experience during incidents and other critical moments. We're looking for experts with a background in incident management and escalation handling to provide fast incident response, clear ownership, and calm, confident communication for our global customer base.

In this individual contributor role, you will play a key part in customer communication, technical engagement, and incident management for our global customers. You will also implement processes and automations, use the same incident and case management tools we build for our customers, and help shape how they evolve.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture — the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What you'll do:

  • Lead the response to our most complex, ambiguous, and high-impact incidents and escalations from start to finish. Set the response strategy, drive cross-functional coordination, and maintain clear ownership through resolution.
  • Navigate competing priorities across multiple critical customer situations, independently assessing business and technical impact and determining the appropriate response and escalation strategy.
  • Represent IEM to regional Support, Sales, and Engineering leadership, building the standing and relationships that let you drive a response when a situation moves faster than process allows.
  • Lead communications during highly sensitive, public, or large-scale incidents, adapting communication strategies for customers, internal leadership, and other stakeholders.
  • Act as a trusted incident and escalation partner across Support, Engineering, Product, and other teams, influencing decisions and driving alignment when ownership or the path to resolution is unclear.
  • Lead high-impact, cross-functional projects that improve how Datadog manages incidents and escalations at scale, identifying systemic gaps and translating them into sustainable operational improvements.
  • Establish and evolve incident and escalation best practices, documentation, runbooks, and training, raising the quality and consistency of response across the organization.
  • Mentor and develop other IEMs or GSEs members, provide guidance during complex situations, contribute to interviewing and hiring, and help raise the operational bar for the team.
  • Design and champion proactive monitoring and detection strategies that surface customer-impacting risks earlier and enable teams to act before issues escalate.
  • Identify systemic patterns across incidents, escalations, customer infrastructure, and product behavior, and influence Engineering and Product partners to address root causes and reduce recurrence.

Who you are:

  • 8+ years of related professional experience, including at least 4 years of experience in incident management and customer escalations, with demonstrable ownership of major, high-impact incidents and business-critical customer escalations in SaaS, cloud, observability, or similarly complex software environments
  • Significant experience in a hands-on technical role at a software or cloud company, such as Support Engineering, Site Reliability Engineering, Solutions Architecture, or a similar technical function

  • Experience operating as the sole or most senior incident responder in a region or timezone — making consequential decisions without an in-hours escalation path, and working effectively with customers and internal teams across different cultures and working norms.

job_title: Investment Analyst MBA Intern, Robinhood Ventures (Summer 2027)
description:
Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. 

Robinhood Ventures’ vision is to build a new kind of venture capital platform, making the best private companies in the world accessible to retail investors everywhere in service of Robinhood's broader mission to democratize finance for all. Through our publicly traded funds in Robinhood Ventures Fund I and Robinhood Ventures Fund II we’ve already invested in companies like OpenAI, Databricks, Ramp, and more - and we’re just getting started.

As an Investment Intern in Robinhood Ventures you will be a core part of our lean team. You will research, evaluate, and support investments across the Robinhood Ventures platform, with a focus on late-stage investments.  

This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA office with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. 

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. 

What you’ll do

  • Research and sourcing - You’ll research markets and sectors that you believe we should be paying attention to, and then identify the key companies in them that Robinhood Ventures needs to meet. 
  • Investment evaluation - You’ll be a key part of the deal team for investments we evaluate. You’ll own core diligence workstreams like the financial model, competitive analysis, and help shape investment theses. 
  • Platform building - You’ll work with teams across Product, Operations, Marketing, Legal, and more to help build experiences in the Robinhood app to further differentiate Robinhood Ventures for both retail investors and portfolio companies. 

What you bring

  • Currently enrolled in a full-time MBA program 
  • Prior experience in investment banking, private equity, or finance at a high-growth company, with fluency in financial modeling, valuation analysis, and market research; late-stage investing or venture capital experience is a plus
  • Intellectual curiosity and a demonstrated interest in emerging technologies and the private companies driving them — you proactively form opinions on key trends and companies
  • An existing network in the startup ecosystem, or the drive to build one, that can help Robinhood Ventures identify and connect with promising companies
  • Proven ability to work independently in lean, high-output environments, with experience collaborating across cross-functional teams

What we offer

  • Market competitive compensation structure
  • Quarterly lifestyle wallet for personal wellness, learning and development, and more
  • Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not
  • Time away including company holidays, paid time off, and sick time
  • Lively office environment with catered meals, fully stocked kitchens, and geo-specific commuter benefits

The Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) team analyzes company financial data (revenue, customers, headcount, expenses, etc.) in order to support the business's growth and success. Within FP&A, the R&D Finance team enables the financial strategy behind Datadog's Engineering and Product organizations. This role sits specifically within hosting cost and cloud margin reporting, reporting directly to the FP&A Manager who owns hosting cost analysis, cloud gross margin modeling, and forecasting.

The Opportunity:

As the first dedicated analyst hire supporting Datadog's hosting cost and cloud margin function, you will own key components of the recurring reporting, close, and forecasting processes that provide visibility into one of Datadog’s largest and most strategically important cost areas. You’ll partner closely with Engineering, FinOps, Capacity Planning, and Vendor Management through a financial lens, with a clear growth path into broader cloud finance and FinOps scope as you build fluency in the space.

What You'll Do:

  • Partner with FP&A leadership to manage recurring forecast updates, review cycles, and board-ready materials.
  • Help manage portions of the recurring hosting close, including savings reporting, cost allocation, and key operational drivers.
  • Assist in maintaining the hosting forecast models across Excel and Pigment.
  • Participate in recurring review cadences with FinOps and Engineering partners to align on capacity planning, savings plan coverage, and cost allocation decisions.
  • Partner with Controllership on accounting support for monthly hosting close files.
  • Work on ad hoc projects and process improvements, including identifying opportunities to automate recurring, manual steps in the close process.
  • Become proficient with financial planning, cost monitoring, and BI tools, including Pigment, Snowflake, Metabase, and Datadog's own Cloud Cost Management (CCM) product.

Who You Are:

  • 2+ years of professional experience in FP&A, Strategic Finance, Accounting, Data Analytics, or a Cloud Finance/FinOps-adjacent role.
  • Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, business, or economics
  • Strong Excel skills, including comfort working within large, formula-driven models.
  • High attention to detail and reliability on recurring, deadline-driven close work
  • Clear, concise communicator who can work independently once ramped, with a humble mindset and 'can-do' attitude

Bonus Points:

  • Exposure to SQL, not required on day one, but a skill you're motivated to build
  • Exposure to cloud commitment-based pricing (savings plans, committed use discounts, reserved capacity) and how they translate into gross margin
  • Interest in cloud unit economics: cost per unit of usage, capacity utilization, vendor cost negotiations 
  • Experience with or interest in Pigment or similar FP&A planning tools
  • Interest in process automation as a growth area within the role
  • Understanding of a consumption-based software business model
  • Hands-on experience with BI/reporting tools such as Tableau or Metabase

  • Delivering an outstanding customer experience for customers through phone, email, and chat channels
  • Driving continuous improvement to delight customers by acting as the voice of the customer by identifying and communicating better ways to serve our customers
  • Growing your financial services expertise as you develop deep subject mastery of complex financial concepts like equities trading, margin, and options trading

  • Active FINRA Series 7 and 63 Licenses with an ability to quickly put your brokerage knowledge into action
  • Excellent customer service, written and verbal communication skills with a passion to support customers
  • Effectiveness and willingness to adapt to CX experience delivery through phone and written channels
  • Ability to quickly defuse customer anxiety through exceptional customer service skills
  • Self-starter and ambitious learner who is comfortable with ambiguity and fast paced environment
  • Able to exercise independent thought and judgment, adapt to new tasks, and the ability to prioritize tasks in a multi-task environment
  • Schedule flexibility as we evolve to meet the growing demands of our customers (initial and/or future shift assignment may include evenings and weekend hours)

What we offer

  • Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career
  • Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching
  • Top Tier benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents
  • Access to the Robinhood Employee Fund that gives eligible US employees the opportunity to invest in a private employee fund that provides exposure to Robinhood Ventures funds.
  • Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not. 
  • Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more
  • Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits
  • Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more!
  • Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces.

description:
The internet is vast, containing trillions of URLs. Perplexity’s crawling and storage system is complex and has multiple stages (URL discovery, crawling, parsing, indexing). Each stage offers many opportunities for improvement and room for intricate bugs. You’ll work at the intersection of data analysis and engineering — designing metrics, building data pipelines, and improving the quality of our search and answer systems.
 
 Responsibilities 
 Find and diagnose quality issues in our crawling pipeline

 Train small models that optimize particular aspects of the pipeline (e.g. parsing quality)

 Build datasets for model training, including LLM-as-a-judge labeling pipelines

 Improve page selection algorithms for indexing

 Design and analyze experiments to validate improvements

 Qualifications 
 4+ years of experience as a data analyst, ML engineer, or in a related role

 Strong coding skills: you should be able to write production-grade code at the level of a mid-level backend engineer

 Experience designing metrics from scratch

 Experience training ML models that shipped to production with measurable metric improvements

 Nice to have 
 Direct experience working on web crawling or indexing pipelines

About Ramp 
 Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
 The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
 We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.
 The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
 If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.
 
 About the Role 
 You will serve as a front-line manager for a team of Enterprise Sales Development Representatives (SDRs) responsible for outbound prospecting and pipeline generation across Ramp’s largest and most strategic accounts.
 As Ramp expands its upmarket presence, you will help build and evolve the Enterprise go-to-market motion from the ground up. You will lead and develop high-performing SDRs who manage named books of business and navigate complex, multi-threaded enterprise sales cycles.
 Key responsibilities include coaching and developing SDRs, setting team strategy, and partnering closely with Sales, Marketing, Product, and executive leadership to drive enterprise pipeline and business outcomes. As a member of the Sales Leadership team, you will play a critical role in shaping, scaling, and refining Ramp’s Enterprise growth strategy.

 Build and scale the Enterprise SDR function, including team structure, playbooks, and processes for a named-account motion.

description:

You will advance reinforcement learning, simulated environments, synthetic data generation, and evaluation methods for agents operating across complex real-world systems. You will set the technical direction for ambitious research programs, raise the technical bar for the researchers and research engineers around you, and collaborate with Datadog's product and engineering teams to translate research advances into products.

  • Drive research in agent post-training and reinforcement learning, shaping the technical direction of ambitious research programs grounded in observability and security
  • Own research problems end to end, from framing the question through experimentation, model development, and evaluation

  • Build simulated environments, synthetic data generation approaches, and evaluation frameworks that enable scalable agent training and rigorous measurement
  • Raise the technical bar across the team by reviewing research directions, mentoring researchers and research engineers, and setting standards for experimental rigor
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams across Research, Product, and Engineering to translate advances in autonomous agents into scalable Datadog capabilities

location_display: New York, New York, USA; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA
description:
As a Staff Research Scientist within Datadog AI Research (DAIR), you will drive research in foundation models and world models as a hands-on individual contributor. You will advance large-scale pre-training and multimodal learning across the diverse signals generated by distributed systems, including metrics, traces, logs, topology, and events. You will set the technical direction for ambitious research programs, raise the technical bar for the researchers and research engineers around you, and collaborate with Datadog's product and engineering teams to translate research advances into products. 

 

What You'll Do:

  • Drive research in foundation models, world models, and multimodal learning, shaping the technical direction of ambitious research programs grounded in observability
  • Own research problems end to end, from framing the question through experimentation, model development, and evaluation
  • Train large-scale multimodal models on diverse telemetry data, including metrics, logs, traces, topology, events, and other non-text modalities
  • Advance approaches to pre-training, representation learning, world modeling, scaling, and evaluation for models that learn the dynamics of complex distributed systems
  • Raise the technical bar across the team by reviewing research directions, mentoring researchers and research engineers, and setting standards for experimental rigor
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams across Research, Product, and Engineering to translate research advances into scalable Datadog capabilities
  • Contribute to research publications, present at top-tier conferences such as NeurIPS, ICLR, and ICML, and help open-source key model artifacts and benchmarks

 

Who You Are:

  • You hold a PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field, or have equivalent experience, with deep expertise in areas such as foundation models, world models, multimodal learning, or generative modeling
  • You have driven technically ambitious research at meaningful scale as an individual contributor, whether in an industry research lab, startup, academic environment, or another research setting
  • You have extensive hands-on experience designing, training, and evaluating large-scale deep learning models (such as large language models), with experience in multimodal or non-text data considered a strong plus
  • You have a track record of research impact through influential publications, significant model or system contributions, widely used research artifacts, or equivalent technical achievements
  • You set technical direction through influence rather than authority, and you have mentored other researchers or engineers and elevated the quality of work around you
  • You want to stay deeply hands-on in research for the long term, and you can communicate complex research findings effectively across technical and non-technical audiences

You will own the enterprise billing lifecycle, translating complex commercial agreements into accurate, timely invoices and building the processes and controls that support our growth.
 This is a hands-on role working closely with Deal Desk, Enterprise Sales, Legal, and Customer Success. The ideal candidate combines strong billing and systems expertise with sound judgement, a customer-focused approach, and the ability to bring structure to a fast-moving environment.
 
 Responsibilities 
 Enterprise and reseller billing: Own enterprise billing operations from customer and subscription setup through recurring invoicing, renewals, amendments, and cancellations, ensuring accurate and timely billing in accordance with executed agreements.

 Contract review: Partner with Enterprise Sales and Deal Desk to review nonstandard billing terms before contracts are signed, assess operational feasibility, and route exceptions for approval.

 Billing inquiries and disputes: Serve as the primary point of contact for enterprise billing questions from customers and internal teams. Investigate discrepancies, coordinate approved credits and rebills, and address underlying causes to prevent recurring issues.

 Reconciliations and close support: Reconcile contract, subscription, and usage data to billing output and investigate any billing discrepancies. Support month-end close and audits through billing completeness checks, reconciliations, and supporting documentation.

 Integration management: Identifying and resolving any billing system integration failures.

 Customer Success and renewal support: Partner with Customer Success, Enterprise Sales, and Deal Desk on renewals, expansions, and changes to customer commitments. Prepare seat, usage, and billing analyses; calculate renewal credits and true-ups; and translate approved agreements into accurate subscription, credit, and invoice updates. Coordinate the resolution of billing issues that could delay renewals or disrupt the customer experience.

 Requirements 
 Bachelor’s degree or higher in Accounting or Finance.

 7+ years of experience in billing operations, order management, order-to-cash, revenue operations, or a related finance function, including hands-on ownership of enterprise SaaS or subscription billing.

 Billing expertise: Demonstrated ability to interpret complex customer agreements and translate them into accurate billing schedules, invoices, and adjustments, including subscription and usage-based arrangements.

 Systems proficiency: Hands-on experience with NetSuite, Salesforce, tax engines, and subscription or usage-based billing platforms, with the ability to investigate issues across connected systems.

 Accounting fundamentals: Working knowledge of accounts receivable, deferred revenue, and revenue-recognition concepts, including ASC 606.

 Resourcefulness, detail-oriented and a motivation for solving problems and finding solutions.

 Excellent communication skills, as frequent interaction with both internal and external stakeholders will be required.

 Ability to multi-task and prioritize effectively in a fast-paced environment.

description:
Perplexity is seeking an experienced Machine Learning Engineer to advance how AI systems search, reason, and work together to solve complex problems. Our work spans search and retrieval, LLM post-training, multi-agent training, and the harnesses that make these systems effective.
 We control the full stack: the models, the agent harnesses, and the search infrastructure underneath. That gives us the freedom to develop new approaches across all three training models to use search more effectively, designing tools and execution environments around learned behavior, and improving retrieval to support how agents actually work. 
 
 Responsibilities 
 Push search and agent quality forward through improvements to models, training data, tools, and system design.

 Develop LLM post-training methods, including reinforcement learning, to improve reasoning, search, tool use, and task completion.

 Train and evaluate multi-agent systems, exploring how agents divide work, share information, and coordinate effectively.

 Design and build agent harnesses around the tools, context management, execution environments, and orchestration that support reliable work over many steps.

 Improve retrieval and ranking models and the search interfaces agents use to find and assess information.

 Build datasets, reward signals, and evaluations that expose meaningful failures and guide improvements.

 Own experiments end to end, from a clear hypothesis to scalable training, deployment, and measurable gains in quality, latency, and cost.

 Collaborate with AI, Search, Infrastructure, Data, and Product teams to bring new capabilities into production.
 

 Qualifications 
 A strong track record of building and shipping ML systems, with deep experience in one or more of LLM post-training, reinforcement learning, search and retrieval, or agent systems.

 Strong software engineering skills and the ability to work across model training, experimentation infrastructure, and production systems.

 Experience designing rigorous evaluations, diagnosing failures, and translating experimental results into practical improvements.

 Comfort with open-ended problems that require both research judgment and hands-on engineering.

 A strong sense of ownership, curiosity, and the drive to carry an idea through to a working system.
 

 Nice to have 
 Experience with training models to use tools or complete tasks over many steps.

 Multi-agent training, coordination, or evaluation.

 Building agent harnesses, distributed training systems, or scalable inference infrastructure.

 Large-scale retrieval, ranking, or recommendation systems.

job_title: Senior Staff Product Designer, Design Lab
description:
Datadog is entering a new chapter in how our product looks, feels, and operates. Our Design Lab is defining a new visual direction for the platform, and we’re looking for a Senior Staff Visual Product Designer to help turn that direction into a coherent product experience.

Datadog is dense, technical, and used by people working through complex problems—often under real pressure. The challenge is not simply applying a new aesthetic. It is rethinking hierarchy, layout, navigation, interaction, and product patterns so the experience becomes clearer, more cohesive, and more expressive without losing the power our users rely on.

This is a hands-on product design leadership role for someone who combines strong visual judgment with deep product and systems thinking. You’ll work alongside visual designers, motion designers, product designers, Design Systems, and Engineering to ensure the new direction changes how Datadog works—not just how it looks.

 

What You'll Do

  • Co-develop Datadog’s next visual direction by applying and stress-testing it across representative product journeys.
  • Translate visual principles into concrete decisions about hierarchy, layout, navigation, information architecture, interaction, and behavior.
  • Use visual language to clarify complex, data-dense experiences — hierarchy, density, and attention.
  • Hold the visual quality bar across work you don't own, and align teams around it.
  • Prototype, test, and refine new patterns before they become systemized.
  • Partner deeply with Product Design, Design Systems, and engineering to turn successful concepts into durable system guidance and implementation.
  • Create clear artifacts, pilots, and narratives that help teams adopt the direction and raise the product quality bar.
  • Influence stakeholders across design, engineering, product, and executive partners.

You will report directly to the Design Director and work as part of a small, focused team defining the future state before it scales across hundreds of designers and engineers.

Who You Are

  • You have 12+ years of experience in product and/or visual design.
  • Your craft is elevated, and you can execute it yourself at a high bar.
