About the Team:

Netlify’s Data team helps the company understand and improve the full product-led growth journey, from activation and engagement through conversion, retention, and monetization. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, and Growth to uncover opportunities, evaluate investments, and understand what drives customer and business outcomes.

We’re hiring a Senior Staff Data Scientist to deepen how data shapes our product and growth strategy. You’ll develop an end-to-end understanding of the PLG journey, proactively identify opportunities, and turn complex data into hypotheses, experiments, and recommendations that influence where we invest and what we build. This is a highly autonomous role for someone who can move from identifying an important question to shaping the approach, defining success, and driving toward an answer.

What You'll Do:

  • Own the analytical understanding of Netlify’s PLG performance across activation, engagement, conversion, monetization, and retention, identifying opportunities before they become requests
  • Partner with Product and Engineering leadership to turn behavioral insights into product bets, defining what to test, how to measure it, and what the results mean
  • Lead experimentation from hypothesis through decision, including study design, methodology, success metrics, guardrails, analysis, and recommendations
  • Apply statistical rigor where it matters while recognizing when there is enough signal to make a decision and move forward, and help teams develop that same judgment
  • Build scalable analytical systems like semantic models, trusted metrics, proactive monitoring, and AI-powered agents  that surface opportunities without waiting to be asked
  • Use AI to investigate faster, automate recurring analytical work, and test more hypotheses without sacrificing the judgment that makes the output useful
  • Identify gaps in measurement, event instrumentation, and metric definitions, and partner with Data and Product Engineering to close them
  • Serve as a trusted analytical partner to PLG leadership, using evidence and product judgment to influence investment decisions and roadmap priorities
  • Influence product strategy through evidence, product instincts, and a clear point of view, without relying on formal authority to do it

What You'll Bring:

  • 8+ years of experience in product analytics, growth analytics, or data science, with a track record of high ownership and measurable impact on PLG or consumer product outcomes
  • Deep understanding of product and growth dynamics across activation, engagement, conversion, monetization, and retention
  • Demonstrated ability to turn behavioral data into product hypotheses and carry them from insight through experimentation and measured outcomes
  • Deep experimentation expertise: study design, statistical reasoning, causal inference, and the judgment to know when an experiment has told you what you need to know
  • Experience building analytical systems such as metrics layers, monitoring frameworks, or semantic models that teams can rely on over time
  • An AI-native approach to analysis: you use AI tools actively to accelerate investigation, automate repetitive work, and surface patterns faster
  • A track record of influencing senior stakeholders and product direction through analytical reasoning, clear recommendations, and sound judgment
  • Comfort operating with significant autonomy in ambiguous problem spaces, including determining which questions are most important to answer
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in distributed environments, with the ability to make complex findings clear and recommendations actionable

This Role is a Great Fit If:

  • You're energized by finding the opportunity before anyone thought to ask - proactive discovery is how you naturally work, not a mode you shift into
  • You think like a product person who happens to be exceptionally rigorous with data, not a data person who occasionally weighs in on product
  •  You thrive when the problem isn't handed to you - you'd rather define the question worth asking than answer the one that landed in your queue
  • You get excited about building systems that keep working after you've moved on to the next problem
  • You're comfortable making a call with imperfect information and can articulate clearly why you made it
  • You enjoy being a thought partner to senior leaders - shaping how they think about investment and opportunity, not just supporting decisions already made
  • You work well in a remote-first, async environment where written clarity and self-direction matter more than proximity
  • You're drawn to roles where the measure of success is outcomes, decisions made, bets tested, metrics moved, not volume of output produced

Applying

Not sure you meet 100% of our qualifications? Please apply anyway!

When applying please include: 

A resume or short listing of your job history & skills (link to a LinkedIn profile would be fine). We appreciate a cover letter explaining why you would enjoy working in this role at Netlify to get to know you a bit better, though this is not required and will not impact your application. Our mission is to “build a better web” and that cannot be done without a diversity of skill sets, backgrounds and thoughts. 

Of everything we've ever built at Netlify, we are most proud of our team. Netlify is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are devoted to building a team of people with diverse backgrounds and lifestyles. Driving equality empowers our team, enables us to innovate, and helps us maintain a more inclusive environment. We don’t discriminate against employees or applicants based on gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, age, race, military/veteran status, citizenship, pregnancy status, or any other differences. If we can do anything to provide a better interview, i.e. accommodate a disability, then please let us know by emailing accommodations@netlify.com. 

 

About Netlify

Netlify is the most popular way to build, deploy, and scale modern web applications, empowering everyone from fast moving solo developers to enterprise teams. Millions of developers and organizations rely on Netlify as their platform of choice for composing web applications that are production ready, performant, and flexible. Now, as we embrace the next era of software development, we are embedding the same fluid, intuitive experience into the Agent Experience (AX), making it just as simple for intelligent agents to understand, interact with, and act on our platform as it is for developers. Whether your user is human or machine, Netlify ensures the path from idea to URL is seamless, fast, and deeply reliable.

We are a Series D company that has raised over $200M from investors such as Andreessen Horowitz, Kleiner Perkins, EQT, Bessemer, BOND, and Menlo Ventures. As a fully distributed company, we aim to create a company culture where the best idea can come from anywhere and strive to be thoughtful, compassionate, and collaborative in our work. If this sounds like something you’d like to be part of, we’re excited to connect with you!

At Netlify, we are committed to a compensation philosophy that prioritizes fairness and equity, positions our employee compensation competitively in the market, recognizes and rewards performance, and takes a comprehensive approach to our rewards package. We anchor our compensation philosophy on a market-based approach, therefore salary ranges may differ depending on the labor cost in a particular location. The salary provided is in addition to robust benefits and participation in Netlify’s equity plan. Perplexity is AI for people who expect more. On the data team, that means building the systems that make our data reliable, understandable, and usable by both humans and AI.
 We're looking for an analytics engineer or data engineer who wants to build the foundation for an AI-native data organization. You'll design core data models, pipelines, semantic layers, data quality systems, governance practices, and warehouse workflows that power the entire company: helping teams make strategic decisions, operate the business, and move faster with trusted data. You'll also make sure those systems are secure, privacy-aware, and legible to AI agents, data scientists, and the rest of the company.
 This role is for someone who can operate at the boundary of analytics engineering, data engineering, data governance, and internal product. You care about dimensional modeling, dbt standards, cost-aware warehouse design, access controls, privacy, and the details that make data trustworthy. You also believe AI should make the data stack faster, easier to maintain, and more accessible across the company without weakening security or governance.
 
 What You'll Do 
 Build the core data foundation - design and maintain high-quality data models, marts, and pipelines that make analysis fast, reliable, and reusable.

 Manage the data warehouse - help own warehouse architecture, environments, permissions, performance, cost, data lifecycle, and operational hygiene so the platform scales cleanly.

 Make the warehouse AI-readable - own the documentation, semantic context, metadata, lineage, and retrieval patterns that AI systems depend on to understand and query Perplexity's data correctly.

 Own data modeling standards - define and champion dbt patterns, dimensional modeling practices, naming conventions, tests, and review processes.

 Lead data governance practices - define standards for access, ownership, lineage, documentation, retention, quality, and sensitive data handling across the analytical warehouse.

 Build with security and privacy in mind - partner with engineering, security, legal, and finance where needed to ensure data access, sharing, and AI-enabled workflows are appropriate and controlled.

 Automate data quality and maintenance - build AI-assisted workflows that detect issues, explain root causes, suggest fixes, generate tests, and reduce manual firefighting.

 Improve data team productivity - automate repetitive workflows, improve tooling, streamline development, and make it easier for data scientists and stakeholders to answer questions.

 Partner across the company - work closely with data scientists, engineering, product, finance, and GTM teams to translate analytical needs into durable data systems.

 Shape tooling decisions - evaluate build-versus-buy tradeoffs, manage vendor relationships when needed, and choose tools that scale with the team.

 What We're Looking For 
 6+ years of experience as an analytics engineer, data engineer, data scientist, or closely related role.

 Deep SQL expertise - you can reason about correctness, performance, joins, grain, and edge cases in complex warehouse queries.

 Strong data modeling experience - you've worked hands-on with dbt (or a similar transformation framework) in production, and you understand dimensional modeling, data contracts, testing, and how analytical schemas should evolve.

 Pipeline ownership - you've built, maintained, debugged, and improved production data pipelines.

 Warehouse management experience - you've worked with warehouse administration, access patterns, permissions, performance tuning, cost management, or operational ownership.

 Governance mindset - you think clearly about data ownership, access controls, privacy, retention, lineage, auditability, and the risks of making data too easy to access.

 AI-native working style - you already use AI to speed up development, documentation, QA, exploration, and repetitive workflow automation.

 Stakeholder fluency - you know how to turn messy analytical requirements into trusted models, metrics, and reusable data assets.

 Autonomy and execution - you can take projects from ambiguous problem to production-quality system with minimal oversight.

 Operational judgment - you care about reliability, governance, security, cost, and long-term maintainability.

 Bonus 
 Snowflake administration, optimization, cost management, or warehouse performance tuning.

 Experience with RBAC, PII handling, data classification, retention policies, audit workflows, or privacy/security reviews.

 Experience with Databricks or other modern data infrastructure.

 Experience building semantic layers, metrics layers, metadata systems, or data catalogs.

 Python experience for data tooling, automation, orchestration, or quality checks.

 Previous experience as an early analytics engineer or data engineer at a high-growth startup.

 Why This Role 
 Own the foundation - your work will determine how fast and confidently the company can use data.

 Build for humans and AI - the next generation of data infrastructure needs to be understandable by agents as well as analysts.

 High leverage - better models, pipelines, and tools multiply every data scientist and every stakeholder who depends on data.

 Small team, broad scope - you'll have room to define standards, choose tools, and ship systems that become company-wide defaults.

About Ramp 
 Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
 The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
 We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.
 The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
 If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.
 
 About the Role 
 Buying something for a business should not require finance teams to piece together requests, purchase orders, receipts, and invoices across disconnected systems. Ramp is building a procurement experience that helps employees get what they need, gives finance teams control over commitments, and helps businesses pay for what they actually received.
 As a Product Manager for Ramp’s Procurement offering, you will own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for Ramp’s core procurement capabilities, including sourcing, requisition, approval workflows, renewals, purchase orders, receiving, two- and three-way matching, and inventory management. You will work with Engineering, Design, and Data to turn complex purchasing and accounting requirements into products that are easy to start using and reliable as customers grow.
 AI creates an opportunity to rethink this work: build agentic buying experiences for employees, automate work for approvers and stakeholders, and businesses make better purchasing decisions. You will decide where automation can take work off a customer’s plate, where a direct workflow is faster, and where a person needs to review or approve an action. Success means customers get value quickly, adopt the product in their everyday work, and spend less time chasing information and correcting errors.
 This role requires working in person at our NYC or SF office at least two days per week. 
 Please note that this role requires in-person presence at our NYC or SF office at least 2 days/week. 
 
 What You’ll Do 
 Own the strategy and roadmap for Ramp’s Procurement pod. Make clear choices about which customer problems to solve, how the capabilities fit together, and what to build next.

 Build connected workflows across sourcing, requisition, approvals, renewals, purchase orders, receiving, invoice matching, and inventory management. Partner with Bill Pay, Accounting, and platform teams so purchasing records and decisions carry through to payment and customers’ ERP systems.

 Spend time with finance teams, procurement leaders, purchasing operators, and employees. Turn observed friction into simpler experiences for first-time customers and powerful workflows for complex organizations.

 Build AI-powered experiences that complete useful work, such as finding new vendors, managing a renewal, drafting a request from a contract, or helping resolve a receipt and invoice discrepancy. Prototype with customers and decide what should be automated, suggested, or handled through direct user controls.

 Make automation dependable. Partner with Engineering and Data to define quality measures, test realistic customer scenarios, learn from corrections, and provide clear explanations, approval boundaries, audit trails, and recovery when something goes wrong.

 Own outcomes beyond launch. Define and improve activation, repeat usage, time to complete purchasing work, and the accuracy of matching and exception resolution. Use data and customer research to choose the next iteration.

 Lead execution with engineers and designers, make scope and sequencing tradeoffs, and align partner teams on dependencies. Work with Sales, Implementation, and Customer Experience to turn customer commitments into repeatable product capabilities and support successful adoption.

 
 What You Need 
 At least three years of product management or equivalent product-building experience, with evidence of owning a product area from customer discovery through launch and measurable adoption.

 Strong product judgment and systems thinking. You can simplify complex workflows while preserving the controls and flexibility customers need.

 Hands-on AI fluency, demonstrated through products, prototypes, or meaningful projects. You can reason about model quality, latency, cost, and user control, and choose where AI improves the experience.

 Technical and analytical fluency, developed through a technical or analytical degree or equivalent practical experience. You can work with engineers on data models and integrations, use data to investigate problems, and build prototypes to test ideas.

 Deep customer curiosity and strong design judgment. You can learn unfamiliar purchasing and finance workflows, distinguish recurring needs from one-off requests, and make the product easier to use.

 A track record of leading cross-functional teams, setting priorities, making difficult tradeoffs, and delivering outcomes through others.

 Clear written and verbal communication. You can explain a product direction, a complex workflow, and the reasoning behind a decision to technical and non-technical audiences.

 
 Nice-to-Haves 
 Experience with procurement, purchasing, inventory management, accounts payable, or accounting software, including purchase orders, receiving, matching, and exception handling.

 Experience shipping AI-powered products used in production, including document understanding, agent workflows, and evaluation systems.

 Experience with ERP integrations, multi-entity businesses, or enterprise approval and permission models.

 Experience building products where accuracy and trust matter, with meaningful auditability, user controls, and recovery paths.

 Experience at a high-growth startup, taking new products from initial concept to sustained use or scaling an existing product.

Datadog is seeking a Manager, Sales Engineering to join our high-growth organization and world-class pre-sales team. You will manage a team of talented Sales Engineers to help qualify and close opportunities and coach the team on their approach to providing technical expertise through sales presentations, product demonstrations, and supporting technical evaluations (POCs). This is a hands-on management role where you will take an active technical role in your region supporting customer facing activities and engagements for key accounts.  You will also enable and nurture strong partnership between the SE team and other organizations within Datadog.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What You’ll Do: 

  • Partner with the Sales Team to articulate the overall Datadog value proposition, vision and strategy to customers.
  • Manage a team of individual contributors, working to expand usage of Datadog in customer accounts
  • Manage resource allocation of your team and ensure their maximum productivity and engagement.
  • Assist recruiting efforts to find and hire top talent within your region. Mentor/coach new hires during on-boarding to ensure proper ramping of skills and capabilities
  • Ensure that your team is enabled to support all required Datadog solutions along with key technical and soft skills
  • Develop a close working relationship with Product Management, Support, and Enablement to ensure continuity between pre and post sales activities
  • Deliver performance reviews along with collaborating on and executing individual development plans

Who You Are:

  • Experienced with 1-3+ years in a Sales Engineering team lead or mentorship role and 3+ years in a Sales Engineering or other equivalent client facing role
  • Coachable, with a strong desire to improve and grow as a professional and a demonstrated ability to navigate through change
  • Proven in your ability to grow and develop a team 
  • Experienced in recruiting both individual contributors and front line leaders
  • Knowledgeable in current infrastructure and monitoring solutions and technologies
  • Able to build and execute an evaluation plan with a customer and mentor others on how to do so
  • Someone with strong written and oral communication skills. This role requires an ability to understand and articulate both the business benefits (value proposition) and technical advantages of our offering while also coaching others how to do so
  • Able to think strategically and creatively about a wide variety of challenges

Fuse Energy is an energy startup on a mission to make energy abundant and affordable, fast. We combine first-principles thinking with cutting-edge technology to build a radically better energy system.
 We've raised over $200M from top-tier investors including Balderton, Lakestar, Accel, Creandum, Lowercarbon, Ribbit, 20VC, Hummingbird and Collaborative Fund, alongside strategic angels including Nico Rosberg and GPs behind Meta, Revolut, Spotify and Uber.
 We're building a fully integrated energy company: developing our own solar, batteries and other generation projects, building our own hardware, improving and developing grid infrastructure, trading power in real time, using AI across the business, and installing distributed energy in homes. By selling directly to consumers we cut out the middleman, lower costs and pass the savings on to our customers.

As we continue to develop cutting-edge technologies and sustainable energy solutions, we are looking for a Mechanical Engineer to join our hardware team and help take our in-house power electronics and energy storage products from concept through to mass production. You’ll own mechanical design end to end, work closely with electrical and firmware engineers, and engage directly with suppliers and test labs to get products built, certified and shipped. 
 
 
 Responsibilities 
 Own the mechanical design of power electronics and energy storage hardware, from concept and architecture through detailed design, prototyping and production release
 Design enclosures, structural components, thermal management and sealing solutions for indoor and outdoor consumer products
 Design for manufacture and assembly across injection moulding, sheet metal, die casting and extrusion; drive tolerance analysis and reviews with suppliers
 Support product compliance and certification activities, working with test labs to meet IEC/EN, UKCA and CE requirements
 Source, qualify and manage mechanical component and tooling suppliers, including on-site visits and production ramp support
 Build and execute test plans; analyse experimental and simulation data to drive design decisions
 Maintain CAD models, drawings, BOMs and engineering change control
 Contribute to feasibility studies and early concept work on new hardware programmes
 Requirements 
 Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering
 Minimum 3 years of experience in mechanical design for hardware products that have reached production
 Strong proficiency in 3D CAD and GD&T
 Hands-on experience with DFM for moulded, sheet metal or cast parts
 Experience working directly with suppliers and contract manufacturers
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a track record of taking designs from prototype to production
 Clear communicator who works well in a cross-functional team and can manage multiple projects simultaneously
 
 Nice to have 
 Master’s or PhD in Mechanical Engineering
 Experience designing power electronics products (inverters, chargers, PSUs or battery systems), including thermal design for high-power-density electronics
 Familiarity with product safety and EMC standards
 Experience with FEA and CFD
 Experience managing tooling and production ramps with overseas suppliers
 Benefits 
 Competitive salary and eligibility for equity
 Biannual bonus scheme
 Fully expensed tech to match your needs
 Private health insurance
 Breakfast and dinner allowance for office-based employees
 
 As we hire globally, benefits may vary by location.

About Ramp 
 Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
 The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
 We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.
 The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
 If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.
 
 About the Role 
 Our Employee Lifecycle team makes sure every Ramp employee has a great experience, from their first day through their last and through every change in between. As Associate, Employee Lifecycle Data, you'll own and look after the employee data behind all of it. You'll keep our Workday data accurate and well structured, and you'll make sure it flows correctly into the systems that depend on it.
 This is a new role in its current scope. You'll own employee data changes from start to finish, manage the data structure that shapes our org, and set up reconciliation and error reporting across our integrations. We're looking for someone who gets the details right, finds the root cause when data breaks, and builds processes that scale as Ramp grows.
 We're moving to Workday on January 1, and we want this person on board before go-live so they can run our employee data changes from day one.
 
 What You'll Do 
 Employee data changes 
 Own the process design and execution for role changes like transfers, promotions, manager and title changes, plus relocations (using our comp calculator for basic geo adjustments and partnering with Global Mobility on more complex moves)

 Own intake and completion of one-off data changes through Serval (our ticketing system) tickets, meeting SLAs and giving employees a clear, helpful experience

 Review and approve data change transactions to protect data quality

 Support internal mobility cycles and position management in Workday (and Ashby)

 Partner with People Business Partners, Compensation and other stakeholders to clarify requirements, manage handoffs and keep data changes moving accurately and on time

 Bulk changes 
 Own bulk data changes from start to finish, including reorgs, comp cycles and mass updates: prepare and validate the data, run the loads and confirm the results

 Build review steps and checklists that make large changes repeatable and low-risk, and partner with HRIS on EIB templates and system-level controls

 Data quality, reconciliation and stewardship 
 Build and run regular reconciliation between Workday and downstream systems, including benefits providers and international payroll

 Monitor integration errors, find root causes and fix data and process gaps with HRIS, Payroll, Benefits and vendor partners, escalating system or integration fixes to HRIS with clear root-cause analysis

 Define and document data standards, ownership and controls for employee data, and run regular audits to find and fix issues in partnership with HRIS team

 Be the go-to expert on how employee data works at Ramp, and help teammates and partners understand it

 
 What You Need 
 3-6+ years of experience in HR operations, HRIS, or HR data roles

 Experience with data changes in Workday HCM, including the ability to manage employee data throughout the full employee lifecycle - processing employee changes, organizational updates, job changes, and audits.

 A solid understanding of payroll and benefits data, and of how HRIS integrations feed those systems.

 A track record of building reconciliation, audit or error-reporting processes from scratch

 Strong attention to detail, a habit of checking your work before and after changes, and sound judgment with sensitive, confidential employee data

 Advanced Excel/Google Sheets skills for data analysis, validation and reconciliation, plus sound judgment when using AI tools—knowing when to rely on them and when human review is essential

 Clear communication with employees and stakeholders at every level

 A process-improvement mindset: you fix the underlying cause of what breaks repeatedly, and build scalable processes that uphold data standards while enabling the business

 
 Nice to Haves 
 Experience at a fast-growing company where the org structure changes often

 Experience with Serval, JIRA, or similar service desk tools

 Experience with Workday reporting

 Experience building data workflows, with and without AI

 SQL skills

Perplexity is seeking a Director of Events to own our external events worldwide: the ones we host, the stages we speak on, and the ones we sponsor. You will set the strategy, run production, manage the budget, and build the team. If you have produced a flagship and a dinner in the same week, know what a good sponsorship deal looks like, and want to build an events function from the ground up, this role is for you.
 Responsibilities 
 Own events. Hosted, speaking, sponsored. Strategy, budget, production, results.

 Set the calendar. Decide which events we run, which we speak at, and which we skip.

 Produce hosted events. Launches, dinners, summits, roadshows. Concept, programming, venue, vendors, run of show.

 Run the speaking program. Pick the stages. Prepare the speakers.

 Manage sponsorships. Negotiate terms, design our footprint, and account for the spend.

 Run field events with Sales. Get the right customers in the room. Make sure someone follows up.

 Be Perplexity. Our events should look and feel like our product. Work with Brand and Creative on every one.

 Lead the team. Equal parts IC and manager.

 Build the system. Playbooks, event tiers, intake, vendors, agencies, budgets.

 Measure. Attendance, coverage, pipeline, signups. Know which events worked and stop doing the ones that didn't.

 Be on site. For the events that matter, you are in the room.

 Qualifications 
 12+ years producing events, including large hosted events, sponsorships, and field programs, ideally in-house at a technology company.

 Has built or led an events team.

 Has owned large budgets, agency relationships, and vendor contracts.

 Has negotiated sponsorships and knows a bad deal when they see one.

 Has run an executive speaking program: selecting stages, preparing speakers, managing the day.

 Knows production: run of show, staging, AV, registration, staffing, security, permits.

 Drives measurement. Has built event attribution and tracked brand sentiment, and reports what each event returned.

 Can partner with Sales, Product, Comms, Brand, Finance, Legal, and executives.

 Power user of AI tools. Most of your work already runs through them, and you can show us how.

 Based in San Francisco or New York. Willing to travel internationally.

Overview
 The Workplace Experience team powers and connects the workday for all Perplexity employees across our global offices.
 We are hospitality and experience-driven at the core. We are made up of People people, meaning that we love supporting each other and all of the People in our workplace. We take on the good and the bad with optimism and with a positive, kind approach to solving problems, dealing with the obstacles handed to us, and proactively creating good around us. We think about each moment through the lens of our colleagues (our customers) so that we can create thoughtful and memorable experiences no matter what task we have at hand.
 As our Global Workplace Business Operations Lead, you will manage the business operations and cross-functional program delivery that enable our global Workplace Experience team to scale. In collaboration with the Head of Workplace Experience, you will set the operating framework for your areas, make decisions within agreed priorities and approval limits, and remain hands-on in delivering results. You will own the effectiveness of portfolio operating processes and internal project delivery.
 
 What You’ll Do
 Own the Workplace operating framework: Lead annual and quarterly planning for your areas, translate team strategy into priorities and resource plans, and establish clear decision rights, delivery commitments and measures of success. Resolve sequencing and capacity trade-offs within agreed parameters and recommend when to add people, vendors or technology.

 Lead internal capital-project delivery: Take accountability for integrated delivery plans across office openings, refreshes and other capital initiatives. Direct the work of external PMs within agreed scopes, align internal workstreams, resolve delivery issues and hold partners accountable for schedule, cost, quality and operational readiness.

 Own portfolio controls and insight: Establish dependable lease administration, obligation tracking, space and occupancy information, and portfolio reporting. Set data and control standards, ensure actions have owners, and turn trends and risks into recommendations before deadlines or capacity constraints become problems.

 Drive financial planning and performance: Own the processes and quality of operating and capital forecasts, commitments, actuals and variance analysis in partnership with Finance. Challenge assumptions, recommend corrective actions and investment trade-offs, and give the Head of Workplace Experience a reliable basis for budget and commitment decisions.

 Set the systems and reporting roadmap: Own business requirements, governance and improvement priorities for workplace tools such as Envoy. Establish useful performance measures, improve data quality, and automate repeatable work while maintaining appropriate controls and keeping processes practical for the team.

 Lead EHS program governance: Establish a risk-based plan, clear responsibilities and a review cadence with qualified vendors and internal teams. Drive follow-through on assessed obligations and remediation across offices and remote populations, maintain evidence of completion, and escalate material risks without substituting for specialist advice.

 Set standards for delivery and handover: Own the development and use of project playbooks, planning processes and operational-readiness criteria. Bring together design standards and occupancy requirements, and ensure completed projects transfer to local operations with the documentation, training, vendor arrangements and issue ownership needed to run well.

 Serve as a senior operating partner: Lead cross-functional operating and project reviews, surface decisions with clear recommendations, and represent your areas with internal and external partners. Drive resolution within your authority, escalate material changes with options, and build accountability without adding unnecessary layers.

 What You Bring
 Senior functional leadership: 8+ years in workplace business operations, corporate real estate, facilities programs or a closely related field, with increasing responsibility for complex, multi-site programs and their outcomes. You have operated with substantial autonomy, not only administered plans set by others.

 Project and program management expertise: You are a project manager at the core. You are quick and agile, but methodical when it comes to planning for, organizing, tracking, and executing on a project in a way that keeps everything and everyone aligned and on task.

 Relevant delivery depth: You have a record of delivering office buildouts, relocations or capital improvements as an internal owner, with accountability for scope, financial performance, schedules, change control and external delivery partners.

 Strong financial and analytical judgment: You have experience driving forecasting and reporting processes, challenging assumptions and translating portfolio data into resource or investment recommendations; strong spreadsheet and analytical skills.

 Experience building an operating framework: You have established planning, governance, performance measures and systems that helped a growing function deliver more predictably. You know when structure improves execution and when it becomes unnecessary process.

 Leadership across organizational boundaries: You can secure commitments, challenge constructively and resolve competing priorities across teams and vendors. You communicate risks and recommendations credibly to senior leaders and know which decisions to make independently and which to escalate.

 Hands-on ownership and sound judgment: You can move between portfolio-level trade-offs and project details, deliver through others without losing accountability, handle sensitive information responsibly, and maintain a kind, service-oriented approach under pressure.

 Helpful, not required: International portfolio experience, workplace technology ownership, EHS program governance, or a relevant project-management credential.

What you’ll do
 Understand the needs of the teams that use our platforms and the customers who depend on them. Use product data, operational feedback, and recurring quality issues to identify the highest-impact problems, and then solve them.

 Turn recurring needs into shared services, tools, and workflows that reduce duplicated work. Exercise judgment about when to build a reusable capability, use an existing solution, or take a simpler approach.

 Work directly with product, engineering, and operational teams to understand their workflows, identify recurring problems, and anticipate the capabilities they will need next.

 Prioritize platform investments across new product enablement, reliability, efficiency, and technical debt. Make clear tradeoffs between near-term delivery and long-term flexibility.

 Define and track success through business impact, reliability, cost to serve, and reduced manual work, connecting these measures to customer and business outcomes.

 Partner closely with engineering on technical tradeoffs, build-versus-buy decisions, and rollout plans. Write clear requirements and drive delivery from problem definition through launch and iteration.

 Qualifications
 Experience owning product strategy and execution on technical products and platforms, or shared systems used by multiple teams such as billing and monetization, identity and access, developer platforms, data and experimentation, internal tooling, support, etc.

 Strong technical fluency. You can reason about APIs, data flows, system dependencies, and failure modes, and work closely with engineers on consequential tradeoffs.

 Strong analytical skills. You can investigate problems independently, define meaningful metrics, and evaluate the impact of platform investments.

 Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to align teams around priorities and make difficult decisions when their needs compete.

 High ownership and sound judgment in a fast-moving environment. You are comfortable moving between long-term strategy and hands-on execution without adding unnecessary process.

 A focus on customer outcomes and product quality, including when your immediate users are internal teams.

 Where this person needs to spike
 Systems thinker, detail-oriented, problem solver. This person needs to have experience wrangling thorny, complex problems. We need someone that is excited about diving into messy workflows, reading through dozens of support tickets, thinking through edge cases no one’s thought of, assuming different behavior across platforms, proactively considering enterprise vs. consumer workflows, etc.

 Experience working on platforms with multiple stakeholders and non-trivial tradeoffs. This person is building products simultaneously for customers, agents, and other internal employees.

 Is “AI-native.” Can build AI products whose outputs require evaluation, safeguards, and human-in-the-loop design.

 Strong analytical skills and experience defining metrics in ambiguity, breaking down workflows, and using quantitative and qualitative evidence to prioritize.

 Some experience working on critical software: support platforms/agents, legal/compliance tooling, identity and account tooling, billing, fraud, trust-and safety, etc.

 High-ownership. This person needs to feel dissatisfied by the current support flow, and hungry to do whatever it takes to clear the backlog.

About the Team

Netlify is a product-led growth company with an unusually large organic top-of-funnel, where tens of thousands of people discover and sign up for Netlify every day. That organic motion is real and meaningful, but paid acquisition is a new investment area for the marketing team, and there's a clear opportunity to build that capability from the ground up. 

As Senior Manager, Demand Generation & Performance Marketing, you'll own paid acquisition end to end - strategy, channel selection, budget, and the agency relationship that supports execution. You'll report to the CMO, with a planned transition to the VP of Growth Marketing as that function scales, and work closely with Marketing Operations, Data, Lifecycle, and Campaigns to make sure paid-acquired users don't just land, but convert and stick. This is a builder role at a company where the organic foundation is already strong, and your job is to build the paid layer that extends its reach.

What You'll Do

  • Build and own Netlify's paid acquisition strategy end to end, including paid search, paid social, retargeting, sponsorships, and any other channels worth testing and proving out. 
  • Own the call on where paid creates incremental value for Netlify. Design the tests, prove which channels and audiences drive growth our organic funnel wouldn't have delivered anyway, and decide where to scale, where to hold, and where not to spend at all.
  • Manage the agency relationship(s) supporting paid/performance work by setting the brief, holding the agency accountable to targets, and deciding what to bring in-house as the function matures.
  • Own budget planning, pacing, and ROI reporting for all paid spend, and make the case for where to double down or pull back.
  • Partner with Marketing Operations to get attribution and UTM tracking right before scaling spend, so every dollar is measurable.
  • Define target audiences and channel mix aligned to Netlify's ICP; partner with Product Marketing on messaging inputs for paid creative.
  • Build the measurement framework for CAC, signup/pipeline contribution, and payback by channel.
  • Partner with Lifecycle and Campaigns to make sure paid-acquired users flow into the right onboarding and activation journeys, not just land and drop off.
  • As the program proves out, build the roadmap and case for a fully staffed paid/performance team.

What You'll Bring

  • 6+ years in demand generation or performance marketing, with direct ownership of a paid acquisition budget in a B2B SaaS or product-led growth environment
  • Hands-on experience running paid search, paid social, and retargeting programs yourself - not just briefing agencies or reviewing their reports
  • A track record of standing up or significantly scaling a paid acquisition program at an early stage, where you had to build the infrastructure and not just optimize what was already there
  • Experience managing an external agency or partner relationship, including setting performance expectations and holding partners accountable to them
  • Working knowledge of attribution and marketing measurement, and a history of partnering with Marketing Ops or Data teams to get tracking right before spend scales
  • Some experience marketing to developers or technical audiences, or with a PLG motion where paid acquisition runs alongside a large organic and self-serve funnel

This Role Is a Great Fit If

  • You're energized by building and scaling a new paid program, not just optimizing one that's already mature.
  • You think like an owner of budget and outcomes, not just a briefs-and-reports manager of an agency.
  • You're comfortable moving between strategy (channel mix, targeting, budget allocation) and getting into the details yourself when it matters.
  • You care about attribution being right before spend scales, not as an afterthought.
  • You want to build in close partnership with Lifecycle, Campaigns, and Marketing Ops rather than run paid as a separate lane that hands off a spreadsheet at the end of the quarter

Applying

Not sure you meet 100% of our qualifications? Please apply anyway!

When applying please include: 

A resume or short listing of your job history & skills (link to a LinkedIn profile would be fine). We appreciate a cover letter explaining why you would enjoy working in this role at Netlify to get to know you a bit better, though this is not required and will not impact your application. Our mission is to “build a better web” and that cannot be done without a diversity of skill sets, backgrounds and thoughts. 

Of everything we've ever built at Netlify, we are most proud of our team. Netlify is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are devoted to building a team of people with diverse backgrounds and lifestyles. Driving equality empowers our team, enables us to innovate, and helps us maintain a more inclusive environment. We don’t discriminate against employees or applicants based on gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, age, race, military/veteran status, citizenship, pregnancy status, or any other differences. If we can do anything to provide a better interview, i.e. accommodate a disability, then please let us know by emailing accommodations@netlify.com. 

About Netlify

Netlify is the most popular way to build, deploy, and scale modern web applications, empowering everyone from fast moving solo developers to enterprise teams. Millions of developers and organizations rely on Netlify as their platform of choice for composing web applications that are production ready, performant, and flexible. Now, as we embrace the next era of software development, we are embedding the same fluid, intuitive experience into the Agent Experience (AX), making it just as simple for intelligent agents to understand, interact with, and act on our platform as it is for developers. Whether your user is human or machine, Netlify ensures the path from idea to URL is seamless, fast, and deeply reliable.

We are a Series D company that has raised over $200M from investors such as Andreessen Horowitz, Kleiner Perkins, EQT, Bessemer, BOND, and Menlo Ventures. As a fully distributed company, we aim to create a company culture where the best idea can come from anywhere and strive to be thoughtful, compassionate, and collaborative in our work. If this sounds like something you’d like to be part of, we’re excited to connect with you!

At Netlify, we are committed to a compensation philosophy that prioritizes fairness and equity, positions our employee compensation competitively in the market, recognizes and rewards performance, and takes a comprehensive approach to our rewards package. We anchor our compensation philosophy on a market-based approach, therefore salary ranges may differ depending on the labor cost in a particular location. The salary provided is in addition to robust benefits and participation in Netlify’s equity plan. Our hiring range for this role is targeted at $150,000 - $200,000  for most US-based locations. Candidates outside the US or in premium markets should consult with their Talent Acquisition partner regarding location-based ranges, as they may be higher or lower than the average US range listed. The starting pay will be determined based on multiple factors, including expertise and skills, market demands, experience, internal equity, and applicable geographic location. These compensation packages and ranges are subject to change and may be modified in the future.

About the Role

We are seeking a Senior Analyst, Procurement Operations to manage vendor onboarding and improve the systems and workflows that support the purchasing lifecycle.

You will guide vendors and internal stakeholders through onboarding requirements, coordinate reviews and approvals, maintain accurate data, and resolve issues that delay requests. You will also help improve Zip and related systems by identifying process gaps, documenting requirements, testing changes, and supporting automation and reporting.

This role is ideal for someone with strong operational judgment, a systems mindset, and the ability to manage a high volume of requests in an evolving environment.

What You’ll Do

  • Manage vendor onboarding requests from submission through completion.
  • Review submissions for completeness, accuracy, and required documentation.
  • Coordinate reviews, approvals, and follow-ups with Privacy, GRC, IT, Internal Audit, Legal, Finance, and other teams.
  • Help vendors and employees understand requirements, complete outstanding tasks, and resolve system issues.
  • Maintain accurate vendor records, approvals, contracts, documents, and audit trails across Zip and connected systems.
  • Monitor request volumes, aging, and cycle times, prioritizing urgent requests and escalating blockers.
  • Serve as a subject matter expert for Zip and related procurement systems.
  • Translate policies and business needs into clear requirements for workflows, routing, approvals, notifications, reporting, and exceptions.
  • Test system changes, document results, report defects, and support releases through training and communications.
  • Identify opportunities to improve P2P processes through data, AI, and automation.

What You’ll Bring

  • 3+ years of experience in procure-to-pay, vendor management, finance, or purchasing operations.
  • Experience managing vendor onboarding or vendor lifecycle processes.
  • Hands-on experience with platforms such as Zip, Coupa, Oracle, NetSuite, DocuSign, Brex, Ramp, or similar tools.
  • Understanding of how vendor data, purchasing requests, contracts, purchase orders, invoices, approvals, and payments connect.
  • Experience maintaining accurate system data and resolving incomplete, inconsistent, or duplicate records.
  • Ability to document business requirements, test system changes, and work with technical teams to resolve issues.
  • Sound judgment when applying policies, managing exceptions, and escalating risks.

Perplexity is continuing to rapidly scale our Enterprise Engineering Organization and seeking Engineering Managers with deep expertise across the Enterprise domain to help lead the next wave of growth.
 As an Enterprise Engineering Manager, you will combine technical judgment, product intuition, and people leadership to help large organizations adopt AI at scale. We are hiring across the enterprise control plane, enterprise data plane, and connector marketplace and activation. Depending on your area of focus, you will lead and grow a team in one of these areas, addressing challenges such as:
 Enterprise Control Plane : Building the identity, security, and governance foundations that enable large organizations to deploy Perplexity confidently, including SSO, SCIM, role-based access, customer-managed encryption keys (BYOK), admin APIs, and enforceable policies governing access to data, models, and tools. Supporting regulated-industry requirements, including SOC 2, HIPAA, data governance, and residency, with audit logs and analytics that give administrators visibility into how Perplexity is used.
 Enterprise Data Plane : Building the connector platform and semantic data layer that give Computer reliable, permission-aware access to enterprise systems and knowledge, including managed authorization, private-system access, and data freshness.
 Connector Marketplace and Activation : Building discovery, recommendations, onboarding, and marketplace experiences that help customers find and adopt integrations, while working with partners to expand the connector ecosystem.
 Across these areas, you will translate enterprise customer needs into scalable technical solutions across Perplexity’s products.
 
 Responsibilities
 Set technical direction for your team and guide architecture decisions across the enterprise platform.

 Build the foundational systems that enable large organizations to deploy Perplexity broadly and confidently.

 Shape roadmaps with product and design, applying strong technical judgment and product intuition.

 Set a high bar for reliability, code quality, testing, and maintenance. Lead incident response and ensure platform changes and connector migrations are rolled out safely.

 Partner with engineering teams across the company to ensure the platforms we build are extensible and easy to adopt.

 Represent engineering in strategic enterprise customer conversations, partnering with sales and customer success to understand requirements and remove barriers to adoption.

 Oversee hiring, onboarding, and mentorship for a rapidly growing team. Develop rigorous interview pipelines and work closely with recruiting to source candidates.

 Work with Perplexity’s co-founders to deliver enterprise engineering priorities.

 
 Qualifications
 Strong technical judgment and experience building enterprise platforms or products, with an understanding of the reliability, security, and usability requirements of enterprise customers.

 Domain expertise in at least one of the following areas: 
 Enterprise control plane: identity and access management, SSO/SCIM, role-based access, key management, admin APIs, policy enforcement, audit logging, data governance, or compliance and residency requirements for regulated industries.

 Enterprise data plane: connector and integration platforms, including authentication, source-system permissions, data synchronization, and reliability at scale; or semantic data layers and knowledge platforms that make enterprise data accessible and useful to AI.

 Connector marketplace and activation: discovery and recommendation systems, integration onboarding, marketplace product UX, or technology partner ecosystems.

 
 Ability to deliver in a fast-moving environment while balancing customer needs, technical quality, and long-term maintainability.

 Detail-oriented and quality-focused - our customers run critical workflows on Perplexity, and our product needs to stay robust and reliable.

 Ability to translate enterprise customer needs into clear technical priorities and communicate tradeoffs effectively.

 Experience building and managing high-performing engineering teams, with a strong management practice grounded in clear feedback, effective 1:1s, career development, and recruiting and retaining high-caliber talent.

 Experience with AI/ML products, enterprise AI adoption, or scaling enterprise platforms at a startup is a plus.

description:
The Technical Solutions (TS) Enablement team empowers Datadog's global post-sales organization—including Support, Customer Success, and Sales Engineering—with the skills, tools, and resources they need to deliver world-class customer outcomes. As a Senior TS Enablement Program Manager supporting Global Support Engineering, you'll own the design and execution of complex, high-visibility enablement programs that drive lasting change across the TS organization. You'll operate with significant autonomy, lead cross-functional initiatives, and serve as a senior voice within the Enablement team—partnering closely with leadership to translate business priorities into measurable enablement impact at scale.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What You'll Do:

  • Own the end-to-end strategy and execution for complex, global enablement programs—managing multiple concurrent workstreams across regions, functions, and timelines with limited guidance.
  • Lead cross-functional stakeholder relationships with senior partners across StratOps, Product, TS Leadership, and the People Team—negotiating scope, aligning on priorities, and driving accountability without positional authority.
  • Translate business goals and OKRs into multi-quarter program roadmaps; communicate priorities, trade-offs, and progress to leadership with clarity and a clear point of view.
  • Design and implement comprehensive metrics frameworks to measure change adoption and program effectiveness; pull and analyze Salesforce and LMS data to track performance against KPIs; present findings to senior stakeholders and iterate for lasting impact.
  • Build and deliver executive-ready materials that tell a compelling business story—translating complex data, program updates, and regional insights into structured narratives with clear recommendations.
  • Conduct ongoing needs assessments, stakeholder interviews, and pulse checks across TS regions; synthesize qualitative and quantitative feedback to inform program strategy and surface emerging gaps.
  • Design the tools, resources, communications, and training frameworks needed to support TS workflow changes at scale—partnering with Curriculum and Field teams on content development and delivery.
  • Partner with Global Support Engineering leadership to design ramp and enablement programs that account for differences in specialist vs. generalist skill development across the support org.
  • Mentor and develop junior EPM ICs on the team—providing structured feedback on program design and stakeholder management, and raising the quality bar across program work.
  • Identify and implement AI-powered workflows, automations, and process improvements that increase the efficiency, consistency, and scalability of enablement programs—from reporting and data pipelines to content creation and stakeholder communications.
  • Maintain a deep, current understanding of regional needs, TS team performance, and functional priorities to ensure programs remain relevant and impactful across a global audience.

Who You Are:

  • Bachelor’s degree and 6–8 years of related experience in enablement, program management, change management, or a closely related field—or a Master’s degree with 4+ years.
  • Proven track record leading complex, multi-quarter programs with high visibility—comfortable operating independently and making sound judgment calls with limited oversight.
  • Expert at building and managing senior stakeholder relationships across functions; can drive alignment, navigate competing priorities, and influence outcomes without positional authority.
  • Deeply data-driven—you design measurement frameworks, analyze program and performance data, and build Salesforce and LMS reports to connect enablement programs to field KPIs and business outcomes.
  • Exceptional presentation and communication skills—builds well-structured, visually compelling decks and delivers them confidently to senior and executive audiences with a clear, well-reasoned point of view.
  • Expert in change management and organizational development best practices, with a demonstrated history of driving adoption at scale across global organizations. PROSCI/ADKAR certification (or equivalent) required.
  • Deep understanding of the day-to-day responsibilities, challenges, and workflows of the TS functions you support; recognized as a credible strategic partner, not just a program coordinator.
  • Skilled in program management tools (Asana, Jira) and collaboration platforms (Confluence, Slack, Docebo).
  • Actively applies AI tools (e.g., Claude, agentic workflows) to streamline operations, surface insights, and improve program delivery—and helps others on the team do the same.

Bonus Points:

  • Hands-on experience in, or working closely alongside, a technical support organization (e.g., prior support engineer, specialist support, or generalist support experience).
  • Expert-level familiarity with instructional design methodologies (e.g., ADDIE, Kirkpatrick) and adult learning theory.
  • Experience building or scaling enablement programs in a high-growth or enterprise SaaS environment.
  • Track record of successfully delivering global programs across multiple regions (Americas, EMEA, APJ).
  • Proficient with the Datadog platform and monitoring best practices (e.g., DD Fundamentals certified), with solid working knowledge of the observability industry and the personas your audience serves.

description:
Job Description

We're looking for an experienced Principal Partner Program Manager to own the Datadog Partner Network's solution provider program end to end, across Datadog's Channels & Alliances organization.

 

In this role, you'll be the program owner for Datadog's solution provider (reseller) partner program — setting program strategy, structure, tiering, and requirements, and driving the partner lifecycle from recruitment and onboarding through enablement and ongoing performance management. You'll also serve as the subject matter expert for partner pricing, helping shape how Datadog structures, operationalizes, and scales partner pricing across its ecosystem, and acting as the primary liaison between Channels & Alliances and Deal Desk on partner-specific pricing requirements and commercial frameworks.

You'll support both internal teams and external partners by providing guidance on program benefits, pricing models, deal structures, incentives, and commercial programs. You'll own enablement for the solution provider program more broadly, including pricing enablement, developing training content and onboarding programs that help Partner Sales Managers and partners confidently navigate the program and Datadog's evolving pricing landscape.

This is a highly cross-functional role that requires deep experience building and running reseller-focused partner programs, along with experience in partner commercial models and SaaS pricing, and the ability to translate program and pricing strategy into scalable processes, tools, and training.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture—the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What You'll Do

Own the Datadog Partner Network solution provider program

  • Own the strategy, structure, and roadmap for the Datadog Partner Network's solution provider (reseller) program
  • Define and manage program tiers, requirements, and benefits for solution provider partners
  • Drive the end-to-end partner lifecycle — recruitment, onboarding, activation, and ongoing performance management — for solution provider partners
  • Serve as the Channels & Alliances subject matter expert for partner pricing, commercial frameworks, and deal strategy
  • Act as the primary liaison between Channels & Alliances and Deal Desk for partner-related pricing, discounting, incentives, and program requirements
  • Advise Partner Sales Managers (PSMs) and partners on program benefits, pricing models, deal structures, and commercial considerations
  • Support partner-facing conversations and help partners understand the solution provider program and Datadog's consumption-based pricing model
  • Partner with Deal Desk, Finance, Operations, Legal, and Leadership teams to evaluate and operationalize new program elements, partner pricing models, incentives, and commercial programs
  • Ensure solution provider program requirements, including partner-specific pricing, are reflected in company-wide processes, policies, systems, and tools
  • Develop scalable documentation, playbooks, FAQs, and resources that improve program and pricing consistency across the partner organization
  • Create and deliver onboarding and ongoing enablement programs for Partner Sales Managers and partners related to the solution provider program, pricing, deal strategy, and commercial programs

Who You Are

  • 8-10 years of experience building and scaling partner programs, with deep expertise in reseller or solution provider-focused programs, within a SaaS or technology company
  • Proven experience owning the full partner program lifecycle, including design, recruitment, onboarding, enablement, and performance management
  • Experience with partner commercial models, including pricing, incentives, rebates, discounts, and other program constructs
  • Direct experience working with Deal Desk or similar functions to support partner pricing, discounting frameworks, approvals, and complex deal structures
  • Strong understanding of SaaS pricing models, including experience supporting consumption-based or usage-based businesses
  • Experience serving as a trusted advisor on program and commercial strategy for partner-facing teams
  • Demonstrated ability to translate program and pricing strategy into scalable processes, tools, and enablement programs
  • Excellent communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills

Bonus Points

  • Experience owning or contributing to partner program platforms, pricing calculators, quoting systems, CPQ tools, or commercial operations platforms
  • Experience building and delivering partner or pricing enablement programs at scale
  • Experience supporting global partner organizations and regional sales teams
  • Quantitative background in business, economics, finance, mathematics, analytics, engineering, or a related discipline
  • Background in SaaS and/or consumption-based software platforms

Reporting Structure

This role reports to the Manager, Global Partner Programs, Channels & Alliances.

description:
About Ramp 
 Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
 The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
 We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.
 The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
 If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.
 
 About the Role 
 How we build software is changing. Designers are building tools and agents, prototyping in code, and shipping directly into the product. More people can create software than ever before. That makes design judgment more important, not less.
 We’re looking for a Design Systems Lead to build that judgment into the foundations of Ramp.
 This is not just about maintaining a component library. It’s about making it possible for designers, engineers, and agents to build experiences that look, feel, and work like Ramp—without a designer driving every decision or the design systems team reviewing every change.
 You’re a designer first, with the technical depth to guide architecture and get into the code. You have exceptional taste and strong opinions about typography, hierarchy, interaction, and motion. Just as importantly, you know how to turn that judgment into patterns, tools, and guidance that make everyone else’s work better.
 You’re deeply curious about AI and already using it to change how you work. You build, experiment, inspect the results, and push past the demo. You can imagine a different way of building software—and lead a team toward it.
 This role is for you if you’re excited by:
 Making great design reproducible. Raise the quality of Ramp’s product and encode what makes it good, so people and agents can produce coherent, usable experiences by default. The system should make excellent work easier, not make every experience look the same.

 Reimagining what a design system can be. Build beyond components and tokens into composition, interaction patterns, agent guidance, and evaluations. Connect exploration and production so the fastest way to build is also a path to great quality.

 Leading a team that multiplies everyone else’s impact. Create clear direction, ambitious goals, and a caring yet demanding environment. Inspire curiosity, develop people, and stay close enough to the work to help make it exceptional.

 The opportunity is to raise the floor for everyone building at Ramp, while giving designers more room to make the most important experiences extraordinary.
 
 What You'll Do 
 Lead and develop the design systems team. Set clear priorities, ownership, and goals. Give direct, timely feedback, hold people accountable, and help them do the best work of their careers.

 Own the system’s vision and direction. Decide what to preserve, evolve, simplify, or replace based on what builders and customers need. Turn that direction into focused work the team can deliver.

 Elevate Ramp’s visual and interaction design. Raise the bar for typography, hierarchy, density, motion, responsive behavior, accessibility, and the states beyond the happy path.

 Make design judgment usable by people and agents. Translate principles into reusable patterns, reference experiences, composition rules, and guidance that produce better work without you in the room.

 Guide technical architecture with engineering. Shape everything from components and tokens to how agents discover guidance, compose interfaces, and check their work. Make sound tradeoffs between flexibility, coherence, performance, and ease of use.

 Stay hands-on. Build prototypes, work in code, and get into implementation details to test ideas, unblock the team, and understand where the system breaks down.

 Define and measure quality. Build repeatable evaluations grounded in real tasks. Measure whether builders can ship better work faster, with less rework—not just whether they use the tools.

 Improve the path from idea to shipped experience. Partner with engineering and AI teams on workflows that support fast exploration, useful iteration, and appropriate production safeguards.

 Earn adoption. Work alongside product teams, listen closely, teach through examples, and turn recurring questions and exceptions into improvements to the system.

 Keep the team moving forward. Experiment as models and tools evolve, share what you learn, and change direction when the evidence calls for it.

 
 What You Need 
 
 Experience leading and developing strong design or design engineering teams, with a track record of setting direction and delivering meaningful outcomes.

 Exceptional visual and interaction design skills. Your work shows a clear point of view, attention to detail, and an ability to make complex experiences feel simple.

 Deep systems thinking and experience building systems that other teams actually adopt. You can show how your work improved both their speed and the quality of what shipped.

 Strong technical fluency. You can prototype and build in code, understand front-end architecture, and work through implementation tradeoffs with engineers—not just hand off specifications.

 Active, hands-on use of AI in your design and building workflow. You understand where it helps, where it fails, and how to improve its output rather than accept it.

 Experience turning design principles into practical guidance, reusable patterns, and quality checks that work at scale.

 Strong product judgment and a habit of staying close to the people using what you build. You connect system decisions to real workflows and customer outcomes.

 The ability to create clarity in ambiguity, make decisions, give difficult feedback, and maintain momentum without losing the quality bar.

 Curiosity that borders on obsession about how AI changes software and how we build it—and the ability to ignite that curiosity in others.

 Nice to Haves
 Experience building agent-usable design guidance, generation workflows, or evaluations for design quality.

 Experience building developer or designer tools that became part of other teams’ daily workflow.

 Experience leading a major design-system migration or company-wide change in how teams build.

 Experience evolving a system across platforms or connecting product and brand experiences.

 Founder or early-stage startup experience.

job_title: Manager I, Applied Science - Frontier Agentic Models
description:
Applied AI is where Datadog's ambitious AI bets get built and shipped (Bits Chat, updog). We sit at the intersection of research and product: turning promising capabilities from Datadog AI Research lab and the research community into production systems that reach real customers. The team builds the foundations for agentic systems capable of operating at scale in complex production environments. Current bets span agents that run autonomously at scale, context and memory layers that make those agents more intelligent over time, and tools that help customers build and validate AI-native services in production. The mandate is to move fast from idea to customer impact, and when a product finds its footing, to set it up for growth.


As an Engineering Manager I in Applied AI, you will lead a team of engineers and applied scientists working on one of these challenges. You will define technical direction, run short feedback loops, make deliberate decisions about what to pursue or stop, and work closely with product managers, research teams, and cross-functional partners to ship AI capabilities that matter.


At Datadog, we place value in our office culture, the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.


What You'll Do 

  • Lead and develop a team of engineers and applied scientists focused on building the foundations for agents operating at scale
  • Work closely with product managers, research teams, and cross-functional partners to shape the team's bets from initial framing through to broader adoption, with a clear definition of success criteria at each stage
  • Own end-to-end delivery of high-quality AI systems, from early research exploration to production-grade reliability, with high standards for operational excellence, system reliability, and technical quality
  • Navigate the unique challenges of shipping AI-powered products: balancing quality, latency, cost, and safety considerations. Drive evaluation and iteration practices for AI systems: define the quality bar and guide the team in building the offline and online evaluation pipelines needed to measure quality and detect drift
  • Contribute to cross-team collaboration and knowledge sharing across the broader AI organization
  • Support career growth for engineers through coaching, feedback, and fostering a culture of experimentation, innovation, and learning. Participate in hiring and help shape the future team as the organization grows


Who You Are

  • A people-focused manager with experience leading and mentoring engineers, able to develop strong engineering talent in a fast-moving domain
  • A technical leader with deep expertise in one or more areas of AI or machine learning: large language models, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), semantic search, agentic systems, deep learning, or NLP
  • Well-versed in evaluation methodologies for AI systems, both offline benchmarks and online metrics
  • A strong product instinct: able to anchor early-stage work in concrete customer problems, define success criteria before writing code, and actively contribute to shaping product direction alongside product and research partners
  • Experience taking AI products from 0 to 1 is strongly valued: able to bring structure to early-stage work by scoping clear hypotheses, moving quickly toward signal, and making deliberate decisions about what to pursue, pivot, or stop
  • BS/MS/PhD in Machine Learning, Computer Science, Engineering, or related field, or equivalent professional experience
