Team description

At Datadog, AI agents are becoming first-class consumers of observability, security, and software delivery data — from third-party coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, and Copilot, to our own Bits SRE, Bits Assistant, and Bits Dev Agent. The Agentic Interfaces team owns the platform that connects these agents to Datadog: the MCP Server, the tools and retrieval surfaces agents call into, and — critically — the evaluation systems that tell us whether an agent's experience on Datadog data is actually getting better over time.

This role is about that last piece. We're hiring a Staff Applied Scientist to define what "good" means for an Agentic interface at Datadog and to build the measurement systems that make it true. "Good" isn't one number — it spans answer quality, tool-selection accuracy, retrieval relevance, latency, token cost, and end-to-end agent success on real customer workflows. You'll design the evals, build the datasets, define the metrics, and partner with the AI engineers on the team to land the platform that lets every product group at Datadog ship integrations that are demonstrably better release over release.

The space is full of open research questions. How do you evaluate an agent end-to-end when the trajectory is non-deterministic? How do you score tool selection when the tool catalog has hundreds of entries and grows weekly? How do you build a measurement system that catches regressions across first-party and third-party agents at once, without each team writing their own harness? If those are the problems you want to spend your time on, come build this with us.

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply.

 

What You’ll Do:

  • Own the evaluation strategy for Datadog's AI agent integrations. Define the metrics — offline and online, quality and cost, single-turn and trajectory-level — that the team and the broader organization optimize against.

  • Build the eval datasets, golden traces, and regression harnesses that catch quality changes before they hit customers, and make those assets reusable by every team contributing tools to the platform.

  • Drive measurable improvements to retrieval relevance, tool-selection accuracy, and context efficiency, partnering closely with the AI engineers on the team who build the underlying platform.

  • Run applied research on the open problems in agent–data interaction: tool selection under large catalogs, multi-turn agent evaluation, grounding and hallucination control on live telemetry, cost/quality tradeoffs at scale.

  • Partner with the Bits SRE, Bits Assistant, and Bits Dev Agent teams so first-party agents benefit from the same measurement substrate as third-party integrations, and so learnings move freely in both directions.

  • Provide technical leadership across the Agentic Interfaces team and the broader organization through design reviews, working groups, and mentorship, and represent the team externally through talks, blog posts, and contributions to the open agent ecosystem.


Who You Are:

  • You have a BS/MS/PhD in a scientific field, or equivalent experience.

  • 10+ years of relevant engineering or applied science experience, including time as a technical lead.

  • Proven track record of leading ML or GenAI initiatives in a product-driven environment, from research through production.

  • Significant experience with evaluation, experimentation, or measurement of ML systems at scale.

job_title: Strategic Account Executive, Public Sector Japan, SLED
description:
DatadogのSLED（State / Local / Education・自治体・教育機関・病院・大学/研究機関）セールスチームは、顧客が直面する現実的な課題を解決するベスト・イン・クラスのプロダクトを提供しています。セールス担当者は、顧客ごとの固有のニーズを的確に把握し、Datadogの価値を明確に伝えるための体系化されたセールスメソドロジーに基づいて活動します。トップセールスから学びたい方、またはトップセールスとして活躍したい方にとって、Datadogのセールスチームは個人の成長とチームの成功の両立を本気で支援する環境です。

私たちは、テクノロジーに強い情熱を持ち、チャレンジングな売上目標を達成できる経験豊富なSLEDセールスエグゼクティブを募集しています。Datadogがより大きな市場へ進出し、Public Sector（自治体・教育機関・病院・大学/研究機関）向けエンタープライズセグメントへの支援を本格化する中で、このポジションは組織成長を牽引する重要な役割を担います。新たなSLEDアカウントの開拓に加え、オンプレミスとクラウドのハイブリッド環境からクラウド移行を進める顧客とも関わることができる、非常に魅力的な機会です。

Datadogでは、オフィスカルチャーによって築かれる人間関係やコラボレーション、そこからもたらされる創造性を大切にしています。私たちは、従業員それぞれに合ったワーク・ライフ・ハーモニー（ワークライフバランス）を実現できるよう、ハイブリッド・ワークプレイス（ハイブリットな職場環境）として運営しています。

業務内容：

  • 自治体・教育機関・病院・大学/研究機関（SLED）の大規模組織に対するプロスペクティングと、効率的なセールスプロセスの実行
  • 担当テリトリーにおける関係者マップの構築・管理（既存関係者および将来的なキーパーソン含む）
  • 顧客ビジネスへの深い理解の構築
  • 価値とROIを軸に、大規模SLED顧客との価格・契約条件の交渉
  • 既存顧客の期待値をマネジメントしながら、担当テリトリー内での関係拡張・深耕
  • 解決が容易でない課題に直面した際の高い問題解決力の発揮
  • クロージングに必要なステップを直感的に把握し、顧客の合意を獲得
  • すべての商談における価値ドライバーの特定
  • 高い予測精度と一貫性のあるフォーキャスト管理

募集要項：

  • 5年以上のクロージング経験をお持ちの方（SLED領域でのフィールドセールス経験を含む）
  • 2～3年以上の官公庁／自治体／教育機関向けセールス経験
  • 年間100万ドル以上の売上目標を達成・超過した実績があり、平均ディールサイズ10万ドル以上の取引経験
  • 自らプロスペクティングし、パイプラインを構築できるセールスメソドロジーを持つ方
  • SaaS、ITインフラなど、革新的なテック企業での勤務経験（尚可）
  • 大規模SLED組織に対する新規ロゴ獲得の実績

Datadogは、さまざまな立場の人々を大切にしています。誰もが初日から上記の資格をすべて満たすわけではないことは理解しています。それでも構いません。テクノロジーに情熱を持ち、スキルを伸ばしたいと思っている方は、ぜひご応募ください。

  • 個々のパフォーマンスと成果に基づく豊かな報酬体系
  • 新入社員への株式付与（RSU / 譲渡制限付株式ユニット）および従業員株式購入制度（ESPP）
  • プレジデント・クラブへの参加機会
  • 継続的な専門能力開発、製品トレーニング、キャリアパスの提供 
  • MEDDICとCommand of Messageに関する丁寧な営業研修 
  • 社内ネットワーク構築のためのメンターおよびバディ・プログラム

  • 幅広く手厚い医療関連の福利厚生制度
  • 企業型確定拠出年金（401K）
  • ペットの養子縁組と保険プログラム

TPMs at Datadog see the problems hiding between teams, engineer away the work that shouldn’t require humans, and drive the company’s most technically complex and consequential bets to completion.

About the Role
Technical Program Management at Datadog operates at the intersection of engineering depth and organizational reach by driving high priority, cross-functional programs that are too complex and consequential for any single team to own. We partner with engineering on solving deeply technical problems at scale by connecting the people, decisions, and context to move Datadog's most important work forward.

We build the systems and automation that make entire classes of program work self-executing. We are in the architecture conversation early, earning trust through technical judgment. We use AI to surface risks earlier, accelerate program execution plans, and find cross-team patterns that would otherwise stay hidden. The faster teams move, the more essential it is to have someone who can operate across them.

What we expect
These are the expectations we hold for every TPM at Datadog.

  • Technical depth, product domain expertise, and AI systems literacy; knowing how AI solutions work, where they fail, and the scope and impact of those failures. AI brings more complexity into the picture - the technical bar is higher, not lower.

  • Build the systems that reduce the need for coordination

  • Identify what matters before anyone asks, and automate the rest

  • Engineer program lifecycles end-to-end

  • See what no single team can see and own the solution

  • Drive the company's most technically complex and consequential bets through cross-functional agreement, organizational visibility, and influence

  • Build AI powered automation tools and deploy them at every stage of program execution

What you will do
See Across: Identify What No Single Team Can See

  • Own large cross-functional programs spanning multiple engineering orgs, product, and business functions

  • Proactively surface systemic risks, cross-pod dependencies, and organizational friction before they become escalations

  • Build and maintain SVP-level visibility through tracked KPIs on Datadog’s highest-priority initiatives

  • Uses technical credibility, trusted relationships, and product domain expertise to bridge the gaps between functions where misalignment is expensive

Engineer Away: Automate What Shouldn’t Require Humans

  • Identify repeatable program archetypes and engineer the lifecycle end-to-end with AI solutions; the goal is to make the program run itself

  • Build automation that reduces the need for coordination, eliminating program overhead so engineers and PMs spend time only on work requiring human judgment

  • Contribute to the TPM toolkit: AI-powered risk synthesis, dependency tracking, stakeholder mapping, and program templates

  • Drive the shift from manual coordination to self-executing program infrastructure

Drive Completion: Move The Company’s Most Complex Bets Forward

  • Lead programs across four archetypes: deep technical, large cross-functional, product delivery, and operational

  • Accelerate alignment by removing friction and overhead, not by adding process.

  • Hold the judgment call on when to escalate, when to slow down, when a technical decision has organizational implications

  • Own outcomes, not activities - your value is measured by what ships and what never had the chance to become a problem

What we are looking for
Required

  • 3+ years of technical program management at a high-growth technology company

  • Demonstrated ability to drive large, ambiguous, cross-functional programs to completion with minimal direction

  • Engineering credibility earned through hands-on experience with technically complex domains — observability, infrastructure, data platforms, or AI/ML systems including model training pipelines, ML infrastructure, and GPU compute. You can go deep on architecture and system design, push back on technical decisions, and hold your own in the room with staff engineers and senior ICs.

  • Track record of earning trust with senior engineering and product leadership - not through title, through judgment

  • Strong written and verbal communication; comfortable owning the narrative at VP+ levels

  • Active AI practitioner, you use AI tools in your daily work and can demonstrate how they’ve changed your leverage

  • You have built something, a tool, a template, an automated workflow, that other people use

Strong Signal

  • You identified a systemic problem no one asked you to find and built the operating system to solve it

  • You automated a program lifecycle or workflow that previously required manual coordination

  • You have operated in observability, infrastructure, data platforms, or AI/ML environments and can speak to the technical architecture, not just the program execution

  • You have managed programs with real unit economics implications - cloud cost, capacity, margin

Datadog Benefits

  • New hire stock equity (RSUs) and employee stock purchase plan (ESPP)

  • Continuous professional development, product training, and career pathing

  • Assigned TPM mentor and engineering buddy program for learning and relationship building

  • An inclusive company culture, active Community Guilds (Datadog employee resource groups), in-person team summits, local office programming

  • Competitive global benefits; free, mental health benefits for employees and dependents age 6+

PSEs engage with Datadog’s Premier Customers via standard technical support channels, but are also involved with cadence calls, demos/presentations, conferences, and various side projects. You will work directly with Datadog’s Premier Customer base, and will be immersed in a fast-paced environment where you will be challenged, but will also immediately witness your contributions to Datadog and to our customers.

 

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

  • Respond to client requests (phone / chat / tickets) on our fast paced team while continuing to educate our clients on the use of the platform
  • Develop relationships with our Premier Customers, working hand-in-hand to truly know their distinct environment
  • Reproduce issues and dive into the 600+ integrations that Datadog works with
  • Build out documentation and knowledge based articles for a variety of technology
  • Drive product conversations based on needs and problems learned during client interactions
  • Participate in routine health check meetings with Premier Customers
  • Work from a Datadog office 3 - 5 days per week

 

Who You Are:

  • Experienced in multi-channel technical support at a SaaS company (5+ years of related experience)
  • A tinkerer with some programming experience and a basic knowledge of Linux
  • Self-motivated, detail-attentive, and have a desire for continuous learning
  • A critical thinker who defaults to a client-centric approach
  • A decision maker but know when the decision should be escalated

 Early Career Talent @ Perplexity
 ​Perplexity believes that exceptionally talented individuals at any stage can thrive in our high-velocity, high-ownership culture. ​Our early career talent program revolves around:
 ​ Breadth : New grads at Perplexity work across the stack, from Perplexity's agent harnesses to our AI inference and training systems. Many of our most beloved features and most important systems were shipped by individuals fresh out of school.

 ​ Depth : New grads are entrusted (and expected) to dive deep into whatever problem domains you work on. Often, your work will require you to become a world expert in some problem space that few others in the world have encountered.

 ​ Mentorship & Growth : We keep the size of our entering new grad cohorts at well below 10% of our technical team. Each individual enjoys a rich network of mentors to help them grow, and our new grads have a track record of becoming some of Perplexity's most senior and prolific team members.

 ​ Recognition : We select for the best and we recognize them accordingly. We set our early career compensation to rise well above that of top tech companies and startups. Post-hire, we aggressively recognize and reward growth in role.

 ​ Mission : Perplexity is AI for people who expect more. Our mission is to build frontier intelligence for the world's most discerning users, and each contribution you make will directly advance that mission.

job_title: Tech Lead and Manager (TLM), Production Engineering
description:
About Ramp 
 Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
 The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
 We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.
 The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
 If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.
 
 About Production Engineering
 Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them.
 A few things that define how we operate:
 One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle.

 If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack.

 We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed.

 We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job.

 We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters.

 You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure. 
 
 Our Teams 
 Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does.
 Right now, we operate across four areas:
 Compute — the foundation everything runs on: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and the deployment systems that get code from engineers' laptops to production reliably and at scale

 Storage — databases, caching, object storage, and the data infrastructure that underpins everything

 Workflows & Messaging — the systems that power Ramp's financial workflows and event-driven architecture

 Developer Infrastructure — the platform that makes every builder at Ramp faster and more autonomous: observability, cost attribution, and CI/CD systems that give teams visibility into what they build and what it costs

 
 What You'll Do 
 Production Engineers at Ramp are full software engineers who happen to specialize in infrastructure . You write production code, you own systems end-to-end, and you drive technical outcomes across the organization — not just within your team.
 As a Tech Lead & Manager, you are a hands-on player-coach : you will lead and grow a team while remaining directly engaged in the technical work. Management at Ramp does not mean stepping away from the technology or the code. You will help set direction, develop engineers, and work alongside the team to deliver consequential infrastructure outcomes.
 Day to day, you will:
 Build, coach, and grow a high-performing team. Create clarity, give direct feedback, mentor engineers, and help each person expand their technical judgment, ownership, and leadership.

 Set technical direction for your team’s domain. Identify the highest-leverage problems, define a path forward, bring the right people along, and stay engaged with the team until the work is delivered.

 Build and operate critical infrastructure across Ramp's compute, storage, messaging, and observability stack — owning the systems that handle real financial transactions at scale.

 Drive architectural change — not just flag problems. When you surface a reliability or scalability issue, you own the path forward: you propose the solution, find the owners across engineering, and stay in until it's resolved.

 Partner with product teams at the design phase — reviewing architectures, embedding golden paths, and making it easy to build correctly the first time.

 Build Ramp's next level of scale — you'll be a hands-on contributor to the most consequential infrastructure shift happening right now: our move to a cellular architecture, enabling Ramp to scale, reach international markets, operate in highly regulated and constrained environments (e.g. FedRAMP), and deliver on enterprise-grade SLAs.

 Enable AI-native engineering — as Ramp builds increasingly AI-powered products, PE is the team that makes sure the platform can support them. You'll proactively partner with product teams on AI infrastructure patterns, define the golden paths that turn one-off solutions into reusable foundations, and stay ahead of emerging challenges before they become blockers.

 Build developer tooling and self-service infrastructure — so that other teams can answer their own questions (cost, performance, reliability) without involving PE.

 Participate in on-call rotation — and more importantly, use every incident as a signal to eliminate the root cause, not just resolve the symptom.

 Lead across the company — PE doesn't just review designs or show up when called. We proactively initiate cross-team architectural reviews, and we take full ownership of company-wide reliability and scalability initiatives: identifying the problem, proposing the solution, aligning the stakeholders, and staying in until it's done.

 
 What We Look For 
 We don't hire for a checklist. We hire for the instincts that make someone exceptional on this team.
 The mindset we're looking for: 
 You love building teams, mentoring engineers, and helping people grow—and you are equally energized by writing code, reviewing designs, and digging into complex distributed systems.

 You are a true player-coach. You know when to coach, delegate, and create space for others to lead; you also know when your direct technical involvement will create the most leverage.

 You can set a technical direction, bring people along, and then lock in with the team to make it happen.

 You do not believe managing engineers means stepping away from the technology or the code.

 You can't walk past something broken without wanting to fix it — and you don't stop at the workaround. You find the root cause and eliminate the class of problem.

 You think in systems, not tasks. You understand that "fixing the bug" is step one; making it so the bug can't happen again is the job.

 You move with urgency but without chaos. You know when to go fast and when to slow down and do it right.

 You treat product teams as your users. You build for them, communicate with them proactively, and measure success by how much faster they can ship. But you're also an owner — when something is broken or blocking, you don't wait to be asked. We win when our customers win.

 You leave things better than you found them. Every system you touch, every process you encounter — you move it forward. Not always dramatically, but always directionally. You picked it up in a certain state; you leave it in a better one.

 You are equally comfortable reading a database query plan, reviewing a system design doc, writing a Terraform module, and jumping into an incident at 2am.

 Experience profile: 
 8+ years of software engineering experience, including a track record of shipping high-quality architectures for critical systems.

 Staff+-level technical leadership: experience setting technical direction and leading complex, multi-quarter technical initiatives from ambiguous problems through durable production outcomes.

 Experience managing, mentoring, and developing engineers. You create clarity, give direct feedback, and help people grow in technical judgment, scope, and leadership.

 A sustained hands-on engineering track record. You are comfortable writing and reviewing production code, evaluating system designs, debugging incidents, and making difficult technical tradeoffs.

 Hands-on experience building and operating distributed systems at production scale.

 Strong software engineering fundamentals — you write clean, well-tested, production-ready code and set that standard for the team.

 Experience with at least one major cloud provider (AWS preferred).

 Familiarity with observability and reliability practices, including SLOs, error budgets, alerting, dashboards, and incident response.

 Track record of delivering through cross-functional coordination: aligning stakeholders, unblocking teams, and staying accountable for the outcome.

 Comfortable using AI tooling and coding agents as part of your everyday engineering workflow — and helping a team use them to move faster and think bigger.

 Bonus (not required): 
 Experience with cellular or multi-tenant architecture patterns

 Prior work on workflow orchestration systems (Temporal)

 Contributions to developer experience or internal platform tooling

 Experience in fintech, payments, or regulated industries (FedRAMP, SOC 2)

 About the Role 
 We're looking for a Senior Corporate Paralegal to join Ramp's Legal team and own the operational backbone of how we govern and structure the company. Ramp runs a growing portfolio of U.S. and non-U.S. entities — including regulated and licensed subsidiaries — across a business that ships constantly and raises, acquires, and expands on short notice. You will be the person who keeps that machinery accurate, current, and audit-ready.

 What You'll Do

 Employment support: Support employment- and immigration-related requests and filings.

description:

Our backend stack includes Python, Go, Rust, PostgreSQL, DynamoDB, Redis, and Kubernetes - built alongside dedicated in-house AI and search interfaces.

 Design and implement highly available, high-performance, and scalable systems.

 Design and implement various tools for other engineers helping them with their day to day job.

 Design and implement CI/CD and other workflows to enhance stability, robustness and speed of iteration.

 Maintain and optimize key-value and relational databases.

 Scale and load balance web server backends to meet rapidly changing needs.

 Monitor systems and applications, proactively identifying and resolving reliability, scalability, or performance issues.

 Develop monitoring tools, alerts, and dashboards to provide visibility into system health and performance.

 
 Qualifications: 
 Strong experience with cloud infrastructure built on AWS.

 Proficient in database management and caching strategies.

 Excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting skills, with the ability to analyze, debug, and resolve complex technical issues.

 Experience working with containers (Docker, Kubernetes) and orchestration tools.

 Excellent communication and collaboration skills.

 Experience with Python and Terraform.

 3+ years of DevOps/SRE/System Administration experience.

About the job 
 We're looking for an experienced Global Mobility Lead to build and run the programs that help employees join, move, and work across borders. You will own our mobility policies, immigration casework, and vendor relationships, and partner with Legal, Finance, and People Ops to make cross-border moves clear, compliant, and well supported.
 
 What you’ll own 
 
 Global mobility
 Own the mobility policy suite end to end: relocation, permanent transfers, short-term and long-term international assignments, remote/cross-border work arrangements, and business travel thresholds.

 Run individual mobility cases from scoping to landing: package design, cost estimates, immigration sequencing, tax and social-security implications, payroll setup, relocation logistics, and post-arrival support.

 Manage employment-based immigration casework in partnership with outside counsel: H-1B (including cap-subject and change-of-employer/AC21 timing), L-1, TN, E-3, O-1, F-1 OPT/CPT, and employer-sponsored permanent residence. Own the internal timeline, the start-date reality check, and the manager/candidate communication.

 Own daily immigration intake and case execution, including employer questionnaires, supporting documents, employment verification letters, signatures, counsel follow ups, and case closure.

 Own right-to-work compliance across jurisdictions: I-9 and E-Verify in the US, Home Office share-code checks in the UK, and equivalent checks in our EU and other markets.

 Decide and document the entity/employment model for each new market (direct entity, EOR, or non-resident payroll registration) with Finance and Legal.

 Own our mobility vendor stack (immigration counsel, relocation, tax, EOR/global payroll): scope, SLAs, cost, and performance.

 Model and track mobility cost, including sponsorship and premium-processing fees, so leadership can make go/no-go calls with real numbers, and obtain and document required approvals before committing sponsorship or spend

 Data and systems
 Build the tracking layer: mobility case pipeline, immigration deadlines and expirations, compensation comparisons, etc.

 Stand up mobility dashboards: case volume, cycle time, cost per move, band penetration, offer-to-band variance, and equity-gap trend.

 Write the employee-facing documentation so moves and pay decisions are predictable and explainable, not one-off negotiations.

 
 What we’re looking for 
 Required
 6+ years of experience in global mobility, with real ownership of cross-border moves and immigration casework, not just vendor hand-offs.

 Working fluency in US employment-based immigration and at least one other major jurisdiction’s work-authorization regime (UK, EU, or Canada).

 Strong analytical skills: comfortable in spreadsheets and HRIS reporting, able to build a defensible model and explain the assumptions behind it.

 Judgment about risk. You know when to escalate to Legal, when to flag classification or permanent-establishment exposure, and how to say no clearly.

 Excellent written communication: you’ll draft policies, verification letters, offer rationales, and executive-facing recommendations.

 Comfort with ambiguity, high volume, and shifting priorities.

About Ramp 
 Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

 Explore our Engineering Blog & Emerging Talent Blog to learn more about how we build at Ramp and what it’s like to start your career here.
 
 About the Role

job_title: Member of Technical Staff, AI Products (Early Career - Industry)
description:
NOTE ON ELIGIBILITY : this role is for industry candidates already working in software engineering for the past 1+ years. New grads and current students should NOT apply to this role (instead, visit pplx.ai/newgrads ). 
 
 About the role
 In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. Millions of people now use Perplexity to transform knowledge into action, through Search, Comet, and Computer. Product Engineering owns those experiences end to end, from the interface a user touches to the search and model calls behind it, on top of roughly 200M queries a day and a 200B+ URL index.
 This is a full stack role in the truest sense. There are no frontend or backend lanes here, and no one waits for a ticket before starting. It suits people who love to build and want the room to do it. What you have shipped and how quickly you learn tell us far more than years on a resume or where you went to school.
 
 What you will do
 Own a user-facing surface end to end, from the interaction, design, and frontend through the application logic, APIs, data models, and the search or model calls behind them.

 Ship to production continuously. New engineers typically have code in front of users in their first week.

 Build with AI as a primary tool, not a novelty. We expect you to use agents and coding models aggressively to move faster, and to have sound judgment about when their output is wrong.

 Turn ambiguous product ideas into working prototypes, then use real usage data and evals to decide what survives.

 Raise the quality bar on reliability, latency, and craft for the surfaces you own.

 Work directly with designers, PMs, and research engineers, without unnecessary process in between.

 What we look for
 1+ years of professional software engineering experience, or a track record of strong internships where you shipped production code at scale.

 Strong in at least one backend language, such as Python or Go, with real experience across services, APIs, and relational data modeling. Comfortable working in React and TypeScript on the frontend.

 Real evidence of building: production work you understand in depth, shipped side projects with actual users, meaningful open-source contributions, hackathon wins, or research you turned into working software.

 Comfort with ambiguity and an instinct to start building incrementally rather than wait for a spec.

 Hands-on experience with AI products, with opinions about their rough edges and what that means for the product you are building.

 Nice to have
 Experience with our stack: React or Next.js, Python, Go, PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker, AWS. You will not be expected to know all of it on day one.

 Experience building on top of LLMs: AI orchestration, RAG, evals, agents, tool use.

 Product taste. You can tell a good interface from a bad one and explain how to improve it.

 A public track record we can read, such as GitHub, a technical blog, or a demo we can try.

Fuse Energy is an energy startup on a mission to make energy abundant and affordable, fast. We combine first-principles thinking with cutting-edge technology to build a radically better energy system.

 We're hiring an O&M Technician to carry out planned and corrective maintenance across our Solar PV and BESS sites. You'll be based on site day to day and act as a key point of contact for operational matters as they come up, working closely with subcontractors, landowners and clients where needed. You'll bring hands-on experience in solar PV, BESS or electrical maintenance, and you'll report into the Operations and Maintenance Manager.
 
 Responsibilities 
 Planned and Corrective Maintenance 
 Carry out planned preventative maintenance (PPM) across Solar PV and BESS sites
 Perform corrective maintenance and repairs on electrical and mechanical systems
 Complete routine servicing in line with maintenance schedules and manufacturer requirements
 Ensure all maintenance work is completed safely and to company standards
 Fault-Finding and Performance Monitoring 
 Conduct site inspections, testing and diagnostic fault-finding
 Identify and resolve equipment issues affecting performance or availability, including underperforming PV arrays, inverters and BESS systems
 Support rapid response to site breakdowns and system failures
 Escalate complex technical issues to senior engineering or operations teams where required
 Identify recurring issues and feed them back into the maintenance strategy to reduce downtime and improve reliability
 Commissioning and Project Handover Support

 Assist with site inspections, testing and energisation during handover
 Help ensure assets are installed, tested and operating in line with design and specification requirements

 Carry out all work in line with HSE procedures, RAMS and company safety standards
 Always follow safe working practices on high-voltage and construction sites
 Support site compliance with contractual, regulatory and operational requirements
 Report hazards, incidents and near misses in line with company processes
 Reporting and Documentation 
 Complete maintenance reports, service records and job documentation accurately and on time
 Record site activities, findings and corrective actions clearly and consistently
 Support accurate tracking of maintenance history and asset condition
 Stakeholder and Contractor Coordination 
 Coordinate with subcontractors and external service providers when required
 Maintain good communication with site teams, internal stakeholders and project personnel
 Support interaction with landowners and clients during site activities where necessary
 Requirements 
 3+ years' experience working within Solar PV, BESS, electrical maintenance or a similar technical environment
 Electrical qualifications such as NVQ, City & Guilds, HNC/HND, or equivalent are preferred
 Basic understanding of solar PV systems, inverters, transformers, switchgear and monitoring systems
 Ability to read and interpret technical drawings and electrical schematics
 Familiarity with health and safety standards and safe systems of work, including [HV authorisation / competency requirement, confirm with HSE]
 Full UK driving licence and willingness to travel to sites
 Good communication and problem-solving skills
 Comfortable working independently and as part of a wider team
 Previous experience in renewable energy or utility-scale infrastructure is desirable but not essential

 Biannual bonus scheme
 Fully expensed tech to match your needs

Perplexity is looking for a detail-oriented Payroll Analyst to join our growing Finance and Accounting team. You will partner closely with the Payroll Manager to keep US and international payroll accurate, compliant, and timely as the company scales through rapid hiring, global expansion, and increasing complexity in equity and benefits administration.
  
 This is a hands-on role with real ownership from day one, working closely with People Operations, Accounting, Tax, and Equity. The ideal candidate combines strong payroll and systems expertise with sharp attention to detail, a service-oriented approach, and the ability to bring structure to a fast-moving environment.
  
 Responsibilities 
  
 US and international payroll processing: Own day-to-day processing support for US multi-state semi-monthly payroll and assist with international payroll cycles across approximately 16 countries, working primarily in Rippling.

 Global contractor payroll: Run the monthly global contractor payroll cycle, including timecard submission tracking, manager approval follow-up, and on-schedule contractor payments.

 Pre- and post-payroll audits: Reconcile benefit deductions, 401(k) deferrals, and employer match against payroll journals and deductions exports; flag and resolve discrepancies before paychecks post.

 State tax account administration: Support state-level employer tax account registration and maintenance (SUI and withholding) as the company grows into new states, including migration of legacy accounts inherited from prior PEO arrangements.

 Benefits and 401(k) support: Assist with 401(k) and benefits administration, including contribution monitoring, HCE and nondiscrimination testing support, and COBRA offboarding notices.

 Equity payroll reporting: Support equity and stock-exercise payroll reporting by tracking Carta exercise data, applying correct NSO/ISO tax treatment, and preparing payroll-side entries at quarter-end cutoffs.

 Reimbursements and systems integration: Manage the Rippling-to-NetSuite reimbursement approval chain, ensuring expense reimbursements route and post correctly across systems.

 Employee support: Serve as a first point of contact for employee payroll inquiries, resolving routine questions and escalating complex cases with context.

 Close and compliance support: Maintain clean, audit-ready documentation and support quarter-end and year-end close activities, including W-2s, ACA reporting, 401(k) true-ups, and year-end reconciliations.

 Process improvement: Identify and help implement process improvements that reduce manual work and strengthen controls as payroll volume and jurisdictional complexity increase.

  
 Requirements 
  
 4+ years of hands-on payroll experience, ideally including multi-state US payroll; international or contractor payroll exposure is a plus.

 Experience establishing and managing US state agency accounts, including troubleshooting agency mailings and invoices for payment, and related account maintenance.

 Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
 The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
 We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.
 The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
 If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.
 
 About the Role 
 Technical Consultants are on the frontlines working to establish partnerships with Ramp customers, and act as a liaison between customers and our internal technical teams. You’ll be partnering with Customer Activation & Account Management teams to identify, prioritize and build financial solutions for new and existing customers so that Ramp continues to scale with their needs.
 You will act as the technical and financial subject matter expert for our customers, and design solutions that address the customer’s needs through Ramp and partner integrations. You will partner with Post-Sales teams to drive Product, Design and Engineering teams’ roadmaps to evolve Ramp to better serve our customers at scale and offer increasingly higher value to the customers.
 You will define the customer’s financial & technical success criteria from onboarding through activation and expansion. You will represent Product, Design and Engineering externally and will operate with deep conviction and understanding of Ramp’s technical capabilities. The role requires technical skills necessary to understand and educate on robust accounting features, and integrate them across all the touchpoints and surface area of a customer.
 What You’ll Do 
 Act as a technical advisor to customers and Ramp’s internal teams while supporting high-value implementations and expansion opportunities by guiding integration, configuration, and system design

 Partner with Customer Activation and Account Management teams to assess customer requirements and propose scalable solutions; particularly involving ERP, HRIS, and API integrations

 Collaborate with onboarding specialists and implementation leads to support technical workstreams (not run them), ensuring faster time-to-value and customer success

 Work with customers to problem-solve technical hurdles and propose effective product implementations for each customer with a deep understanding of the full range of integration and configuration options

 Participate in technical discovery to understand customer systems and workflows, and recommend best-fit Ramp architecture. This includes when and how to use Ramp’s API

 Be a subject matter expert across our HRIS and Accounting integration partners, partnering with Sales, Product and partners to advocate for integration development in-line with customer needs

 Troubleshoot integration blockers and guide customers through complex configuration decisions without writing code directly

 Contribute to internal documentation and tooling that scales Ramp’s ability to support integration use cases across a growing customer base

 Influence Ramp’s product roadmap by channeling customer pain points and feedback to the Product and Engineering teams

 What You Need 
 Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, finance, business, or a related field

 4+ years in technical consulting, solutions engineering, implementation, or a similar customer-facing technical role, ideally in a SaaS or fintech environment

 Familiarity with ERP systems (e.g. NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Microsoft Dynamics, Oracle Fusion) and finance/accounting workflows

 Comfort working with APIs, integration logic, and system architecture and being able to explain those concepts to finance and operations stakeholders

 Strong communication skills: able to translate complex technical solutions into business value, guide customers toward scalable approaches, and diplomatically steer conversations when requests are misaligned with best practices or product capabilities

 Collaborative mindset and ability to work cross-functionally with Sales, Customer Success, Product, and Engineering

 Exceptional organization and problem-solving skills, with a bias toward action and a high level of ownership

 Thrives in ambiguity and fast-paced environments; adaptable and resourceful as we scale Ramp’s upmarket motion

The ideal candidate brings deep experience negotiating a wide range of commercial technology agreements, including infrastructure and compute procurement agreements, a strong command of data privacy and security frameworks, and the practical judgment to make principled risk calls independently. This is a high-impact, hands-on role for someone who thrives in fast-paced environments, knows how to be a true partner to the business without being a bottleneck, and is excited to help build a best-in-class legal function at one of the most consequential AI companies in the world.
 
 Responsibilities 
 Lead end-to-end drafting, review, and negotiation of commercial agreements, including MSAs, SaaS and API agreements, DPAs, partnership and reseller agreements, strategic collaboration and co-marketing agreements, procurement and vendor contracts, technology and infrastructure agreements, and IP licensing arrangements.

 Provide strategic counsel on legal risks across AI infrastructure, compute, partnerships, and enterprise deployments as the company scales.

 Qualifications

Perplexity is hiring an experienced Communications & Marketing Recruiter to help build the teams responsible for how our company and products are positioned, launched, explained, and experienced.

You will work closely with Communications and Marketing leaders to define each search, build the market, assess candidates, and close the people who can raise the quality of the work. You should be comfortable reading portfolios and writing samples, digging into campaign results, and separating individual contribution from team output.
 You will also help us use AI more effectively across recruiting. That means applying it to research, talent mapping, outreach, and workflow automation while maintaining a high bar for judgment and candidate experience.
 
 What You’ll Do 
 Own full-cycle recruiting across the Communications & Marketing team.

 Partner with Communications and Marketing leaders from intake through close. Turn early or ambiguous briefs into clear candidate profiles, interview plans, and sourcing strategies.

 Build talent maps across technology companies, consumer brands, enterprise software, media organizations, and agencies.

 Develop sourcing strategies specific to each discipline. Know where strong writers, communications operators, product marketers, and performance-minded marketers build their reputations.

 Evaluate candidates beyond titles and company names. Review portfolios and writing samples, understand campaign context, clarify individual ownership, and probe for measurable results.

 Help hiring teams build structured work-sample and portfolio reviews that reflect the actual work of each role.

 Represent Perplexity clearly and credibly. Explain the product, the pace of the company, and the opportunity without relying on a generic AI pitch.

 Run a thoughtful candidate process from first conversation through close, including senior candidates with competing offers and high expectations for the recruiting experience.

 Track pipeline health and search performance, identify gaps early, and adjust the strategy before a search stalls.

 What You Bring 
 7+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience, including meaningful depth across Communications and Marketing.

 A track record of partnering closely with senior Communications or Marketing leaders on important and difficult searches.

 Strong functional judgment. You understand the differences between product marketing, communications, editorial, brand, growth, and field marketing, including which backgrounds transfer well between them.

 Comfort evaluating portfolios, writing samples, campaign work, and business results alongside the hiring team.

 Strong writing and communication skills. You can sharpen a search brief, write credible outreach, and communicate clearly with candidates and executives.

 The ability to manage several distinct searches without giving candidates or hiring teams a generic experience.

 About the role
 Corporate Security at Ramp owns the security of our internal environment: the device fleet, the identity and access layer, and the AI tools employees use for their work. We are hiring a Systems Engineer to build and operate the controls across these systems.

 3–5 years of experience in Client Platform Engineer/Endpoint Engineering, Identity Access & Management, or Corporate Security

We’re looking for a Senior Cinematographer to define how Perplexity looks on film. Working with the Creative Director and Video Lead, you’ll translate our visual identity into a practical cinematographic language, then bring it to life across the team’s day-to-day output.

 This is a hands-on role. One day you’re shooting a candid office moment or executive interview with a small kit; the next, you’re leading a full camera and lighting crew on a brand film. Most of your time goes to prepping, testing, lighting, and shooting.

 You’ll also help build and run our in-house studio, from selecting gear and designing flexible lighting setups to keeping the space production-ready. When turnaround is tight, you’ll support media management and light editing.

 You’ll report to the Video Lead and work closely with the Video Producer, Brand Lead, designers, motion designers, Growth, Comms, Product Marketing, and external production partners. The Producer and Video Lead handle crewing, budgets, schedules, and logistics so you can stay focused on production and craft. However, you should think like a storyteller, not just a technician, bringing your own ideas for how to show our product and people more vividly through moodboards, shot lists, storyboards, and a willingness to experiment.
 
 What You'll Do 
 Partner with the Creative Director and Video Lead to define and evolve Perplexity’s cinematographic language, and turn it into repeatable approaches for lighting, lensing, composition, movement, and color.

 Shoot and light a steady mix of day-to-day content: candid office moments, executive interviews, product demos, social, events, and documentary stories.

 Lead cinematography on brand films, campaigns, partnerships, and launches.

 Scale to the work: operate solo with a minimal kit, lead a small crew, or help build a full camera, lighting, grip, team (with help from producers).

 Bring storytelling ideas to the table through moodboards, shot lists, storyboards, and experimentation.

 Own camera, lighting, and movement decisions from creative development through capture: build packages, run tests and tech scouts, and solve constraints before the shoot.

 Recommend crew and equipment for each production and lead the camera and lighting departments on set. Producers handle budgets, schedules, contracts, and logistics.

 Help design, build, and run the in-house studio, including lighting, audio, grip, and monitoring.

 Own the team’s gear: recommend, purchase, organize, and maintain it, with ready-to-shoot packages so no setup gets rebuilt from scratch.

 Handle color grading in DaVinci Resolve, and support selects, stringouts, and light edits when turnaround is tight.

 Keep the visual standard high across formats and crew sizes without overbuilding.

 What We're Looking For 
 6+ years as a cinematographer or DP across branded, commercial, documentary, and interview work.

 A standout reel showing visual authorship, lighting craft, camera movement, and an eye for honest, unscripted moments.

 A strong point of view, paired with the sensitivity to work within and strengthen an existing brand.

 Deep command of camera systems, lenses, exposure, color pipelines, lighting, grip, and on-set monitoring.

 Genuinely hands-on: equally comfortable building a camera, shaping light, operating, troubleshooting, and leading a crew.

 The judgment to make premium images under real constraints, solo with a small kit or leading a full production.

 Strong pre-production instincts: turning a creative idea into a technically sound, right-sized plan.

 Experience briefing and leading freelance crews and vendors on set, and managing professional production equipment.

 Working proficiency in DaVinci Resolve for color grading, selects, and light edits.

 Collaborative and low-ego. You bring a strong opinion, take direction, and solve problems with partners.

 Comfortable moving fast in an ambiguous, high-output environment without compromising craft, safety, or footage.

 Based in or able to work on-site in San Francisco, with flexibility for travel and long shoot days.

 Nice to Have 
 A strong Bay Area and Los Angeles network of camera, lighting, grip, sound, production, and rental partners.

 Experience within an in-house brand studio at a technology or consumer company.

 Strong documentary instincts and experience working with founders, executives, talent, or people who are not professional performers.

 Experience with multi-camera interviews, live events, tabletop or product cinematography, motion-control systems, or virtual production.

 Color-grading experience and a strong understanding of how capture decisions carry through finishing and delivery.

Perplexity's API Platform brings our work in AI, search, and agent orchestration to developers. Our customers range from AI-native startups to some of the world's largest technology companies. Working with them, alongside our own developments in building Perplexity’s core application gives our team direct exposure to how search, models, and tools are used to build and scale AI-native products and applications.
 
 About this role
 We are looking for a technically fluent Customer Success Manager to help our API customers succeed and shape how we support them as the business grows. You will own a portfolio of customers, understand what they are building, and help them move from evaluation to production and broader adoption.
 
 Alongside your accounts, you will lead projects such as product and endpoint migrations, customer enablement, and communications for product updates and incidents. You will work directly with customers developing AI products and with the engineers building the APIs they depend on. As an early member of the team, you will help shape our customer success programs and bring what you learn from customers into product decisions.
 
 Responsibilities
 Own customer relationships across onboarding, adoption, retention, and expansion, building trust with developers, technical leaders, and business stakeholders.

 Understand each customer's use case, integration, and success criteria. Help them evaluate the APIs, resolve adoption barriers, and establish a path to production.

 Use account and product usage data to identify declining adoption, technical risks, and growth opportunities, then work with customers on specific next steps.

 Investigate technical questions using API documentation, sample requests, and usage data. Coordinate with Engineering and Support on deeper issues and keep customers informed through resolution.

 Lead customer-facing programs such as endpoint migrations, product rollouts, and enablement. Define milestones, coordinate internal owners, and track customer readiness and completion.

 Manage customer communications for product changes, deprecations, and outages, partnering with technical teams to provide accurate updates and clear guidance.

 Build and improve the API customer success playbook, including onboarding, account reviews, customer health signals, escalation paths, and sales-to-CS handoffs.

 Partner with Sales and account owners on renewals and expansion, using adoption, consumption, and business outcomes to demonstrate value and surface risks early.

 Bring customer feedback into product planning and work with Developer Relations and Support on documentation and enablement that address recurring needs.

 What we're looking for
 4+ years of experience in customer success, technical account management, solutions engineering, or a related customer-facing role at a technology company.

 Technical fluency: comfortable reading API documentation, making API requests, interpreting responses and errors, and discussing integration questions with developers.

 A track record of driving adoption, retention, or growth across a portfolio of customers, with clear ownership of follow-through.

 Experience creating or improving a customer program, playbook, or cross-functional process, not only operating an established one.

 Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain technical issues clearly and communicate carefully when facts are still developing.

 Sound judgment in balancing account needs with strategic projects, setting priorities, and moving work forward without a detailed brief.

 Nice to have
 Experience with APIs, developer tools, cloud infrastructure, or usage-based products.

 Familiarity with AI applications, search, retrieval, or agents, including how customers evaluate quality, latency, and cost.

 Working knowledge of Python or SQL for reproducing issues, analyzing usage, or automating recurring work.

Fuse is an AI-first energy company on a mission to make energy abundant and affordable, fast. We combine first-principles thinking with cutting-edge technology to build a radically better energy system.
 We've raised over $200M from top-tier investors including Balderton, Lakestar, Accel, Creandum, Lowercarbon, Ribbit, 20VC, Hummingbird and Collaborative Fund, alongside strategic angels including Nico Rosberg and GPs behind Meta, Revolut, Spotify and Uber.
 We're building a fully integrated energy company: developing our own solar, batteries and other generation projects, building our own hardware, improving and developing grid infrastructure, trading power in real time, and installing distributed energy in homes. By selling directly to consumers, we cut out the middleman, lower costs and pass the savings on to our customers.
 We're hiring a Regulatory & Compliance Analyst to help us navigate the regulatory landscape as we scale. The role sits in our Regulatory & External Affairs team, working directly with our Head of Regulatory & External Affairs across everything from Ofgem submissions to government engagement. You'll have real ownership from day one.
 
 Resposibilities
 Take genuine ownership of regulatory workstreams end-to-end in a fast-paced environment - this is not a role where work is handed to you fully scoped
 Support compliance workstreams with supply licence obligations and industry codes, including tracking obligations and preparing submissions
 Draft responses to regulatory consultations, RFIs and stakeholder queries, and support engagement with Ofgem, DESNZ, code bodies and other industry parties
 Monitor regulatory and policy developments across the energy sector, assess their impact on Fuse, and brief internal teams on what matters and why
 Build and maintain compliance trackers, checklists and internal processes that keep the business ahead of its obligations as we grow
 Requirements 
 Bachelor's degree from a top university in policy, international relations, politics, economics, law or a similar field
 Knowledge of, or strong interest in, the UK energy industry and its regulatory framework
 Comfortable with data analytics - able to work confidently in spreadsheets
 Excellent written communication - able to draft precise, well-structured submissions and correspondence for regulators and government
 Thrives with high ownership
 Highly organised, with the ability to juggle multiple deadlines and workstreams without dropping anything
 Benefits 
 Competitive salary 
 Biannual bonus scheme
 Fully expensed tech to match your needs
 Private health insurance
 Breakfast and dinner allowance for office-based employees
 
 As we hire globally, benefits vary by location.

job_title: Member of Technical Staff (Applied AI Engineer, Agent Capabilities)
description:
Perplexity Computer is one of the defining products of the new era of agentic AI. Millions of people use Perplexity to transform knowledge into action, and the Agent Capabilities team sits at the intersection of frontier AI research and product innovation, building the foundations that shape how users and agents solve increasingly complex tasks.
 
 As every major breakthrough in AI models creates new possibilities, the Agent Capabilities team is responsible for turning frontier AI breakthroughs into reusable product capabilities. We are often the first to evaluate emerging model capabilities, determine where they create real user value, and transform them into reliable, scalable, high quality experiences for both users and agents. This is a highly leveraged role with broad ownership at the intersection of frontier AI research, agent systems, platform engineering, and product innovation.
 
 Tech Stack : Python | Go | Rust | PostgreSQL | DynamoDB | AWS | TypeScript
 
 Why Perplexity is different
 Craftsmanship . We build high quality, tasteful products targeting both the AI native and AI curious.

 Ownership . You identify the problem, design the solution and ship it.

 Entrepreneurship . We think like founders, act with urgency, and hustle to deliver for each other and our users.

 Scholarship . Work among highly talented peers, pursuing knowledge and truth, upleveling ourselves, our teams, and our products.

 Partnership . We amplify each others' strengths, break down silos, and give selflessly to help our colleagues deliver excellence.

 
 What you'll do
 Evaluate frontier models against real user tasks, identify useful behaviors and failure modes, and turn the most promising advances into production agent systems. Own the lifecycle from rapid prototyping and evaluation through launch, monitoring, and iteration.

 Improve agents’ ability to plan, use tools, manage context, recover from errors, and complete long-running tasks reliably.

 Apply state of the art ML and LLM techniques to design scalable agent capabilities such as skills, plugins, artifact generation, tools integrate and use, auto-research, and multi-agent collaboration. Shape the architecture, abstractions, and product experiences that enable both users and agents to compose increasingly sophisticated solutions for real-world tasks.

 Own agent behavior and capabilities end-to-end, from user-facing products and interfaces to backend services. Define offline and online evaluations for task completion, correctness, safety, latency, cost, and user satisfaction. Iteratively improve across models, prompts, harnesses, and products for different problem spaces.

 Build secure, observable, and reliable agent systems, including permissions and safeguards for sensitive actions. Develop tracing, replay, and monitoring infrastructure that makes agent failures reproducible and actionable.

 Collaborate closely with PM, Data Science, Research, to identify high-impact opportunities in understanding and validating emerging model capabilities, and turn complex agent behaviors into simple, reliable product experiences.

 Apply relevant advances in models, inference, evaluation, and agent architecture when they produce measurable improvements in production performance. Set technical direction on ambiguous problems and raise the bar through design reviews, mentorship, and technical leadership.

 
 Qualifications
 Typically 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a track record of building and owning robust AI-powered, large-scale, user-facing or data-intensive products. Exceptional candidates with less experience and an outstanding record of impact are encouraged to apply.

 Strong software engineering fundamentals, with experience building and operating AI/ML products, backend services, or distributed systems at scale.

 Experience owning the AI product lifecycle, including data analysis, rigorous evaluation, production monitoring, and iterative improvement. Able to define metrics and use production data and user feedback to guide decisions.

 Practical experience in one or more relevant areas, such as agent harnesses, tool use, context engineering, model evaluation, browser automation, or long-running task execution.

 Strong product judgment and execution: you can translate ambiguous user needs into applied AI or ML problems and ship durable solutions with measurable user impact.

 Genuine interest in frontier AI capabilities, agent systems, and excitement for rapidly exploring, evaluating, and productizing new model behaviors.

 
 Nice to have
 Experience with LLM context engineering or harness engineering, experience with subagents, coding assistants, long-running or autonomous task execution.

 Deep familiarity with the strengths and limitations of current model families across reasoning, tool use, context management, and long-horizon tasks.

 Experience building agent permissions, safeguards, evaluation infrastructure, or production observability systems.

 Experience with mid-training, post-training, or reinforcement learning for frontier or open-source models, along with a strong understanding of model strengths and limitations across reasoning, tool use, context management, and long-horizon tasks.

 AI/ML research experience demonstrated through publications, open-source contributions, or other meaningful research impact.

 Time spent at a fast-growing startup or on a high-ownership engineering team.

About Ramp 
 Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
 The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
 We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.
 The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
 If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.
 
 About the role
 Ramp is building its UK partnerships ecosystem, and we're looking for a Channel Partner Manager who can turn relationships across a myriad of industries into meaningful customer opportunities. This is a generalist role for someone who can see where a partnership makes sense, move quickly, and build momentum across a varied partner portfolio.

You'll identify how and where Ramp can create value for a prospective partner's customer base, then carry the relationship through to qualified introductions and customer adoption. You'll learn what uniquely motivates each partner and turn early success into a repeatable flywheel of referrals. Some relationships will need to be built from the ground up; others will need sharper activation and follow-through. The mix will evolve, so you should be comfortable moving between different partner models while staying focused on commercial outcomes.

You'll work closely with Ramp's UK Sales team and colleagues in Partnerships, Marketing, Events, Product, and Engineering to connect the right partners and customers and make each introduction count.
 
 What you'll do
 Build and manage a varied portfolio of UK partners, adapting your approach to each relationship and industry.

 Identify how Ramp can create value for a prospective partner's customer base, then prioritize relationships with the clearest path to fast execution.

 Understand what matters to each partner and shape a referral motion that gives them a compelling reason to keep bringing relevant customers to Ramp.

 Create repeatable sources of qualified introductions through partner enablement, account mapping, joint campaigns, events, and warm networks.

 Use business communities, hospitality, and executive events when they can create relevant introductions and measurable commercial value.

 Coordinate partner introductions and follow-up with Ramp's Sales team so opportunities have a clear owner and a strong customer experience.

 Track partner activity from introduction through qualified opportunity and customer adoption; use the data to refine each motion and focus time on what works.

 Run regular partner reviews, keep commitments moving across teams, and represent Ramp credibly with partner executives and prospective customers.

 
 What you need
 5+ years of experience, including 3+ years in partnerships, business development, partner sales, account management, or commercial strategy.

 A record of building trusted senior relationships and delivering measurable commercial results through partners.

 The ability to learn different partner business models quickly, understand their customers, and spot where Ramp can create value.

 Strong commercial judgement in prioritizing prospects, shaping warm introductions, and managing opportunities with sales teams.

 Experience executing partner go-to-market activity, such as enablement, account mapping, campaigns, events, or co-sell programs.

 Comfort using performance data to assess partner activity, report results, and adjust course.

 Excellent written, verbal, and listening skills, with the ability to work across partner organizations and internal teams.

 A hands-on, organized working style that keeps multiple relationships and commitments moving at once.

 UK-based, with flexibility to travel across the UK and attend occasional evening or weekend partner events.

 
 Nice to haves
 A background in strategy consulting or investment banking.

 Experience creating B2B pipeline through partner networks, executive events, hospitality, or account-based campaigns.

 Familiarity with UK small and medium-sized businesses and the finance leaders who buy and use Ramp's products.

 Experience building a new partner motion in a growing market or adapting a successful approach to a new partner category.

 
 What success looks like
 Ramp has a prioritized UK partner portfolio with a clear customer opportunity and path to activation for each active relationship.

 Partners and Ramp teams know who owns each introduction, opportunity, and next step.

 Partner activity produces a consistent flow of relevant introductions, qualified opportunities, and customers.

 Partners continue to bring relevant referrals because the relationship creates value for their customers and for their own business.

 The strongest partner motions are repeatable, and the team has evidence to decide where to invest next.

 About the role 
 Perplexity Computer enables customers to build AI-powered workflows that navigate tools, interact with applications, and complete multi-step work. Helping organizations adopt this new way of working requires more than a product demonstration or one-time kickoff.
 Enablement Specialists design and deliver the programs that move customers from initial access to confident, sustained use.  What you'll do 
 Design customer journeys. Build onboarding and adoption programs for customers and user cohorts with different roles, goals, technical readiness, and levels of AI experience.

 Deliver high-quality enablement. Lead technical kickoffs, workshops, office hours, remote sessions, onsite programs, webinars, and train-the-trainer experiences.

 Make complex concepts accessible. Teach Computer and agentic-workflow concepts clearly to both technical and nontechnical audiences.

 Guide customers through setup. Help customers understand access, members, permissions, connectors, credits, models, initial workflows, and the practices required to get started.

 Diagnose adoption barriers. Determine whether a customer is blocked by knowledge, readiness, process, configuration, product capability, or technical complexity.

 Route complex needs well. Recognize when a question requires an Applied AI Architect, Customer Success, Support, Product, or Engineering and provide a clear handoff.

 Create scalable assets. Turn repeated onboarding and adoption needs into curricula, customer checklists, implementation guidance, lifecycle communications, videos, examples, and internal enablement.

 Use evidence to increase adoption and consumption. Segment customers by readiness and usage behavior, identify where consumption stalls, deliver targeted interventions, and measure activation, time to first value, repeat usage, sustained credit consumption, and program effectiveness.

 Build the learning loop. Bring customer patterns and feedback back to Applied AI, Product, Customer Success, Marketing, and Support.

 What we're looking for 
 The strongest Enablement Specialists can teach, diagnose, and design for scale. You should be able to run a compelling customer session, understand the technical details behind a blocker, and build a repeatable program rather than solving the same problem one customer at a time.
 Must-haves 
 4+ years in technical onboarding, customer enablement, implementation, solutions consulting, customer education, or a technically oriented Customer Success role.

 Strong facilitation and communication. You can explain complex product and AI concepts clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences.

 Technical fluency. You can guide customers through permissions, connectors, models, credits, workflows, and common integration concepts.

 Strong diagnostic judgment. You can determine whether a customer is blocked by education, readiness, process, configuration, product capability, or technical complexity.

 Data-informed growth mindset. You have used product and usage data to identify adoption gaps, trigger interventions, move customer cohorts toward sustained use, and evaluate impact.

 High ownership. You set clear expectations, improve weak processes, and operate effectively in a fast-moving environment.

 Nice-to-haves

 Background in adult learning, instructional design, customer education, or enablement operations.

 Experience using product and usage data to trigger interventions and measure activation, time to value, and sustained engagement.

 Experience developing customer-facing technical content, workshops, or certification programs.

At Perplexity, infrastructure sits on the critical path of every answer, supporting real-time search, retrieval, model serving, and agent workloads where latency, reliability, and rapid iteration directly shape the user experience. This role is for strong infrastructure engineers whose experience spans multiple domains and who are energized by cross-cutting problems that do not fit neatly within a single platform team.
 
 You do not need to be a specialist in every area. Scope ranges from owning major production systems to setting technical direction across teams, leading complex infrastructure programs, and shaping infrastructure strategy across the organization. If a specialized Cloud Infrastructure, Storage Platform, Backend Platform, Data Platform, Connector Platform, or AI Acceleration role clearly matches your expertise and interests, apply directly to it. If your experience spans several infrastructure domains or you are most energized by cross-cutting systems problems, apply here. Submit one application, and we will consider you across the Infrastructure organization.
 
 Key Responsibilities
 Own cross-cutting infrastructure problems that span compute, storage, networking, data, deployment, and reliability, including eliminating bottlenecks across retrieval and serving paths, building shared abstractions across deployment environments, and resolving failure modes that cross platform boundaries.

 Design, build, and operate distributed infrastructure supporting Perplexity’s consumer, AI, and enterprise workloads, owning systems from architecture through production operation.

 Identify gaps between existing platforms and build shared abstractions, automation, and tooling that make infrastructure easier and safer to use.

 Improve system performance, availability, scalability, and cost-efficiency across online request traffic and background workloads.

 Debug complex production issues across service and infrastructure boundaries, then turn the findings into durable architectural improvements.

 Set technical direction for complex infrastructure systems, lead high-impact programs across teams, and establish durable technical standards through collaboration with infrastructure, product, AI, and security partners.

 4+ years of professional software engineering experience building and operating production backend, platform, or distributed systems.

 A track record of owning complex production systems end to end and delivering sustained technical impact across teams.

 Strong software engineering skills in Python or other systems or backend languages such as Go, Rust, C++, or Java.

 Meaningful experience across at least two infrastructure domains, such as cloud platforms, distributed systems, Kubernetes, storage, databases, networking, data systems, developer infrastructure, or production reliability.

 Ability to develop depth quickly in unfamiliar systems, reason across software and infrastructure layers, and drive production incidents from diagnosis through durable resolution.

 If you’re excited about this role, we encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn’t match every qualification listed above.
