About Ramp 
 Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
 The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
 We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

 About the Role 
 Over the past few years at Ramp, we've reimagined how businesses manage spend, and the backbone of that vision is Procure-to-Pay. The P2P team builds the systems that connect vendors, invoices, and payments into one seamless, automated flow. It's where billions of dollars move through our platform, and every line of code matters.
 
 We're looking for a backend engineer who loves complex systems, obsesses over correctness, and wants to shape how money moves in modern finance software. You'll help design and scale the infrastructure that powers our payment rails, ensures auditability across products, and unlocks the next wave of AI-driven automation.
 
 It's a chance to work on systems that actually move money, with a team that cares deeply about precision, reliability, and scale. The problems are tough, the stakes are high, and the impact is massive.
 
 What You'll Do 
 Design and build core P2P systems, from invoice ingestion and approval workflows to payment orchestration and reconciliation logic.

 Enable AI agents to classify, validate, and process invoices automatically, reducing manual review and accelerating financial close.

 Own backend services that process large volumes of financial events across Bill Pay, Procurement, and Treasury.

 Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Finance, and Data to translate accounting and compliance policies into robust, testable code.

 Extend Ramp’s financial ledger to handle new transaction types, international payments, and automated audit trails.

 Drive technical excellence around reliability, observability, and data integrity in systems where correctness directly impacts financial reporting.

 Continuously improve developer tooling and internal APIs that make P2P data accessible across Ramp’s product ecosystem.

 
 What You Need 
 3+ years of backend engineering experience, ideally in fintech, payments, or transactional systems.

 Proven experience designing and maintaining data-intensive distributed systems with strong consistency and auditability requirements.

 Deep knowledge of Python (or a comparable backend language) and SQL.

 Comfort building event-driven systems and scaling high-volume, low-latency architectures.

 Strong system design and debugging skills; you care about correctness as much as speed.

 Ability to work closely with finance, risk, and product stakeholders to translate business rules into software logic.

 Passion for building systems that are precise, reliable, and extensible as Ramp scales globally.

 
 Nice to Have 
 Experience with accounts payable, payments, or reconciliation systems.

 Familiarity with accounting or ERP integrations (e.g. NetSuite, QuickBooks, Oracle).

About Ramp 
 Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
 The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
 We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.
 The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
 If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.
 
 About the Role 
 Ramp's Enterprise CSMs don't manage accounts — they transform how companies run their finances. This is a role for people who have been inside large organizations when change was hard, who speak the language of a CFO, and who already use AI the way surgeons use instruments: not occasionally, not as an experiment, but as the default way they work. You'll be embedded in Ramp's enterprise accounts, responsible for driving genuine workflow transformation — not just onboarding completion.
 
 What You'll Do 
 Lead enterprise customers through the full transformation journey — from implementation through agentic workflow adoption — with clear accountability for time-to-value and measurable business outcomes

This fluency is what lets you speak credibly to Controllers and finance ops teams about how Ramp fits into their existing systems of record.

The opportunity
 
We are looking for a Senior Platform Engineer profile who will design and implement the Pigment infrastructure for tomorrow. Pigment is a technically challenging platform. It calculates and synchronizes large datasets that must be updated in real-time. Data comes from client models that can be up to billions of rows. This data can be pivoted, transformed, and aggregated on-demand through our formula engine while rendering live on our front end.
Here are the challenges to be tackled as a Senior Platform Engineer:
Define and build the infrastructure needed to answer our performance challenges, automate it, and make it scalable. In particular, ensure that the infrastructure scales in and out according to the platform usage.
Secure high availability and redundancy of the Pigment platform.
Ensure that the platform’s performance and correctness are monitored accordingly, spread observability best practices across the engineering team.
Participate in incident response.
Accompany Pigment geographical expansion as the company grows and we sign clients overseas.
Work with our security team on the implementation of their roadmap when related to infrastructure and development pipelines (code repository, credentials management, ...)
Continuously chase inefficiencies within our development practices and pipelines. Seek improvement and automation wherever possible. Drive change across the software engineering team.
In addition to Platform responsibilities, we expect you to contribute to software development activities. This is not limited to scripting and automations - we expect to you to be fully capable of reading and writing code. We believe Senior Platform Engineers should collaborate closely with software engineers, fostering a shared understanding of day-to-day challenges, rather than operating in separate teams. Last but not least, you will not be alone! You will be part of an SRE team.
 
Our Engineering team
Our Engineering team is responsible for developing our SaaS platform and building a comprehensive and user-friendly product.
Pigment engineers participate in the entire application development lifecycle, focusing on design, coding, and keeping the production platform up and running. They can be specialized, but there is no strict separation between the infrastructure, backend, and the frontend.
 
We value user-centricity and pragmatism: we choose the most relevant tools for the problem we have to solve, understanding the strengths and constraints of each technology.
Our engineering culture also values curiosity, humility, trust, ownership and team spirit.
 
Technical stack:
Kubernetes (GKE, hosted on Google Cloud Platform): hosting all our infrastructure components except some PostgreSQL hosts, hosted on Google Cloud SQL
Terraform: all our infrastructure is managed via this infrastructure as code (creation of GKE clusters, Google Cloud SQL databases, GCS buckets, IAM permissions...)
Databases: PostgreSQL (CloudSQL and CloudNativePG), SingleStore, ElasticSearch
RabbitMQ: queuing system
Temporal.io: workflow automation platform
Others: ArgoCD, Istio, Vault, Github, Docker (for local development)
Backend: Microservices written in C# ASP.NET Core 8 (running exclusively on Linux) & Golang
Frontend: React + Typescript, Jest, Cypress, Vite...
 
Who you are
 
More than knowledge of a specific cloud provider, language, or automation framework, we are looking for great engineering skills: the ability to translate product requirements into an elegant and simple architecture, and then make sure our product runs well on it.
In any case, you have:
Experience as a software engineer & Platform Engineer. Hands on coding is a must for this role.
Experience with a container orchestration platform (Kubernetes is a plus)
Experience with a public cloud provider, GCP is a plus
Proven experience in software developments with languages such as C#, Java, C++, Golang, Rust, JavaScript, Python, or Ruby (this list is not exhaustive).
Experience with observability tools (e.g. Datadog, Prometheus, ELK, Jaeger...)
Great team spirit with a problem-solving attitude.
A good dose of humility and the willingness to grow (no matter your seniority!).
Fluency in English

Interested in recruitment, technology, and what it takes to build great teams?
Join Pigment and work alongside our three-person in-house Tech Talent Acquisition team, helping us attract talent for our Engineering and Product teams. You’ll learn how to identify and engage candidates, build your interviewing skills, and contribute to projects that improve the way we hire.

Find and engage tech talent
Learn about our Engineering and Product roles and understand hiring needs alongside recruiters and hiring managers.
Identify potential candidates through LinkedIn, relevant communities, and other sourcing channels.
Write personalised outreach that sparks conversations and helps candidates understand our opportunities.
Build and maintain talent pools, keeping candidate information and follow-ups up to date.
Track response rates and candidate progression to understand what works and refine your approach.
Develop your recruitment and interviewing skills
Shadow recruiters and participate in hiring discussions to learn how we assess candidates.
Review applications and help identify relevant profiles using agreed criteria.
Depending on your interests and progress, gradually conduct initial interviews with coaching from the team.
Help keep candidates informed and supported throughout their recruitment journey.
Contribute to or own projects that interest you

Employer branding: help tell the stories of our Engineering and Product teams through employee content, social media, and tech events.
Campus program: develop school and university relationships, coordinate student events, and help organise internship and apprenticeship recruitment campaigns.
Recruitment improvements: test new sourcing approaches, improve candidate communication, or contribute to our referral programme.
AI and recruitment tools: explore practical ways to support research, outreach preparation, and everyday workflows, and share what you learn with the team.

Recruitment interests you: you enjoy meeting people, understanding their motivations, and helping them explore opportunities.
You’re curious about tech: you want to understand what Engineering and Product teams do and the skills they need.
You’re interested in AI: you’re keen to explore new tools and think critically about where they can be useful.
You enjoy projects: you like turning ideas into concrete actions and following through.
You’re a curious learner: you ask questions, welcome feedback, and take the initiative to explore unfamiliar topics.
You work well in a team: you share ideas, communicate openly, and support the people around you.
You’re organised, attentive to detail, and interested in using simple data to improve your work.

Growing autonomy as you develop your skills and confidence.

As a Supply Chain Solutions Consultant, you will partner with Account Executives to shape the vision of prospects and existing clients, and present Pigment's thought leadership around Supply Chain Planning. You act as a trusted advisor who bridges operational supply chain expertise with the power of a modern planning platform.

Discovery: Deeply understand supply chain planning challenges - demand forecasting, S&OP/IBP, inventory planning, capacity planning - and help prospects articulate their goals and future vision. Build strong relationships with operations, supply chain, and finance stakeholders.

Advanced problem-solving and troubleshooting skills

About the Growth Team at Pigment
GTM Engineering builds AI-first products and systems that help Pigment's GTM organization - Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and RevOps - operate with greater speed, focus, and leverage.
Our mandate is twofold: 
enable GTM teams with automations and AI-powered applications that drive real efficiency gains
directly generate pipeline through AI-powered, automated outbound motions across our North America market.
We build the internal tools and agents behind high-impact GTM workflows, including prospecting intelligence, expansion insights, outbound automation... Our work combines product craft, applied AI, hands-on GTM operating experience, and a tight feedback loop with the field.
 

 
The Role
Based in New-York, US
We’re hiring a GTM Engineer to design, build and scale AI-first GTM systems, and to directly contribute to pipeline generation across our US market.
This is a hybrid role by design:
70% applied AI (internal GTM products, workflows)
30% pipeline ownership & outbound experimentation
You’ll operate at the intersection of builder, operator, and PM - turning manual GTM best practices into scalable, repeatable systems, and owning pipeline generation through those systems.
 

 
Your Missions
#1 - Build & Scale AI-First GTM Automation (70%)
Design & ship AI-powered GTM systems: Turn proven GTM workflows into scalable automation building internal tools and AI agents (e.g. expansion insights, deal intelligence, AE > CS handoffs, and GTM copilots).

Own GTM automation as a product, from discovery to adoption, while continuously measuring, optimizing, and scaling its impact on GTM efficiency, automation ROI, and pipeline influence to unlock step-change productivity.

Lead and empower the Tech TA team
Manage, coach, and develop a team of three Tech Talent Acquisition Managers
Create a healthy and collaborative environment built on trust, transparency, and shared accountability
Leverage the team’s expertise and give each member the autonomy to own their roles, stakeholders, and projects
Set clear priorities and allocate resources based on the hiring plan, business needs, and team capacity

Adjust priorities and approaches based on business changes, market insights, and recruitment data

Align stakeholders on hiring priorities, target profiles, assessment criteria, and timelines
Provide clear visibility into pipeline health, progress, risks, and team capacity
Use data and market insights to guide decisions, challenge assumptions, and recommend actions
Coach Hiring Managers and interviewers to improve assessment quality and decision-making
Help unblock complex situations and maintain efficient hiring processes

Own selected strategic, senior, or complex searches end-to-end
Proactively identify and engage high-quality candidates
Build effective sourcing, assessment, and closing strategies
Support offer negotiations and closing when needed
Ensure a consistent and high-quality candidate experience

Track key metrics, including pipeline health, conversion rates, time-to-hire, offer acceptance, and source effectiveness
Assess progress against the hiring plan and identify areas for improvement
Improve recruitment processes, workflows, and tools
Maintain consistent and scalable hiring practices across R&D
Lead initiatives such as interviewer training, talent mapping, candidate experience, and Tech employer branding
Who you are
You have strong experience in Tech Talent Acquisition, ideally in a fast-growing and international environment
You have experience managing/mentoring and developing a Talent Acquisition team
You know how to create a collaborative environment while giving people autonomy and holding them accountable
You can translate a hiring plan into a clear recruitment strategy and priorities

You bring clarity and structure to complex, fast-changing environments
You care deeply about hiring quality and candidate experience

Our Engineering team
Our Engineering team is responsible for developing our SaaS platform and building a comprehensive and user-friendly product. Pigment engineers participate in the entire application development lifecycle, focusing on design, coding, and keeping the production platform up and running. They can be specialized, but there is no strict separation between the infrastructure, backend, and the frontend.
We value user-centricity and pragmatism: we choose the most relevant tools for the problem we have to solve, understanding the strengths and constraints of each technology. Our engineering culture also values curiosity, humility, trust, ownership and team spirit.
👉 Curious to see what we’re building? Check out our Tech Blog!

As a Software Engineer Intern, you will work on meaningful projects that directly impact our product, collaborating with experienced engineers and contributing to challenges at scale. During your internship, you will have the opportunity to work on one of the following projects:
Project overview in the Data Ingestion team:
The Data Ingestion team is in charge of how customer data gets into Pigment, notably through our library of connectors to external systems.
Upgrade, migrate and improve our connector library
Upgrade and migrate existing connectors to newer versions and approaches.
Improve the reliability, performance, and consistency of the connector library.
Contribute to shared tooling and documentation to make new connectors faster to build.

Project overview in the Modeler team:
The Modeler team builds the AI-powered tools that help customers create and evolve planning models in Pigment.
Importing a model from another planning tool with the Modeler Agent 
Explore whether recent progress in LLMs and the Modeler Agent makes it possible to recreate a model from another planning tool in Pigment.
Design an automated approach to translate its structure, dimensions, and formulas into Pigment blocks and valid formulas.
Define tests to validate that the imported model behaves as expected.

Technical Stack
Our stack includes:
Languages & Frameworks: C# (.NET Core Linux), React, TypeScript
Databases: PostgreSQL
Infrastructure: Google Cloud Platform, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, RabbitMQ
CI/CD: CircleCI
We don’t expect you to know them all. What matters most is strong software engineering skills: the ability to translate requirements into simple and elegant designs and deliver robust code.

Work Environment
Hybrid: possibility to work partially remotely
Office in the heart of Paris
Choose your working environment (hardware / OS)
A competitive remuneration package
Opportunity to continue your journey with us after your internship

The opportunity
 
We are looking for an Engineering Program Manager (EPM) to help us scale our engineering team. Because we have EPMs almost since the beginning of Pigment, the role is already well-known. Our team is central to the engineering organization, perceived as a force multiplier by all the other engineers. We are constantly on the lookout to improve how we work. We like to try new ideas, whether it is to accelerate delivery, structure the organization or develop a unique culture. By joining our passionate, close-knitted team, you can have an impact in many different ways and learn in a team that is both young and fast-growing! 
Here is what the day-to-day of an EPM looks like at Pigment:
 
Deliver: You make a difference every day in the engineering team(s) you are working with, as you enhance clarity, direction, scope, and keep all the parts together with other roles (such as Product Managers). Typically an EPM accompanies 1 to 3 teams in their delivery, ranging from technical projects (e.g. scalability and performance, SRE) to more functional ones (e.g. bringing automations to our product).
 
Scale: You contribute to the engineering instances wherever you can bring added value. For instance, you can contribute to maintaining a healthy release pipeline, participate to incident response, oversee improvements to our monitoring and alerting practices…You also lead initiatives of various sizes to tackle the needs and issues that arise when growing as an organization. For instance, suggest evolutions to roles and responsibilities, better organize knowledge management, or work on large-scale projects related to quality management and production stability.
 
Federate: You contribute to the general well-being of the team, upon opportunity and based on affinity, for example as an organizer of regular instances (all-hands meetings, newsletters…), hackathons, team building activities, and any other idea related to the promotion of Pigment culture internally and externally. You also contribute to Pigment hiring and branding initiatives.
 
The team
As a team, we have a mission statement and a roadmap that we maintain over time. We are open to different styles and we rotate responsibilities and projects on a regular basis between us. We regularly exchange on our challenges in “co-development” sessions and sound new ideas to one another. You will also grow as an individual thanks to a career ladder and a culture of on-going feedback.
 
Explore Our Tech Blog:
If you're curious about the kind of challenges our engineering team tackles, our culture, and our organization, we invite you to explore our Tech Blog!
 
Who you are
 
We expect demonstrated experience in helping technical teams build and run in a fast-paced environment, with the right touch of processes and empowerment of individuals. 
 
Technical project/product management, engineering management, quality engineering, and production-related roles are typically the kind of roles where such an experience is demonstrated, but we are open to a diversity of backgrounds.
 
Experience as a software engineer is a plus but not required. The position does not involve coding. You should be able to read and understand code and read / comment / challenge a technical design.
 
To help you better understand the role, here are the qualities we are looking for in an EPM:
Resourcefulness: you like to be dropped in a new context and come up with your own solutions 
Change management: you are a people person and you convey change smartly and courageously
Diligence: you are curious and connect the dots in ways no one else can, you strive to reach alignment through shared understanding, clarity, and direction
Integrity: you lead by example, inspire others, and always play “first team”
 
The position doesn’t involve people management.
Fluency in English (French not required)
 
Folks from underrepresented minorities: science shows that you are less likely to apply if you feel that you don’t have all the necessary prerequisites. If this description matches where you are now or what you'd like to grow into in your next position, we encourage you to apply.

Join Pigment: The AI Platform Redefining Business Planning
 
Pigment is the AI-powered business planning and performance management platform built for agility and scale. We connect people, data, and processes in one intuitive platform, with AI agents that work alongside every team, from Finance to HR, to build, adapt, and align strategic plans in real time.

Founded in 2019, Pigment is one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies globally, passing $100M in ARR in 2026 and doubling revenue for the second year in a row. Industry leaders like Unilever, Uber, Anthropic, Snowflake, and Siemens use Pigment every day to make better-informed decisions and navigate any scenario with confidence.

In October 2026, we raised a $250M Series E at a $2.3B valuation, bringing our total funding to $650M+. Today we’re a growing team of 700+ across Paris, London, New York, Toronto, San Francisco, and Austin, and we’ve been named a Visionary in the Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Financial Planning Software two years running.

At Pigment, we take smart risks, celebrate bold ideas, and challenge the status quo - all while working as one team. If you’re driven by innovation and ready to make an impact at scale, we’d love to hear from you.


The opportunity
 
We are looking for a Senior SRE profile who will design and implement the Pigment infrastructure for tomorrow. Pigment is a technically challenging platform. It calculates and synchronizes large datasets that must be updated in real-time. Data comes from client models that can be up to billions of rows. This data can be pivoted, transformed, and aggregated on-demand through our formula engine while rendering live on our front end.
Here are the challenges to be tackled as an SRE :
Define and build the infrastructure needed to answer our performance challenges, automate it, and make it scalable. In particular, ensure that the infrastructure scales in and out according to the platform usage.
Secure high availability and redundancy of the Pigment platform.
Ensure that the platform’s performance and correctness are monitored accordingly, spread observability best practices across the engineering team.
Participate in incident response.
Accompany Pigment geographical expansion as the company grows and we sign clients overseas.
Work with our security team on the implementation of their roadmap when related to infrastructure and development pipelines (code repository, credentials management, ...)
Continuously chase inefficiencies within our development practices and pipelines. Seek improvement and automation wherever possible. Drive change across the software engineering team.
In addition to SRE responsibilities, we expect you to contribute to software development activities. We believe SRE engineers should collaborate closely with software engineers, fostering a shared understanding of day-to-day challenges, rather than operating in separate teams. Last but not least, you will not be alone! You will be part of an SRE team.
 
Our Engineering team
Our Engineering team is responsible for developing our SaaS platform and building a comprehensive and user-friendly product.
Pigment engineers participate in the entire application development lifecycle, focusing on design, coding, and keeping the production platform up and running. They can be specialized, but there is no strict separation between the infrastructure, backend, and the frontend.
 
We value user-centricity and pragmatism: we choose the most relevant tools for the problem we have to solve, understanding the strengths and constraints of each technology.
Our engineering culture also values curiosity, humility, trust, ownership and team spirit.
 
Technical stack:
Kubernetes (GKE, hosted on Google Cloud Platform): hosting all our infrastructure components except some PostgreSQL hosts, hosted on Google Cloud SQL
Terraform: all our infrastructure is managed via this infrastructure as code (creation of GKE clusters, Google Cloud SQL databases, GCS buckets, IAM permissions...)
Databases: PostgreSQL (CloudSQL and CloudNativePG), SingleStore, ElasticSearch
RabbitMQ: queuing system
Temporal.io: workflow automation platform
Others: ArgoCD, Istio, Vault, Github, Docker (for local development)
Backend: Microservices written in C# ASP.NET Core 8 (running exclusively on Linux) & Golang
Frontend: React + Typescript, Jest, Cypress, Vite...
 
Who you are
 
More than knowledge of a specific cloud provider, language, or automation framework, we are looking for great engineering skills: the ability to translate product requirements into an elegant and simple architecture, and then make sure our product runs well on it.
We are also looking for engineers who understand the product and the customer's needs in detail and can suggest innovative ideas: in the end, it's all about delivering value to end-users.
 
In any case, you have:
Experience as a software engineer & DevOps / SRE
Experience with a container orchestration platform (Kubernetes is a plus)
Experience with a public cloud provider, GCP is a plus
Proven experience in software developments with languages such as C#, Java, C++, Golang, Rust, JavaScript, Python, or Ruby (this list is not exhaustive).
Experience with observability tools (e.g. Datadog, Prometheus, ELK, Jaeger...)
Great team spirit with a problem-solving attitude.
A good dose of humility and the willingness to grow (no matter your seniority!).
Fluency in English
